rows.src: The rest of the ANNO queue — thirteen issues, read from Volltext
rows.what: Every issue this archive had queued for a human to open, read in one sitting instead
rows.got:
**A street, a court officer, a schoolmaster on the other side of the argument, and a date this archive may have wrong.**

· **«Via Carlo Defranceschi», Pola** — in the classified columns of *Il Giornaletto di Pola* in **110 issues between 3 January 1914 and 20 May 1919**. Rooms to let, a beer depot at number 3. **Pola named a street after him and by 1914 it was just an address.** The landmarks page had been asking «any others?» since it was written.

· **Johann Defranceski of Šturje** — seventeen issues of the *Laibacher Zeitung*, 1865–1875, always as ***Curator ad actum*** for defendants of unknown whereabouts. This archive had inferred from the three-issues-in-nine-days rhythm that somebody of the name was under repeated legal process. **The rhythm was right and the reading was backwards**: that is how an edict is published, and he is the court's officer inside it. Šturje is in the Vipava valley — **a region this archive had never placed the name in**.

· ***Naša Sloga*, 28 May 1914** — at two Croatian electoral meetings in Istria, one of them in the yard by the Croatian school with over five hundred people present, the speakers include *«domaći učitelj Defranceski»*, **the local schoolmaster**. Naša Sloga is the paper that existed to oppose Carlo De Franceschi. **Sixty-six years after Carlo was denounced in the Lloyd as an Italian irredentist, a man of his name is speaking for the Croatian side in the Croatian paper.** Like the Eduard-and-Valente pair of 1859, they did not need to be related for that to be true about the name.

· ***L'Istria*, 28 January 1882** — a journalist visits Carlo, finds him ill (*«il male che lo tormenta»*), and records that he went to school at **Gorizia and Graz and finished his studies in 1832**.

· ***L'Eco di Pola*, 3 September 1887** — a **de Franceschi «integerrimo deputato al Parlamento»** stands godfather to a workers' society banner at Umago, beside the wife of the Podestà.

· ***La Fiamma*, 1912** — a scholarly bibliography citing **Camillo De Franceschi's «Dante a Pola»** (Giornale dantesco, Florence 1906) and his work on pilgrims to the Holy Sepulchre who stopped at Pola.

· And **two contemporary sources giving Carlo's birth year as 1810**, against the register's 1809 — filed as an open question.

**The queue is cleared.** What had been written up as an errand for a human with a browser took one sitting, because every ANNO issue carries its own full text.

rows.src: Austro-Hungarian casualty lists — «Verlustliste» and «Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte»
rows.what: The first First World War records this archive has ever read
rows.got:
**This archive has covered the Second World War in detail and had never once opened a First World War casualty list.** Two surnames were sitting in them.

The lists are a genealogist's document by accident: to tell families apart they print **rank, regiment, company, province, district, commune and year of birth**, and then what happened to the man.

**«Verlustliste», 6 May 1916** — *Fernasar Josef, Inft., k. k. LIR. Nr. 5, 10. Komp., **Istrien, Pisino, Gračišće**, 1884; kriegsgef., Merw, Gebiet Transkaspien, Rußland.* A man of **Maria née Fernasar's own village**, born 1884, a prisoner of war at **Merv in Transcaspia** — now Mary, in Turkmenistan. The surname of our fourth generation's mother, placed at last, in a printed record.

**«Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte», 14 December 1914** — *Fernasar Josef, Jäg., FJB. Nr. 20, Pisino [I]strien, 1883, Hufschlag a. d. r. Ferse, Vereinshilfsspital Nr. 2 in Kassa.* Same name, same district, a year out and a different unit. Same man or a cousin; not settled.

**«Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte», 21 December 1914** — *Defranceski Josef, Jäg., TJR. Nr. 1, 2. Komp., **Branzoll**, 1885, Schuß i. d. r. Hand, Festungsspital Nr. 8 in Krakau.* A Tyrolean rifleman shot through the right hand, in the fortress hospital at Kraków. **And Branzoll is Bronzolo, in South Tyrol** — so the family's own -ski spelling, in the Austrian press, is at least partly **Tyrolean and not Istrian**, which corrects an assumption made here yesterday. It also joins up with the *Defranzeschi* cluster in *Der Tiroler* and the Innsbruck papers, and gives the Trentino blind spot its first named person.

**The method note that matters more than any of it**: these were read from ANNO's own **Volltext** view — `annoshow?text=<paper>|<date>|x` — which returns the whole issue's OCR as plain text. Every ANNO issue has one. This project had spent a year treating the page images as the only way in.

rows.src: «Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd», Triest, 7 September 1848 — read in full
rows.what: The best unread document this archive had: nine occurrences of the surname in one four-page issue
rows.got:
**The prediction was wrong and the issue is better than the prediction.**

This archive expected shipping and quarantine notices: the Lloyd's journal carried them, and 1848 is the year **Ferencz Defranceschi** was running the quarantine station at Martinšćica. Nine mentions in four pages looked like a port list.

**Every one of the nine is Carlo.** The issue carries a long, furious, signed-off attack on *«dem Istrianer Deputirten Herrn Carl De Franceschi»* — announced in the contents page, running across pages three and four.

What it gives, beyond a great deal of 1848 invective:

· **A publication of Carlo's this archive did not know about** — a *Flugbogen*, a broadsheet, answering the Lloyd's Trieste correspondents on whether Istria was a land of Slavic character, *«in sehr vielen Exemplaren in Istrien verbreitet»*.
· **His post in 1848**: *Rathsprotokollist des Landrechts zu Rovigno* — council protocolist of the district court at Rovigno. This site had him as an *Auscultans* at Pazin in 1842 and expelled in 1854, and nothing between.
· **His own words in Italian**, quoted by an enemy: *«voi non Istriano, chi diede mandato d'immischiarvi [nelle] cose nostre…»*
· **The bootblack.** He called his opponent's *Stiefelputzer* as a witness against him, and the correspondent will not let it go.
· And the detail that he and Facchinetti and Madonizza, asked who had authorised their protest against joining the German Confederation, answered that they had protested **as private persons** and that the word *Deputati* had got into the title by oversight.

**And one conflict this archive cannot resolve.** The Lloyd says three times that he sat for **Rovigno**. This site says **Pisino**. A hostile paper is not a better source than a historian, but it is a contemporary one, printed while he was sitting. Both are now on his page and neither is preferred.

Read from the issue's own *Volltext* view at ANNO — which is the lesson worth keeping: **every ANNO issue has one, and this archive had been treating the page images as the only way in.**
rows.dest: ANNO — Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd, 7 Sept 1848

rows.src: ANNO — every spelling, including the family's own
rows.what: Seven variants of the surname against the whole Austrian press, and the one nobody had ever tried
rows.got:
**«Defranceski» — the spelling this family actually uses — had never been searched in the Austrian press. It returns 28 issues.** «De Franceski» gives 4 more, «Defranzeschi» 19, «Di Franceschi» 13, «Defrancheschi» 1. Sixty-five issues in variants, on top of the 950 and 722 for the two main forms.

**And the dates give the game away.** Look at when «Defranceski» appears in the official papers:

· *Wiener Zeitung* — **21, 24 and 29 December 1872**. Three issues in nine days.
· *Vereinigte Laibacher Zeitung* — **3, 6 and 11 March 1875**. Three issues in eight days. And again **15, 24 and 28 June 1869**. And again across June and July 1872.

**That is not news coverage. That is an edict.** Austrian official gazettes published legal notices — summonses, estates, bankruptcies, tenders — three times at set intervals, and the *Wiener Zeitung* and the *Laibacher Zeitung* were the gazettes of record for the empire and for Carniola. Seventeen issues of the Laibach paper between **1865 and 1875** carry the name, in exactly that rhythm.

So somewhere in Carniola in those ten years, a **Defranceski** was the subject of repeated official legal process. Whether that is one man or several, and whether a court, an estate or a business, the issues themselves would say in a line.

**Two more that open ground this archive has never been on:**

· ***Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte*, 21 and 30 December 1914** — the Austro-Hungarian **casualty lists**. A Defranceski, twice, in the war's first winter. This archive has covered the Second World War in detail and has **never once looked at a First World War casualty list**.

· ***Lagerzeitung für Wagna*, 4 February 1917** — the newspaper **of the Wagna camp itself**. The archive already holds the camp's intake lists from the Rovigno monograph, with two Defranceschi of Dignano in them; this is the camp's own paper, which is a different record, and it names a *Defranceski*.

**And the Tyrolean cluster sorts itself out.** «Defranzeschi» is almost entirely *Der Tiroler*, the *Innsbrucker Nachrichten* and the *Allgemeiner Tiroler Anzeiger*, 1899–1927, published at Bozen and Innsbruck — which is the Trentino group this site files as a blind spot. It now has a spelling and a set of dates.

None of it has been read: ANNO's page viewer is behind a Cloudflare check this archive does not answer.

rows.src: Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages — historical index
rows.what: Every spelling of the surname this archive carries — DEFRANCESKI, DEFRANCESCHI, DE FRANCESCHI, FRANCESCHI — across births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to 1996
rows.got:
**Nothing, under any spelling, in 167 years of the Queensland register.**

DEFRANCESKI returns zero. DEFRANCESCHI returns zero. FRANCESCHI returns two, and neither is ours — Joseph Franceschi, who married Menichina Amedei in 1877, and Jacques Ange Franceschi, a Corsican-French name, who died in 1989 to Albert Franceschi and Marcelle. (The two-word «DE FRANCESCHI» appears to return a hundred rows, but the space defeats the index's exact-match flag and it falls back to fuzzy matching — the results are «de Ruyter de Wildt» and «de Jong de Silva». It is not a holding.)

**And the null is the expected one, which is why it is worth writing down rather than worrying about.** This family's only two Queensland deaths are Mario De Franceschi in 2013 and Antony De Franceski in 1999. The index closes deaths at 1996. Both fall outside it by design, not by absence — so this search could not have found them, and finding nothing else means there was no earlier Queensland branch.

The arrival in Brisbane is as recent as this archive says. Nobody of this name registered a birth, a marriage or a death in Queensland before 1996.

rows.src: ANNO — Austrian Newspapers Online, searched properly for the first time
rows.what: The lesson from the Hungarian material applied to the Austrian press: the surname as two words, as one, and in the family's own spelling
rows.got:
**This archive has been searching ANNO with one hand.**

ANNO has a clean JSON endpoint behind its search page — `/anno-suche/rest/search/simple?query=…&from=N` — which returns, per issue, the paper, the date, the place of publication, the language and **the number of hits inside that issue**. Run three ways, the surname gives:

· **«De Franceschi», two words — 950 issues.**
· **«Defranceschi», one word — 722 issues.** This is the only form this archive had ever used.
· **«Defranceski», the family's own spelling — 28 issues, never searched here at all.** «De Franceski» gives 4 more.

The forms overlap but do not contain one another. **Roughly a quarter of the Austrian press coverage of this surname was invisible to every ANNO search this project has run.**

**Who is in it.** Proximity search — matching words standing within three of each other rather than anywhere in the same issue — sorts it out: **Carlo De Franceschi, 42 issues**; **Camillo, 5**; and **Enrico, 392** — an opera singer working in Vienna and Salzburg in 1930 and 1931, who is not ours, is now named on the namesakes page, and who accounts for two fifths of everything ANNO holds under this name. Anyone who searches it will hit him first.

**And a reading queue, which is the useful part.** Of the 950, **185 issues are Istrian or Adriatic** — *Il giovine Pensiero* of Pula, *L'Istria*, *Il Popolo Istriano*, *Il Giornaletto di Pola*, *L'Eco di Pola*, *La Fiamma*, *Naša Sloga*, the *Pester Lloyd*, and the **Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd**. Those are the papers that would print this family, and they are now listed by date and by how many times the name appears inside each issue.

**The single best of them is the oldest.** *Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd*, **7 September 1848 — nine occurrences in one four-page issue**, published at Trieste and Vienna. The Austrian Lloyd's journal carried shipping movements, quarantine and port notices; **1848 is the year Ferencz Defranceschi was running the quarantine station at Martinšćica.** That issue has not been read, because ANNO's page viewer at data.onb.ac.at sits behind a Cloudflare check **which this archive does not answer**.

rows.src: Hungaricana — the spelling «De Franceschi» with a space, and the Hungarian kingdom directories
rows.what: Working the same seam a second day: variant spellings, and the almanacs of the Hungarian crown
rows.got:
**Three offices, a successor state, and a correction to one of this archive's own authorities.**

The surname searched as one word gives 263 hits; **searched as two words it gives another 60**, and they are a different set. Most of those 60 are Hungarian scholarship citing Carlo De Franceschi's *L'Istria* as an authority — Fest Aladár's 1891 study of the Uskoks and the Venetians in the history of Fiume leans on him on page after page. That is worth knowing in itself: **Carlo was standard reading in Hungarian historical writing within a decade of his death.**

The Hungarian kingdom's own directories then gave three people:

· **Valentin Defranceschi, 1835 — *Passualist* in the Polizey-Behörde of Fiume.** The passport officer of a free port, listed among the city's patrician office-holders. The earliest office this archive can put the name in, and a civil one.

· **Ferencz Defranceschi, 1848 — *Főnök* of the St Francis quarantine institute at Martinšćica**, the lazaretto of the Kvarner, with a clerk, a surgeon-teacher, a chaplain and four guards under him. The same page records the harbour captaincy at **Buccari as vacant**.

· **«Dr Defranceschi», 21 December 1918 — South Slav representative**, addressed by the Austrian State Chancellor over the removal of the Austro-Hungarian archives to Yugoslavia. HHStA, Neues Politisches Archiv 397.

**And a correction to the shelf.** Vjesnik 18 (Zagreb, 1916) carries **Milko Kos**, publishing twenty unpublished Vienna parchments expressly to *«fill out and in many places correct Franceschi's conclusions on the genealogy of the lords of Pazin»*. Camillo De Franceschi's *Storia documentata* is cited across this site; on the medieval lords of Pazin it must now be read beside Kos. Kos also quotes Camillo admitting he was *«unfortunately not in a position to establish a complete and certain genealogy»* — which is the best sentence anyone in this family has written about this work.

rows.src: Hungaricana — the Hungarian Cultural Heritage Portal
rows.what: The surname against Hungarian state records, because Fiume and Bakar were Hungarian crown land
rows.got:
**The Kvarner name is a family of Habsburg maritime officials, and this morning's inference is now corroborated.**

Earlier today this archive read *«Francisci Defranceschi **Regii**»* on an 1849 Bakar baptism and inferred, from that one word, that the name held a royal office. It does. Hungaricana — free, unblocked, full-text — holds the Hungarian state's own paperwork for exactly these two towns, and nobody here had ever opened it.

· **Anton Defranceschi**, 1827, drew the *«Bauriss der zu Buccari befündlichen aerarial Salz-Einnehmer und Controlors Wohnung»* — the ground plan and section of the **imperial salt-receiver's and comptroller's residence at Buccari**, which is Bakar. Manuscript, 56 × 45 cm. National Archives of Hungary, **T 62 No 1642**, out of *E 96 Tricesimalia 1827*.

· **Ferencz Defranceschi**, **révkapitány — harbour master — of the Fiume Maritime Authority**. The parliamentary pension schedule of 1872 gives him **42 years, 10 months and 5 days** of public service and a pension of **1,050 forints from 1857**. Forty-three years back from 1857 puts him into state service about **1814**.

· **Francziska Defranceschi**, «*Defranceschi Ferencz révkapitány árva leánya*» — the harbour master's orphan daughter — drawing a **kegydíj** of 80 forints, renewed in three-year terms, in the state accounts of **1888, 1892, 1894, 1898 and 1900**. So her father was dead by 1888 and she was still unmarried and on the state's charity twelve years later.

· **Valentin Defranceschi**, K. K. Kriegs-Marine, **Marine-Direktion at Pola**, in the Militärschematismus of **1854, 1855 and 1856** — and *Valentin* is the one forename that recurs through the Rijeka households, fathering there in 1742–57 and again in 1794–1805.

· **Julius Defranceschi**, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine — **196 entries** across the rank and distribution lists from **1894 to 1909**, by then *Linienschiffsleutnant*. A whole naval career, free, page by page, not yet worked.

· **Theodor Defranceschi**, K. K. Landwehr, 1909.

**And it re-reads the saints.** This morning this archive noted that nine of twelve children born to Valentino and Ursula at Rijeka carried *Nepomucena* or *Nepomuc*, and read it as Habsburg dynastic piety. That is half of it. **John of Nepomuk is the saint invoked against drowning**, the patron of bridges and of men who work on water. In a harbour-master's town, in the Hungarian crown's free port, a family that names nine children for him is not only being loyal. It is being careful.

rows.src: The Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island Foundation, Arrival Records Collection
rows.what: The whole surname against American arrivals, 1820–1958 — the first time this portal has been used here
rows.got:
**A ship's name, and a large clean negative.**

Ellis Island manifests have been used by this archive for years — but through Findmypast, FamilySearch and an aggregator, never through the Foundation's own free database. It turns out to have a plain JSON endpoint, no account and no paywall, and to cover **seven** arrival collections rather than one, including *New York, Passenger Lists 1820–1920* — the Castle Garden decades that the *Ellis Island 1892–1925* set cannot reach.

**The ship.** The 1882 household that this archive already had from *Italians To America* — Giov b. 1846 with Angiola, Romeo, Marietta and Teresa — now has a vessel against it: all five records name the **St Germain**. Their ages at arrival are on the record too: **thirty-six, five, four, three and one**. The *St Germain* was a Compagnie Générale Transatlantique liner on the Le Havre run, which is worth knowing about a north-Italian family in 1882, although the departure port field on these particular records is blank and this archive is not asserting it from the ship alone.

**The negative, and it is the useful part.** One thousand four hundred arrivals of this surname were read, of which **429 record a last residence**. Exactly **two** of those 429 are Istrian — *G. Pedena* and *G. Gallignana*, which are Antonio and Albina on the Conte Rosso, 9 September 1922, already on this site. Everything else is Veneto and Friuli: Castelgomberto and Cornedo in Vicenza, Ponte nelle Alpi in Belluno, Pederobba in Treviso, and Sequals, Lestans and **Pinzano** in Pordenone, with Torrington in Connecticut as the American end of that chain.

**And the spelling that is not there at all.** *Defranceski*, *De Franceski*, *Defrančeski* and *Defranzeschi* each return **zero** records in the entire database. The -ski spelling — the family's own — never crossed to America under that form.
rows.dest: The Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island Foundation

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 172–174
rows.what: Testing Michiela De Franceschi fu Giuseppe against the marriage register
rows.got:
**The test is not settled, and the reason is worth more than the answer would have been.**

The plan was to find the marriage of **Michiela De Franceschi × Domenico Giachin** — a marriage entry names *both* of the bride's parents, so if her mother is **Lucia Tromba** she is Giuseppe's daughter. Her first child is baptised in **1817**, so the marriage should fall about 1815–16.

**What was established.** The register opens **«LIBER COPULATORUM in Ecclesia Sancti Blasii Adignani, Annus 1815»**, first entry **12 October 1815**. The fourteen De Franceschi marriages this archive has already catalogued from it run **1817–1832**, and **none of them is this one**. So the marriage lies either in the register's first fifteen months or **before the book begins**. Images 172–174 were opened; the 1815–16 entries have **not** been scanned surname by surname, and that is a bounded job, not an open one.

**What was found instead, and it changes the reading.** There are **at least three different Michiela De Franceschis** at Vodnjan in this period:

**Michiela *fu Pietro*** — wife of Andrea Palin, house 24, dead before January 1831.
**Michiela *di Cristoforo* q.m Gio: Maria** — mother Maria Luigia Manzin, born about 1800, married in the register.
**Michiela *fu Giuseppe*** — wife of Domenico Giachin, house 532, alive in 1833.

**Michiela is not a rare name in this family; it is one of its commonest.** That is exactly why the inference has to rest on the patronymic and not on the name — and it is a good argument for *not* having claimed the Giuseppe link outright.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 572 (book pages 174–175)
rows.what: February – June 1833, entries 45–81
rows.got:
Thirty-seven entries, no De Franceschi. But this stretch is where the parish register stops being only about the parish.

**Entry 73, 24 April 1833, «Caserma Militare»** — not a house number but the **barracks**. *«Giorgio Carl… soldato della Compagnia XXI, Battaglione III, Reggimento XXII Principe Leopoldo, entrò nel 1808»* — dead of an inflammation of the bone *«in parte per caduta accidentale»*, in part from an accidental fall. Enlisted in 1808 and still serving in 1833: **twenty-five years a soldier**.

**That is the third appearance of the XXII Prince Leopold regiment** on this film — page 164 entry 11, page 172 entry 8, and now this. The regiment was quartered at Vodnjan, and the parish buried its men and its men's children.

**Entry 71, 22 April, house 280.** *«La Sig.ra Elisabetta nata Klettner fu Ignazio, Vedova del Sig.r Francesco Kneipf, nata … in Moravia»* — a Moravian gentlewoman, dead of apoplexy and buried on the 24th.

Taken with the gunner *Giorgio Sabotz* and the man from a district in the Friulian provinces, that is **four outsiders in about a year**, each given more biography by this register than most of the town's own children get.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 571 (book pages 172–173)
rows.what: January – February 1833, entries 4–44
rows.got:
Forty-one entries. **One De Franceschi** — Michiela *fu Giuseppe*, at entry 41, written up separately — and two things that only appear if you read the book in order.

**House 109, in seven months.** On **24 July 1832** a child of *Marchio* and *Eufemia Bergamasco* is entered as *«N. nato morto»* — born dead, unnamed. On **28 July** his twin, *Giacomo*, follows him. On **10 February 1833**, entry 37, the father goes: *«Marchio figlio delli furono giugali Marco Benaco fu Giacomo e Giustina Cosseani fu Pietro, era ammogliato con Eufemia Bergamasco d'Antonio»*, dead of *malattia acuta di petto*, house **109** — the same house. **Eufemia buries two sons and her husband inside seven months.** No index would ever have put those three entries together; they share no name and no date. Only the house number and the order of the book connect them.

**The regiment again.** Entry 8, 10 January 1833, is a child of the **«Battaglione 3.o Reggimento XXII Principe Leopoldo»** — the same regiment named at entry 11 on page 164. The Prince Leopold regiment was quartered here, and its soldiers' children are buried in this parish under their fathers' units rather than a house number.

Also on these pages: **«vajuolo naturale»** — natural smallpox — entered as a cause for the first time in this stretch.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 571
rows.what: February 1833
rows.got:
**Entry 41, 20 February 1833, house 532.** «*Giacomo figlio del fu Dom.co Giachin q.m Giacomo e di **Michiela De Franceschi fu Giusep.** giugali*» — dead of **idrotorace**, with confession, communion, extreme unction and the indulgence.

**A seventh woman of the name, and she is not the Michiela already known.** The one this archive holds is *Michiela De Franceschi **fu Pietro***, wife of Andrea Palin at house 24, dead before January 1831. This is *Michiela De Franceschi **fu Giuseppe***, wife of Domenico Giachin at house 532, **and still alive in 1833** — it is her son who dies, and her husband who is already *«del fu»*.

**The father's name is the interesting part.** This archive holds exactly one Giuseppe De Franceschi: **1758 – 14 February 1830, house 324, × Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo**, dead suddenly and without a priest. He was in his grave three years when this entry was written, which is what *«fu»* requires. If this Michiela is his daughter, she stands beside **Don Stefano the priest, Pietro the ploughman, Cristoforo the weaver and Maria Francesca** as a **fifth child** of that household.

**That is an inference and is marked as one.** What the register says is that her father was called Giuseppe and was dead. It does not say which Giuseppe, and the name is not rare. The baptism register would settle it.

Her son's age is written in a column this viewer will not render legibly and is **left unread rather than guessed**.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 569–570 (book pages 168–171)
rows.what: August 1832 – January 1833, entries 84–157 and 1833/1–3
rows.got:
**Seventy-seven entries, no De Franceschi.** **The year 1832 is now closed** — entries 1 to 157, read end to end — and 1833 has opened.

**A fifth pair of twins.** Entries 124 and 125, both **18 October 1832**, both house **149**: *«Dom.co figlio gemello»* and *«Antonio figlio gemello»*, dead the same day. That is five sets of twins buried together in about eighteen months of one parish's register.

**Two outsiders who died here and are not of the town.** Entry 98, 5 September, has **no house number at all** — a man of a commune in another province, dead of *febbre perniciosa* with no priest. Entry 121, 15 October, is **«Giorgio Sabotz, canoniere»** — a gunner of a foreign regiment, also without the sacraments. The register takes them in and says where they came from, which is more than it does for most of the town's own children.

**One entry still unseen: number 83**, which sits at the foot of page 167 below the rows already read. Written down here rather than glossed over, because the entry numbers are the only checksum this reading has.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 566–568 (book pages 164–167)
rows.what: January – July 1832, entries 7–82
rows.got:
**Seventy-six entries, no De Franceschi.** The 1832 sequence now runs unbroken from entry 1 to 82.

**One candidate, examined and given up.** Entry 21, 14 January 1832, house 238: *«Domenico figlio del fu Ant.o De Ribecchi fu Dom.co e della fu Bonetta **da Francesche** giugali»*. At scanning zoom that last phrase is indistinguishable from *De Franceschi*. At full magnification it is not: the preposition is **da**, not *de*, and the ending is **-esche**, not *-eschi*. That makes **three** such candidates given up on this film — the other two were *«q.m Francesco»* and *«di Francesco»* on image 560.

**A fourth pair of twins**, and the hardest entry of the stretch: **24 July 1832, house 109, «N. nato morto»** — a child born dead and not named — and four days later, same house, same parents, **«Giacomo figlio gemello»**. One twin stillborn, the other dead within the week.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 567
rows.what: Two cut strips laid on a blank leaf
rows.got:
Frame 567 is **the same opening as 566, photographed a second time** with **two cut strips of a register page** laid on the facing leaf. The strips are not new material: their house numbers — **592, 600, 159, 75, 78, 102** — are page 164's entries 11 to 17, which frame 566 already shows in place.

**This changes how the film has to be counted.** Consecutive frames share a page, and some frames are re-shoots of a page already filmed. **581 frames is not 581 pages**, and any estimate of how long this book takes to read that is built on the frame count is wrong. The reliable unit is the **book's own page number**, written at the top outer corner, with the **entry numbers** as the check that nothing has been skipped between them.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 561–564, left-hand pages (book pages 156, 158, 160)
rows.got:
**The hole closed.** The left-hand page of every frame had been going unread; three of them are now read, and the 1831 sequence runs **continuously from entry 20 to entry 167** with no frame unaccounted for.

Sixty-five further entries, **no De Franceschi** beyond the two already published. Two more pairs of twins dead together — **Giovanni and Giovanna Baratich**, both 20 August 1831, house 471; **Domenica and Maria Manzin**, both 1 January 1832, house 422.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 561
rows.what: January 1831, re-read
rows.got:
Re-read in full because the frame had been half-read. **It confirms, independently, what this archive already published** from it — *«Domenica figlia di Andrea Palin q.m Pio. e della fu Michiela De Franceschi fu Pietro giugali»*, the sixth Vodnjan woman recovered through a child's death entry.

**Two details the page did not carry:** Domenica was **22**, and she died of **tisi polmonare** — the same pulmonary consumption that took Maddalena Francin at house 456 ten weeks later.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 564–565 (book pages 161, 162, 163)
rows.what: August 1831 – January 1832, entries 120–167 and 1832/1–6
rows.got:
**Forty-eight consecutive entries, no De Franceschi.** Recorded because a family archive that only writes down its hits cannot tell you how thoroughly it has looked.

Two things on these pages are worth keeping anyway. **Page 161 carries a bishop's visitation note** in a different hand: *«Vidi die 5.ta 9mbris 1832 — Antonius, Ep.us Parent.»* — *I saw this on 5 November 1832, Antonio, Bishop of Parenzo.* The diocesan inspection, signed in the book itself. And every page closes with the parroco's own signature, *«Joannes Tromba Sac. Th. D.r Parochus»* — the priest this archive already knows from the marriage register.

**1832 opens with twin girls.** Entries 2 and 3, both 1 January 1832, both house 422: *Domenica* and *Maria*, *«figlia gemella di Gio. Batta Manzin q.m Lorenzo e di Bonetta Manzin di Venier giugali»* — twin sisters, dead the same day.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 563
rows.what: May – June 1831
rows.got:
**Entry 84, 19 May 1831, house 456.** «**Pasqua figlia di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro, e della fu Maddalena Francin di Gio. giugali**», dead of **tosse convulsiva** — whooping cough.

**«della fu Maddalena»** — *of the late Maddalena*. The register itself confirms the March death nine weeks later, in the ordinary course of writing down her daughter. That is the check this archive wants and rarely gets: **the same book, corroborating its own entry, without being asked.**

**Three deaths in that house in five months.** Pietro, eleven, of scarlatina on 15 December 1830. Maddalena, thirty-nine, of consumption on 14 March 1831. Pasqua, of whooping cough, on 19 May 1831. **Her age is not recorded here** — the column is written small and sideways and could not be read with confidence at the resolution the viewer allows, so it is left unread rather than guessed.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 562
rows.what: March 1831
rows.got:
**Entry 48, 14 March 1831, house 456.** «**Maddalena Francin di Giovanni, Moglie di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro**», *cattolica*, *femmina*, **aged 39**, dead of **tisi polmonare**. The sacraments column is full: *Conf.e, Com.e, Extr. Unz.e, Ind. in art. mortis.*

**She is the mother of the eleven-year-old.** House 456 is where, on **15 December 1830**, «Pietro figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro e di **Maddalena Francin di Giovanni** giugali» died of scarlatina — and the two entries name the same couple in the same words. **The boy dies in December; his mother dies ninety days later**, in the same house, of consumption.

The sacraments columns set side by side are the whole of it. For the boy: «*senza assistenza spirituale per la malattia repentina*» — no priest, the illness was too sudden. For his mother, dying slowly of tuberculosis: **every rite there is**.

Aged 39 in March 1831 puts her birth about **1791–92**, and about **27** at the boy's birth in 1819.

rows.what: Eight scenes the archive can defend from documents, each written as a prompt with negative constraints and a list of details that must be right; the first — Imotski 1717 — generated and installed
rows.got: Standing rules, so nothing here can ever be mistaken for a source: no invented face is ever captioned with a real person's name; no invented lettering on a real inscribed stone and no invented heraldry for a family whose arms are documented; every image captioned as a constructed illustration with its departures from the record named; no fabricated documentary apparatus — no title block, scale bar, dimension, survey date; the unaltered original archived in the source library beside its brief, marked with whatever was removed. Briefs at notes/image-prompts.md. ALL EIGHT NOW DONE, seven published: the house at Gologorica, with the 1711 tablet deliberately blank; Imotski 1717; the road of the Furlans 1679; the Salamon palace; the mills at Perinuša; Crikvenica in the winter of 1943; Pfullingen 1944. Plus a lapidarius of Gračišće, published as the trade and explicitly NOT as a portrait of Antonio, because the model gave it a detailed invented face. TWO WITHHELD: the first Gologorica house, which carried a fabricated pseudo-Latin inscription across the 1711 tablet; and a close detail of the arms and the Madonna relief, because the coat of arms in it does not match the blazon Carlo gave Kobler and the carving the family photographed — a cross crossed by two arrows over a pomegranate. Both kept in the library marked WITHHELD. Four failure modes, each seen more than once: a caption burned into the picture; a watermark; an invented inscription or coat of arms on a real carved stone; and an image returned dressed as a measured conservation survey of a real protected building, with title block, scale bar, dimensions and date. Every one of them was caught before publication.

rows.src: defranceski.com — the family's own Google Site
rows.what: All eleven pages captured as HTML; both Google MyMaps exported as KML; every external link on the site diffed against this archive's own; the linear family chart checked date by date against the Direct Line

rows.src: Ližnjan — the parish record indexes, targeted
rows.what: Four spellings across three country filters, every record matched whole for Ližnjan; then every entry naming a Gregorius, Gregorio, Gregorii or Grga pulled out in full
rows.got: 127 entries of the surname at Ližnjan, 1788 onward. Grga is real: Gregorius Defranceski, aged 22 at his marriage on 10 June 1874, so born 1851, son of Gregorio Defranceschi and Agata Skifić, husband of Maria Vojnić, father of Anastasia (1875 and 1876), Maria (1878), Justina (1879), Maria (1882) and Josephus (1887). His daughter Justina married Josephus Fedel on 22 Nov 1898 and a Stana married Jacobus Vojnić on 7 Aug 1899 — Fedel and Vojnić being two of the surnames standing beside «Defrančeski Ante» in the Ližnjan subscription list of 1920. Behind Gregorio stands a Mattio De Franceschi and a Madalena Peucovich. Index entries only; the books are at Pazin and unread.

rows.src: Monheim (Bavaria) and Zagreb — the rest of the map pin
rows.what: German record indexes, Croatian digitised newspapers, and burial indexes searched for a Defranceschi at Monheim and for a death of Grga at Zagreb
rows.got: Nothing for either. The Monheim pin is Monheim in the Donau-Ries, not Monheim am Rhein — about a hundred kilometres from Metzingen, and Metzingen is four from Pfullingen. Both the Monheim line and «Grga dies in Zagreb» carry no note, no date and no document on the map they came from, and neither could be confirmed here. The nearest thing is a Zagreb grave for Marija Defrančeski, 1884–1971, two years off Grga's daughter Maria of 1882 — suggestive, not proof, and left as such.

rows.src: MyHeritage — David's live family tree
rows.what: Read directly from his logged-in session: 459 individuals carrying the surname, harvested through the site's own lookup and person-panel endpoints, with their dates, places, relationships and source citations
rows.got: The 2018 GEDCOM this project had been using holds 8,286 people; the live tree holds 15,643, and David's own verdict on the old file is «really old and really wrong». The direct line agrees wherever both hold a fact, and the tree supplies what this archive lacked: exact death dates for Antonius (4 Aug 1894) and for Giovanni Battista (14 Sep 1846), Gologorica rather than Gračišće as the 1787 birthplace, and an ark for the 1750 Giovanni that no page had ever been put in front of. The working notes behind it are not published: they quote the export row by row, and the export carries living people in full. What the reconciliation actually settled is on this page and in the corrections it produced.

rows.src: David's Google MyMaps — the emigration layers
rows.what: «High Level of Emigration from Here» (44 pins) and «Italian Lines» (90 pins), read from the archived KML
rows.got: A departure region for the Brazilian cluster, which this archive has never had. Scorzè, Moniego (Noale), Cornedo Vicentino, Castelgomberto and Pederobba in the Veneto — with «DE FRANCESCHI Luigi, spouse BAROLO Caterina Luigia, from Moniego, Noale, Venezia to São Paulo» and «Giuseppe Romano De Franceschi, born Scorzè 22 May 1835, died Moniego». And a second region entirely: the Castelnuovo pin is Castelnuovo in the Valsugana, Trentino — four kilometres from Telve, where David's tree holds eighteen people of this surname. Also on those layers: Castelnovo del Friuli to Trostberg in Bavaria (Peter DeFranceschi b. 19 Feb 1841); Mione to Biella; Bishop Lucio Soravito de Franceschi of Adria-Rovigo; and a France cluster around Metz, Nancy, Fréjus and Propriano.

rows.src: Andrea de' Franceschi and Titian
rows.what: The Grand Chancellor's portraits — Detroit, Hampton Court, Washington — and the 2016 Artibus et Historiae paper
rows.got: Closed as far as it can be from here, after a year on the roadmap. Grand Chancellor of Venice 1529 to his death in 1551; Titian's friend; painted into the «Presentation of the Virgin» in the Accademia; owned two portraits of himself by Titian, the head in both taken from Titian's own picture now in Detroit. The Hampton Court double portrait was cleaned in 1958 and gave up a third figure painted out earlier. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds a further portrait it declines to call Titian. Not kin, and never claimed as such. Still unread: Charles Hope's «Titian's portraits of Grand Chancellor Andrea de' Franceschi», Artibus et Historiae 74 (2016), 139–151 — the academia.edu copy sits behind Cloudflare. The National Gallery of Art site requires JavaScript and the National Trust site served a CAPTCHA; neither was circumvented, and the facts above come from those institutions' own catalogue text as quoted elsewhere.

rows.src: Francesco de' Franceschi, the painter
rows.what: The fifteenth-century Venetian painter carried on the roadmap as unfinished
rows.got: Active 1443–1468, birth and death unknown. Religious work on church commission; the style follows Michele Giambono and he may have worked with Antonio Vivarini. An altarpiece of 1447 in the Museo Civico at Padua; a St Mary Magdalen and a St Catherine of Alexandria in the Ashmolean at Oxford; a St Michael the Archangel and a St Mamas series. Not kin — two and a half centuries before this family reaches Istria. Roadmap item closed.

rows.src: «Franceschi dalle Rose»
rows.what: The byname on David's old map, pinned Ravenna → Venice 1040 → Giudecca
rows.got: No such family in the literature. The byname «dalle Rose» belongs to the Donà — the Donà dalle Rose, a Venetian noble house with origins in Romagna and Altinum, two Doges, and a surviving main branch whose archive is at the Museo Correr. The pin's Ravenna-to-Venice sequence is the Donà origin story. Recorded as a probable conflation so that it is not repeated.

rows.src: The family's own field photographs, 2026
rows.what: 491 images from six visits — Carnia (Ovaro, Mione, Muina, Agrons), Gologorica house and graves, Gračišće, Seget and Umag, Crikvenica–Klenovica–Novi–Senj, and the Pazin reading room — read as contact sheets so that the frames worth publishing can be chosen
rows.got: Read as contact sheets and plated. **31 published so far.** Gologorica (11): the builder's tablet, the memorial to Carlo, the arms cartouche with the Madonna aedicule beneath it, the blazon in the tomb pediment and the same arms weathered nearly smooth on an older stone, the tomb, the house from the lane, the arcaded end with the number 22, a wall niche, a carved ring, the chapel. Carnia (10): SORAVITO DE FRANCESCHI cut in stone at Ovaro with Anna Crosilla his widow; De Franceschi Ugo 1930–2020; Antonio 1877–1962 with Marta Anzola dead at twenty-five; Gio. Batta 1880–1963; Francesco 1887–1945; an 1850s stone; the war memorial carrying Vittorio and Isidoro De Franceschi; the campanile of Santa Maria di Gorto over the graves — the pieve whose parishes drew up the 1679 return. Gračišće (3): «F DE FRANCESCHI» with Marfan Virginija and Nazarijo; the Salamon grave, which turns Francisca Salamon from a surname into a family still in that ground; and a Marfan stone. Umag and Seget (7): the tomb's blue-and-gilt ironwork lunette with a lion rampant beneath a star under a coronet — the other family's arms, against Gologorica's cross, arrows and pomegranate; «FAMIGLIA DE FRANCESCHI — SEGHETTO»; «FAMIGLIA ETTORE DE FRANCESCHI»; a stone of 1848; the house at Seget; the tomb whole; the pine-cone finial. Living people appear in many frames and are excluded throughout. Klenovica and the coast (6): «OBITELJ DEFRANCESKI» with three portrait medallions — the household under the name it took on the coast — and then the Kalanj, who are everywhere in that ground: Marija 1889–1970, Josip, Franjo and Zora on one stone, Rozalija Anton Marija and Milan on another, Vinko and Paulina, Tomislav, Marijan, and the Kalanj-Perković. Anton Rudolf's mother was Ana Kalanj of Klenovica house 22, and it is her family and not his that stayed. Also a partisan star laid in white stone among the graves. **39 field plates published across six places.** The Pazin reading-room set of 117 is register images rather than ground; two of them are now published on The Eleven — the Gračišće Status Animarum for house 24, which carries the midwife Maria Fernazar's household, the eleven children in one column, and Daniel's household beneath. That page also settled Josip's birth at 22 March 1863 and joined Basilio of New York to this line.

rows.src: Documents and photographs supplied by the family, 8 September 2026
rows.what: Five items sent in one morning: the Zdravko plaque at Horsham, Ivan's grave at Senj, the whole opening of Anton Rudolf's 1890 baptism, a marriage register opening of 1772, and the 1951 Senj birth certificate — checked one by one against what this archive already held
rows.got: Three of the five were already here and all three were held in a worse copy. The Horsham plaque was a 1000-pixel thumbnail out of the family tree package and is now the 3648-pixel camera original, with the founder's mark legible. Ivan's grave was **400 pixels wide** and the dates could not be read at all; at 2368 they read **1925–1995**. Anton Rudolf's 1890 baptism was a cropped strip of entry 9, and the whole page adds three things the strip cut off — a pencil note «vjenčao se na Crikvenici», a remarks column explaining that the parents were staying with the wife's people at Klenovica, and the printer's line «Tisak H. Luster u Senju». The 1951 certificate was new, and carries the word STATELESS against the father in his own country. The 1772 marriage was new **as an image**: this archive had the FamilySearch index row for it and had written that an index is only an index. It is now the page.

rows.src: Crikvenica baptisms, 1901–1903
rows.what: The three names the Crikvenica monument adds — a ZO… born 1894, a POLD… born 1901 and RUŽA JARMACKI née DEFRANCESCHI 1903–1939, none of them on this archive's list of Josip and Ana's children. Searched signed in to FamilySearch across the indexed records, the catalogue film notes, the full-text corpus, and the Croatian State Archives portal
rows.got: **Settled, and the answer is that they are not online.** FamilySearch's Crikvenica holding, catalogue item 522842, gives its own coverage in the film notes: **Rođeni 1859–1896**, Vjenčani 1859–1908, Umrli 1859–1892 and 1893–1908. The births stop in 1896 and the other two series run twelve years further. The same cut is on every parish along that coast — Senj births end 1894 with marriages to 1920, Bribir births end 1886, Grižane 1886. It is the hundred-year rule as it stood when the films were made. The family's own photographs stop at 1896 because they were taken from the film. FamilySearch full-text search — which does read unindexed images — holds **no Croatian church-book collection**; its nearest are Italian civil registration and a Zadar-only Dalmatian births series. ARHiNET is gone: NAIS was retired in June 2020 for HAIS, and hais.arhiv.hr resolves but times out from here. **The next step is a letter to the Župni ured at Crikvenica or to the Rijeka archdiocese, not another search.**

rows.src: FamilySearch full-text search — the unindexed-image corpus
rows.what: Tested for the first time from a signed-in session: the full-text service reads handwriting off images that were never indexed, and reports its own coverage collection by collection
rows.got: **3,965 hits for «Defranceschi» across 172 collections, and not one of them is Croatian.** The corpus is Italian civil registration, the Americas, and a Dalmatian births series that turns out to be Zadar only. That is the negative this archive needed before writing letters. It is also a lead: **«Italy, Trieste, Trieste, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1924–1939» carries 53 Defranceschi**, with Padova 143, Bologna 501 and Treviso 7 beside it. Trieste 1924–1939 is the right city and the right years for the Istrians who left through it, and this archive has never read a line of it.

rows.src: HR-HDA-1448 — the Croatian State Archives' supplementary register microfilms
rows.what: The finding aid at arhiv.hr, searched for Crikvenica and Proložac across all seven kinds of register. This collection filmed the parish offices and the civil registry offices as well as the state archives, so it is not bound by the cut that ends FamilySearch's Croatian birth registers in the 1880s and 1890s
rows.got: **The single most useful thing found for this archive in weeks, and it is a catalogue rather than a record.** For Crikvenica it lists births to **1948**, marriages to **1947**, deaths to **1928**, and — this is the one — a **Status animarum of the twentieth century**, roll ZM-34J/251, mark M-5976, digitised, from the Župni ured Crikvenica. A Status animarum lists a house, its head, his wife and every child with a birth date; it is the form that gave this archive the whole of Gračišće house 24 in one opening. Crikvenica births 1897–1908 are absent here too and may not survive, but the household book and the marriage register of 1909–1947 between them should answer the three unaccounted names on the Crikvenica monument without the baptisms at all. Proložac, the Imotski family's own parish, runs unbroken 1853–1949 with everything from 1892 digitised. Ordered by e-mail to info@arhiv.hr quoting place, kind, period, roll signature and topographic mark; read in the HDA reading room, ten units a day. **Nothing has been read yet — this is the list of what exists and where.**

rows.src: Seget and Imotski, taken back to the sources
rows.what: The two non-Istrian houses of the surname, researched past the secondary accounts this site had been using: the 2016 conservation study of Stancija Seget, the Istrian encyclopaedia, and the Franciscan province of Split's own histories of its Omiš and Imotski convents
rows.got: **Seget:** the house carries its own dates — «1724» on the courtyard portal and «1732» with the initials «MA. F.» on the cistern, Marc'Antonio's monogram on his own well-head. A generation appears that this archive had never printed: **Giorgio de Franceschi, 1788–1865**, who threw a staircase block along the east front in **1843–45** and put a classicist façade over it, frescoed inside by **Michele Urban**, the architect to be sought among those practising at Trieste. The estate's economy turns from wine to olive oil about 1840. And the Venier–Valier disagreement is settled for Venier, from 1623. **Imotski:** four corrections. The friars were not at Proložac village but **on an islet in Prološko blato from about 1600**, marked by a stone cut A.D. 1609. The party Zuane sheltered was **fifteen people of whom nine were friars**, with a lay brother, four schoolboys and a hermit. Skalice at Omiš was begun **13 July 1716** and blessed **29 October 1718** on ground belonging to Pavao Despotović and Jakov Mariani. And **the friars did not return in 1717 — they returned in 1738**, building at Imotski from 1740. Zuane's own dates are 1673–1741. **And one unopened primary source:** at Skalice there is a book bound in sheepskin, written in bosančica on 416 leaves, which is the friars' own chronicle of the flight. It is in a friary, not an archive. **And then the thesis was read.** David cleared the repository's bot check himself, and «Uloga obitelji Franceschi u mletačkom osvajanju Imotskog» — Matea Kaćunić, Split, September 2025, 77 pages, open access — turns out to be the best single source on the Dalmatian family that exists. It corrects this archive six times and adds a second estate. Full account on the Imotski page; the PDF is now in this project's library.

rows.src: The Imotski death register, read off the page
rows.what: The first unindexed FamilySearch register image this archive has read at full resolution, rather than through the viewer's shrunken view — Imotski-Glavina, Atti di Morte, third quarter 1845
rows.got: **Entry 17. «Franceschi Domenica», 48, Cattolica, «Moglie di q.m Giovanni Vucemilovich» — and in the PATRIA column, «Nata in ALMISSA, domiciliata in IMOSCHI».** Almissa is Omiš. Her parents are given as «q.m Vicenzo Franceschi, q.m Antonia Cappelletti»; she died at three in the morning of 10 August 1845 in her husband's house of chronic gastritis, was seen by the district surgeon Ravlin on the 11th and buried the same day in the town cemetery of Imotski, by fra Bernardino Brajković. **That is the join between the Omiš branch and the Imotski household, in a parish register.** The method is the other half of the finding and it is reusable: FamilySearch serves each image as a Deep Zoom pyramid, and from a signed-in session the tiles of any chosen rectangle can be composed at true resolution — a 6180 × 4247 master read as clearly as the open book, instead of the 600-pixel view the ordinary viewer gives. Written up on the Parish Books page. **Every unindexed volume this archive has listed is now actually readable.**

rows.src: Donji Proložac, deaths 1837–1859 — swept page by page
rows.what: The whole register read for the surname, to test the Frančeski gravestone the family photographed in that churchyard. FamilySearch film 005494056, item 2, images 61–111, unindexed; read by composing the Deep Zoom tiles of each page's name column at full resolution
rows.got: **No Franceschi and no Frančeski in twenty-two years of that parish's dead.** The surnames are Šegarić, Prlina, Ćurić, Grizinić, Zorko, Martinis, Vlašanović, Smoljan, Dujmović, Babajko, Točina, Fazinić, Kosulić, Šimac, Marinović, Rosulić, Šinožić — a Croatian peasant parish with no Italian household in it, and the names do not change even when the register itself switches from Italian to Croatian in the 1850s. One near miss checked and discarded: «Maria Martinna Franinacich», image 74. **A complete negative is worth more here than a hit would have been**: it says the family were not parishioners of Proložac, so the stone is either later than 1859 or belongs to someone brought there — and there is a reason they would be brought there, because their own church at Opačac is in the immediate vicinity of the village. Next: Imotski deaths after 1851, and the Proložac deaths from 1859 on, which are not on FamilySearch but are digitised on HDA rolls ZM-34F/1118 and ZM-34F/1119.

rows.src: Šišić, «An Abridged Political History of Rieka (Fiume)», Paris 1919
rows.what: A 160-page brief written for the Paris Peace Conference by a member of the Yugoslav delegation, with a documentary appendix of Fiume's nineteenth-century election papers. Read in full for the surname and for the Istrian and Kvarner place-names
rows.got: **One hit in a hundred and sixty pages, and it is the right one.** Appendix XVIII, the protocol of the electoral committee of Fiume's second college, 20 April 1871: the assessors are «Signor Francesco Defranceschi» and Francesco Seemann under president Pietro Dabalà, and the protocol is signed at the foot **«Frco Defranceschi»**. 128 of 1,115 electors voted; 126 chose Dr Antonio Randich to replace the resigning Giovanni de Ciotta in the Croatian-Slavonian Diet. Almost certainly Kobler's Francesco Giuseppe de Franceschi, patrician councillor and royal harbourmaster, of the stock that came «da Pisino» — which is the County of Pazin, which is where this archive's own villages are. Written up on the Kobler page. It also names a source worth chasing: the Fiume electoral roll of 1871.

rows.src: Regan & Nadilo, «Istarski kašteli … sjeverno od Čepićkog polja», Građevinar 2012
rows.what: A civil-engineering journal's architectural survey of the fortified places north of the Čepić field, including Gologorica building by building — supplied by the family
rows.got: **A hard date for the lease, and a name for the relief.** The Gologorica benefice was founded in **1443** by the Pazin provost Andreas Schuel; Frederick III took the right of appointment; the holders were the captains of Pazin and the bishops of Pedena, then the Marquis de Prié, then Charles Antoine Biotz, and «**naposljetku od 1772. obitelj De Franceschi … do ukidanja feudalnih odnosa 1848**» — the De Franceschi held it on lease from **1772 to 1848**, seventy-six years. That fits Carlo's «affitto fermo» rather than contradicting it, and dates it. The house is described as «velika kamena palača obitelji De Franceschi, dvokatna građevina s balkonom i portalom iz 1711., ukrašena grbom i natpisom te **reljefom s prikazom Isusa**» — which settles a thing this site once got wrong: the relief over the door is a figure of Christ, and it is real. Also: Gologorica burned in 1463, 1508 and 1511; the bell tower finished 1740; an Imago pietatis of 1446 and a Glagolitic inscription of 1595 in the parish church; and **Mikula Gologorički**, priest of this parish, wrote the Croatian Glagolitic version of the Istrian Boundary Settlement of 1325.

rows.src: Four more PDFs from the family, September 2026
rows.what: Šišić's Fiume brief of 1919; Regan and Nadilo's architectural survey of the Istrian castles; a Croatian historiography syllabus; Belaj on sacred triangular structures; and Orbanić in Acta Histriae 32 (2024)
rows.got: **Three yields, one modest, one nothing.** Šišić gives a Francesco Defranceschi signing a Fiume election protocol in 1871. Regan and Nadilo date the Gologorica benefice lease to **1772–1848** and name the relief over the door as a figure of Christ. **Orbanić is the most valuable of the four, and not for its subject.** Its source list cites «Župni arhiv Gologorice, Matična knjiga krštenih 1691–1763» and «Matična knjiga umrlih 1646–1777» — **the Gologorica parish registers, in the parish, being read by a historian in 2024.** This archive has been saying they are the great absence in every collection it has searched. They exist, and the deaths start in 1646. It also gives Petar Kruzila, parish priest there 1722–31, deaf from a fall for doubting a miracle. The historiography notes add Carlo De Franceschi's full bibliography and his offices — secretary of the Istrian provincial committee at Poreč 1861–76, president of the Istrian archaeological society 1866–69 — with the flat Croatian verdict «potpuno prožet talijanskim duhom Istre». **Belaj on «Crkvina i svete trokutne strukture» has nothing**: zero occurrences of the surname in 670 lines. It is a study of pre-Christian sacred landscape geometry and is not relevant to this family.

rows.src: Scribd, swept from a signed-in session
rows.what: The surname in every spelling crossed with the towns and the events — Gologorica, Gallignana, Pisino, Pazin, Fiume, Buccari, Crikvenica, Ližnjan, Fažana, Medulin, Mione, Seghetto, Omiš, Imotski, Perinuša, and the 1945 census and cadastre
rows.got: **Scribd is a library of uploaded scans, so it behaves like a bad index over good books.** Most name-plus-town queries return nothing (Gologorica, Gallignana, Pisino, Ližnjan, Medulin, Seghetto all zero) and the broad ones return noise — «Defranceschi» alone gives 517 documents, of which the top hit is a lute suite. But four real things came out of it, and one is important. **«ISTRA — Popis stanovništva 1945. / Cadastre National de l'Istrie», 664 pages, printed by Nakladni zavod Hrvatske at Zagreb in July 1946** — the ethnic cadastre the Yugoslav side took to the peace negotiations, and the source behind this archive's «twenty-five Defranceschi families left in Istria on 1 October 1945». The whole book is there. **S. Bertoša, «Puljska prezimena prema popisima krizmanika iz 1825. g.»** — Pula surnames from the confirmation lists of 1825, which bears directly on the Pula–Fažana–Ližnjan cluster this archive has just opened. **«Dalmacija — prezimena 1725»**, twice uploaded, for the Omiš and Imotski side. And **G. Radossi's historical and comparative toponymy**, 439 pages, which returns hits for both Fiume and Fažana. **What Scribd will not do is give the text.** Its reader loads page by page behind the subscription, in-document search is not offered on these files, and downloads are blocked from this browser. So the sweep's product is a shelf list rather than a reading: four titles worth having, all of them published books that should be looked for in a library or an open repository as well.

rows.src: «Rassegna di storia istriana» and «Čemu» 28 — two more scans from the family
rows.what: Both read in full for the surname
rows.got: **The Rassegna is Carlo, seen from the Slovene and Croatian side.** Fourteen mentions, all of him as a historian: «L'Istria — note storiche» (Parenzo 1879), «Sulle varie popolazioni dell'Istria» (1852), and a **«Studio critico sull'istrumento della pretesa reambulazione di confini»** that this archive's bibliography of him did not have. He appears again in the 1848 group with Michele Facchinetti and Francesco Vidulich. **«Čemu» 28 has nothing at all** — zero occurrences of the surname in eighty-three lines. It is a philosophy faculty's journal presentation and has no bearing on this family. Recorded so it is not searched again.

rows.src: The Zoppola thread — tested and cut
rows.what: The one clue that pointed the Pula–Fažana–Ližnjan cluster at Friuli: a Giambattista De Franceschi with children registered at Zoppola in Udine in 1779, 1811 and 1813
rows.got: **Not evidence. A Smart Match.** Four things kill it. The tree gives the same father a daughter **Lucia born 1779 and dead 1813** and a second daughter **Lucia born 19 January 1811** — a second living daughter given her sister's name, which does not happen; so these are two men. The 1813 citation names him «Giambattista De Franceschi **o Samassa**», and **Samassa is a Zoppola surname in its own right** — Samassa Rachele and Samassa Giovanni are both in Zoppola's own civil registers. A full-text sweep returns De Franceschi all across that plain: Azzano Decimo 1897, Cordenons, Pordenone 1888 and 1898, Zoppola. And **Zoppola is the Friulian plain twenty-five kilometres west of Pordenone; Carnia is sixty kilometres north, in the mountains** — so even a real link would not have been a Carnian one. The cluster is back to having no origin, which is the honest position.

rows.src: Križman, «Antička svjedočanstva o Istri» (1979) — found online and read
rows.what: David asked whether the book could be found. It can: the full text is uploaded to both Scribd and idoc.pub, and it was read there
rows.got: **Carlo De Franceschi is cited eleven times** — indexed at pages 170, 189, 192, 193, 211 and 263, with «L'Istria, note storiche» (Poreč 1879) quoted at pp. 10–11, 38ff, 45 and 67, on the topography of the Istrian war of 177 BC, the siege of Nesactium, and whether the Pontic and Adriatic Histri are one people. Križman sets him beside Kandler, Gnirs, Benussi and Zippel, and endorses his identification of Livy's **Mutila with Medulin** and Faveria with Mutvoran as the least likely to be wrong. **And it puts Gologorica in antiquity**: Gnirs's proposal that the ancient Alùon lay on the Veli potok **between Pićan and Gologorica**, where the Roman inscriptions CIL V 322, 323, 424 and 425 were found.

rows.src: Twenty-three scans from the family, read and ranked in one pass
rows.what: Every one converted to text and tested for the surname in five spellings and for fifteen place-names, then the ones that scored were read
rows.got: **Three worth a section, five worth a line, eleven with the places but not the family, and four that cannot be read at all.** The best is **«LOS FRANCESCHI, la pequeña historia de una familia»** by Napoleón Franceschi González (Caracas 2002) — the Corsican branch written from inside it, from **Ersa in Cap Corse**, first generation **Pietro Franceschi 1694–1771**, out through the French Caribbean to Venezuela, with **not one line touching Istria**. That closes the Corsica marker on the family's map. **«Atti» 39 of Rovinj** yields Camillo De Franceschi's Pula bibliography, including **«Testamenti polesani del secolo XV con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola»** — sixteen fifteenth-century Pula wills he transcribed, which is the obvious next reading for the southern-Istrian cluster. **«Istra iz pera Nobilea»** reports the **ex libris «De Franceschi – Seghetto»** on books in the Provincial Library — the Seget house's own library — and has Camillo buying the Nobile drawings at Koper in 1934 and 1941, and Giulio drawing monuments better than Nobile did. **Four are image-only with no text layer and need OCR**: the Planckenstein almanac of Trieste 1869 (327 pages), Jelenić on the sacred art of Umag and its surroundings (135 pages), the Hrvati i Karolinzi catalogue, and «Piazza Maggiore era troppo piccola». The first two are worth the trouble; an 1869 Littoral almanac is exactly where a harbourmaster or a civic assessor is listed by name.

rows.src: Jelenić, «Sakralno bogatstvo Umaga i okolice» — OCR'd and read
rows.what: A 168-megabyte image-only scan with no text layer at all, put through optical character recognition on this project's machine and then searched. 135 pages, parallel Croatian and English
rows.got: **Four things, and one of them is a correction.** A section on **Seget**: the villa fifteen hundred metres from Umag among the vineyards on the Novigrad road, passing to the De Franceschi in **1720**, «ranije vlasništvo **Katarine Bernardo Valier**» — which gives the vendor a Christian name and **moves the Venier–Valier question to Valier**, against this site's earlier reading. The **library** confirmed from the parish's side — «vrlo bogatu knjižnicu» — matching the ex libris «De Franceschi – Seghetto» found in the Provincial Library. The **family chapel**, right of the villa entrance with its own door and a small apse outside; a wooden altar, an Assumption with St Anthony and St Catherine, an old canvas of St Lucy, a wall cupboard — **restored in the 1990s, and Mass said in it once a year on Easter Monday.** And in the parish church of Umag, a canvas of **1650**, Our Lady of the Rosary, whose painter's name is illegible but which carries **the arms of the De Franceschi of Umag — nineteen years before the flight from Candia.** Either the arms were added later by a donor family, or the name was at Umag before 1669. Not resolved, and not guessed at.

rows.src: «Guida schematica di Trieste» 1869 — OCR'd and read
rows.what: 327 pages of city directory, scanned at 122 megabytes with no text layer; converted on this project's machine and searched for the surname in every spelling
rows.got: **Four occurrences in three hundred and twenty-seven pages, and two of them are people.** «**Defranceschi Corrado, controllore in pens., V. Caserma 12**» — a retired controller of the imperial financial service, listed among the possidenti e privati. And «**Gleyre Costante (Enrico de Franceschi), in manifatture e pece, V. S. Spiridione 7**» — a merchant house in textiles and pitch, with Enrico de Franceschi named as the man behind it. The other two are Franceschinelli and Defrancesco, different formations of the same root, recorded so the next search does not stop at them. Nothing joins either man to a line on this site; what the book proves is that two households of the name were living and trading in Trieste in 1869, twenty years before Camillo De Franceschi settled there. The directories for other years would say whether they stayed.

rows.src: The Pazin archive's own price list — the acquisitions queue, priced
rows.what: «Acquisitions» has sat on this project's research log as a wish list for months. DAPA publishes a current price list; it was read, and most of what was wanted turns out to be in print and cheap
rows.got: **Seven titles, about a hundred and fifty-four euro, and the first three would close three questions this site currently prints as open.** **Jelinčić's «Knjiga ređenja u Pićnu (Prothocollum) 1632–1783», €19.91** — a hundred and fifty years of Pedena ordinations, and an ordination entry names the ordinand's father. This archive has four priests of the name it cannot place. **Orbanić's edition of de Buset's spiritual visitation of 1788, €13.27**, 477 pages, ISBN 978-953-7640-30-9, published in the Vatican and covering Gologorica and Gallignana parish by parish in the last year of the diocese of Pićan. **Doblanović Šuran and Mogorović Crljenko, «Matična knjiga krštenih župe Umag 1483–1643», €26.54** — which is the direct test of the 1650 painting in Umag that carries the family arms nineteen years before the family is supposed to have arrived. Then **Joksimović's edition of Valier's 1580 apostolic visitation of the diocese of Pula, €60**, aimed straight at the unplaced southern-Istrian cluster; the **1571 urbarium of the County of Pazin, €10**; Slukan Altić's «Katastar Istre», €9.29; and DAPA's own beginner's guide to genealogy in its holdings, €15. Two wanted volumes are sold out. Both the translator and the editor of the 1788 visitation — **Jakov Jelinčić and Elvis Orbanić** — are already on this project's list of people to write to, and both work at Pazin.

rows.src: ANNO — «Defranceschi» + «Buccari»
rows.what: The Austrian National Library's historical newspapers, for the Bakar question David asked months ago
rows.got: **Nine issues, named and dated — and the reader is behind a bot check.** The search itself runs: *Gazzetta di Zara*, 4 August 1840 (3 hits in the text); *Agramer Zeitung*, 27 December 1845 and 6 July 1898; *Vereinigte Laibacher Zeitung*, 8 June 1876, and *Laibacher Tagblatt*, 23 June 1876 — the same story from two papers a fortnight apart; *Il giovine Pensiero* of Pula, 21 December 1894 and 1 August 1896; the *Pharmaceutischer Almanach* of 1904 (4 hits); and the *Allgemeine Sport-Zeitung* of 1886. **The page viewer at data.onb.ac.at is behind a Cloudflare check, and this archive does not answer those.** The nine citations are exact and any reader can open them; what cannot be done from here is read them. The Zadar paper of 1840 is the one to open first.

rows.src: IstriaNet — Camillo De Franceschi's collected bibliography
rows.what: A queued item finally worked: the site's page of his selected works
rows.got: **Forty-five entries between 1898 and 1964, with volumes and pages**, compiled from the Italian librarians' biographical database and the Trieste civic library catalogue. Three land on questions open on this site today. **«Testamenti polesani del secolo XV, con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola», AMSI 42 (1930), pp. 167–219** — now properly cited, and aimed straight at the unplaced Pula cluster. **«La popolazione di Pola nel secolo XV e nei seguenti», Archeografo Triestino ser. 3 vol. 3 (1906), pp. 221–315** — the same question from the other side, ninety-four pages of it. And **«Quando e da chi sia stato ideato l'apocrifo istrumento di confinazione della Contea di Pisino con la data del 1325», Archivio Veneto ser. 5, 30/31 (1942)** — in which Camillo, of Gologorica, argues that the Istrian Boundary Settlement is a forgery, a document whose Glagolitic version was written by the parish priest of Gologorica. Also «I Castelli della Val d'Arsa» (1900), with unpublished documents and genealogical trees, and «Ricordi di biblioteca» (1959), seventy-four pages by the man who bought the Nobile drawings and shelved the Seget library.

rows.src: «Piazza Maggiore era troppo piccola» — OCR'd
rows.what: The third of the four image-only scans, converted and searched
rows.got: **Nothing, and it is not even the right century.** One hundred and thirty-one pages converted; a single occurrence of the name, and it is **Lydia Franceschi**, in a report of an Italian workers' and students' meeting of the late 1970s. The book is about the Bologna student movement. No Istrian place-name in it worth the count. Recorded so it is never opened for this purpose again.

rows.src: «Gazzetta di Zara», 4 August 1840 (ANNO)
rows.what: The oldest of the nine issues ANNO returned for «Defranceschi» + «Buccari», read page by page
rows.got: **One occurrence of the surname, and it is at Omiš, not Bakar.** A state-property auction notice of the I.R. Pretura d'Almissa, 6 July 1840, lists a vineyard at Strane in Vrisovec «tenuto a colonia al quarto da **D. Nicolò Defranceschi**», fiscal value fl. 8 k. 20. **«Buccari» appears in a wholly separate notice pages away** — so ANNO's pairing is whole-issue co-occurrence, not a Defranceschi at Bakar, and the Bakar lead is weaker than it looked. Published on the Omiš line. PDF fetched by David; the bot check was not answered.

rows.src: «Hrvati i Karolinzi» — the 2000 exhibition catalogue, OCR'd
rows.what: Two hundred pages of the fourth image-only scan converted and searched
rows.got: **No person of the name, and none expected** — the catalogue is about the ninth century. But the surname is in it three times, and every one of them is **Camillo De Franceschi in the bibliography**, cited for his 1932 and 1933 work on the early-medieval church sculpture of Pula and Sv. Ivan od Nimfeja, alongside Gnirs, Marušić, Šonje and Rapanić. Sixty-seven years after he published, the standard national catalogue of Croatia's Carolingian-period art still cites him by name. Recorded as a nil return for people and a footnote for Camillo.

rows.src: Darovec, «Migration to Istria and the North Adriatic in the Modern Age» (2021)
rows.what: The queued migration paper, read in full — from the publisher's open PDF, not from academia.edu
rows.got: **No occurrence of the surname, and the best contextual source this archive has found.** It puts both of our Istrian arrivals inside documented movements: the *Carni* as one of the named peoples of Istria in Petronio's list of 1681, settling exactly at **Pazin, Pićan, Gradišće, Žminj and Tinjan**; the Slavicisation of immigrant Friulian surnames (*Furlanich*, *Callegarich*), which is the mechanism behind **Defrančeski**; and **twelve Venetian attempts between 1530 and 1669** to settle Greeks from Crete and the Morea in Istria, the survivors absorbed into the Italian-speaking towns. Published on the Lines page. Note for method: academia.edu is behind a bot check this archive will not answer, and the paper was open on the publisher's own site all along.

rows.src: Rotilio Defranceschi, in Argentina and in America
rows.what: «Rotilio» as a given name across the Argentine record; the surname in Argentina 1900–1910; and the whole United States index
rows.got: **Nothing, and the lore loses its one prop.** A dozen Argentine Rotilios — Voltolini, Cichini, Moreira, Jurado, Ballesteros — and not one of the surname; a dozen Argentine Defranceschi, all of them an Italian-mainland stock with Piergiacomi and Rosso in-laws, and not one Rotilio. Meanwhile the album's detail that «he married Albina Chinkopan» turns out to be **his sister's marriage**: Albina De Franceschi, born 14 April 1900, married Frank Chinkopan of the same village and died at Brooklyn in 1945. Published on the Eleven.

rows.src: The Eleven of Gračišće, against the American record
rows.what: United States naturalizations, censuses, death certificates and the Numident, searched for every child of Antonio the mason
rows.got: **Five of the eleven documented in New York, four of them in Brooklyn.** The proof is a misspelling: Albina's New York death certificate of 27 April 1945 names her mother **«Maria Walhart»** and Bruno's naturalization names her **«Mary Walhal»** — both of them the **Volhardt** the Gračišće priest wrote in 1925. Also corrects this archive: Antonio «Tony», whom the album put in Italy, naturalised at Brooklyn in 1922 and 1929.

rows.src: Monheim — the German telephone directory, nationally
rows.what: Every spelling of the surname searched across the whole of Germany, after the archive realised it had been searching the wrong Monheim
rows.got: **One private listing in the entire country**, spelt «Defranceski» exactly as this family spells it, at **Langenfeld (Rheinland) — five kilometres from Monheim am Rhein, in the same district**. The only «Defranceschi» in Germany is a company at Mannheim, the German arm of an Italian winery-equipment firm. This archive had been reading the map pin's coordinates literally and searching **Bavaria**; there are two Monheims and it was looking at the wrong one. Living people, so no one is named. Published on the Ližnjan page as a correction.

rows.src: Brhan, «Stare cum loco et foco» — the fourth paper, read in full
rows.what: The Carnia–Istria emigration study hosted openly by the Amici dell'Orologeria Pesarina, searched for every occurrence of the surname
rows.got: **Twenty-two occurrences, and one of them closes a gap this archive has flagged as open on four pages.** Brhan prints the Catasto franceschino of 1820 for Moncalvo: **six De Franceschi proprietor households — Maria, Giuseppe, «Giobatta (di Gallignana)», Leonardo and Antonio** — «the most influential family» in a district of ten Croatian villages. A Giobatta *of Gallignana* holding at Moncalvo is the first object that puts the two villages together. Also new: a **Stanzia De Franceschi at Sanvincenti**, lost by 1820; Defranceschi among the Carnian families in the Barban contrade; and, after Bertoša 1985, that the Moncalvo family came from **Agrons** with gismanial feudal rights and that the **Umag family is of «un'origine completamente diversa»**. Academia.edu hosts it too, behind a bot check; the Carnian association's own site does not.

rows.src: HR-DARI-254 — the family's own archive, finding aid read in full
rows.what: The published register of fonds of the State Archive in Rijeka, for both De Franceschi fonds
rows.got: **The 1610 problem is closed.** The fond's earliest item is the **Glagolitic income book of the parish church at Hum, 1610–1685** — the only Croatian-language item in it, and part of the family's *collection*, not its papers. The collector was «most probably Carlo De Franceschi». The family's own earliest paper is **1703**. Also recovered: an eighteenth-century business of **money-lending and buying up debts** reaching Kastav, Mošćenice, Labin and Carniola; and the fact that **until 1990 this fond was physically merged with the Šeget family's fond «through ignorance of the family's history»** — the same confusion this site argues against, made by the archive that holds both.

rows.src: Tassini, «Curiosità veneziane» (1872) — the Venetian street-name authority
rows.what: The standard dictionary of Venetian toponymy, downloaded whole and searched for the surname
rows.got: **The street is real and the entry is a windfall.** «FRANCESCHI (Rio terrà dei) a' SS. Apostoli» — and before the canal was filled in it was crossed by **a Ponte dei Franceschi**. Named for the *cittadini* family whose arms were **a lion rampant, motto «Sero sapimus»**, and specifically for the houses of **Benda Franceschi (redecima of 1514)** and her nephew and heir **Andrea, Grand Chancellor**, who declared a *casa da statio* there in 1537. Four new facts about Andrea, three further Venetian vignettes, and one earlier dismissal reopened.

rows.src: «Defranceschi bridge, Rijeka»
rows.what: Croatian sources, the maritime-heritage register and the Rijeka chronologies
rows.got: **There is no bridge. There is a pier — «De Franceschijev gat», the former Mol Zichy**, in the main harbour: 150 m east, 134 m west, 80 m south. The first iron-and-concrete building in the port went up on it in 1882, and the **first electric light in Rijeka was lit on it**, by Zipernowsky, with lamps borrowed from the Torpedo Factory. **Who the De Franceschi is, no source says**; the city archive would settle it.

rows.src: Raymundus Defranceschi, b. 9 October 1823
rows.what: The Status Animarum page re-read at full magnification, and every index searched in every spelling of both names
rows.got: **Alive at home and unmarried in about 1848, and then nothing at all.** The house 5 page gives him all four sacramental ticks and **leaves both the marriage and the death column empty** — as it does for all four sons. The indexes have no Raymundus, Raimondo, Rajmund or Raymond of this surname anywhere on earth, in any century.
