The eldest son of the house vanishes and the second son inherits, which is why this archive's whole spine runs through Antonio. Three bounded things would break it: the Gallignana death register 1848–1880, the marriage register for the same years, and the Austrian conscription lists for the County of Pazin.

rows.src: Doblanović on Svetvinčenat, «Sezonska kretanja začeća/rođenja» (2012)
rows.what: The full paper, fetched from an open repository after the Croatian journal host went behind a bot check
rows.got: Confirms and sharpens what this archive already quoted. The Carnian surnames — De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis — are in the 1734 Status animarum **only inside the castello of Svetvinčenat, not in the villages around it**, and the Carnians «were mainly in trade», working as **prekupci i preprodavači — buyers-up and resellers**. The same economic type the Rijeka finding aid describes for the Gologorica house: money-lending and buying up debts.

rows.src: hrcak.srce.hr, and the Croatian «Dabar» repositories
rows.what: Four queued Croatian journal and thesis PDFs
rows.got: **Both are now behind bot checks that this archive will not answer.** hrcak.srce.hr returns «Confirm you're not a robot», and so does the Dabar repository network that carries the Pula and Koper university theses. This archive has used hrcak successfully before, so this is a change rather than a rule. Where a paper exists elsewhere — a university's own site, CORE, an author's page — it can still be read; the Doblanović paper above was got that way. Recorded so the same doors are not knocked on twice.
rows.dest: Hrčak — Portal of Croatian scientific journals

rows.src: Pomara, «An Attempted Albanian Settlement in Istria (1610–1612)», Diasporas 43 (2025)
rows.what: An open-access article on Venetian-organised settlement in Istria
rows.got: **No person of the name.** Carlo De Franceschi is cited as an authority — on the depopulation of Istria and on Poreč falling to some three hundred souls by 1601 — which is one more instance of the historian still being quoted, this time in 2025. Nothing for the family.

rows.src: Pomorski i povijesni muzej Hrvatskog primorja, Rijeka
rows.what: The museum's digital collection searched for the surname
rows.got: The public search returns nothing for any spelling, and the interface is script-driven rather than searchable from here. **Not a negative worth trusting** — 75,000 objects in 48 collections, and the digital fundus is a fraction of it. The museum should be written to, along with the Rijeka city archive about the De Franceschi pier.
rows.dest: Pomorski i povijesni muzej HP, Rijeka

rows.src: «Zbirka obitelji De Franceschi u NSK» (Libellarium 13/2, 2022)
rows.what: A search for the Šeget fond's finding aid turned this up instead
rows.got: **The family's library is not lost. It is in Zagreb, and it has been catalogued.** 2,396 items, 1503–1945, taken out of the house at Gologorica in 1948–49, boxed, and left unprocessed in the National and University Library's store for sixty years — not in the card catalogue, not in the electronic one, «nobody could know of its existence». Processing began 2009 and finished in 2021. It holds an Aldine of 1503, the signatures of five generations, letters of D'Annunzio, poems of Giuseppina Martinuzzi, and the very Metastasio, Petrarch, Tasso and Ariosto that Carlo says he found on the family shelves as a schoolboy. Published on the Library page.

rows.src: MyHeritage, tree 4 — the whole surname re-harvested
rows.what: 386 given names × four spellings of the surname, then a person-panel fetch for every hit
rows.got: **573 individuals of the name in the live tree** — a hundred and fourteen more than the harvest of a year ago, which ran on a shorter name list. Merged into the roster, they take it from 577 people to **1,021**, of whom **572 now carry a FamilySearch record link and 513 a link into the tree**. They also open two clusters this archive had barely registered: **forty-four in Trentino and South Tyrol** — Telve, Strigno, Fiera di Primiero, Laives, Cles — and the **Corsican family at Tomino and Mandolacce**, which the Lines page already draws as its own lane. The earliest are three at Pula born 1669, 1671 and 1674.

rows.src: «Croazia, Austria» — resolving the unnamed parish
rows.what: The three earliest people in the roster, traced from index entry to image ark to film to catalogue
rows.got: **A method, and a correction.** FamilySearch's Croatian index often gives no parish at all — just «Croazia, Austria». But every persona carries the ark of the image it was read from, and the digital-archive service turns that ark into a **DGS film number**, which the catalogue names. The three earliest — born 1669, 1671 and 1674 — resolve to **DGS 005497884 = «Matična knjiga 1568–1917», Župa Svetvinčenat**. Which means the entries this archive has published for a year as «**Pula 1667**», the opening of the whole southern-Istrian line, are **Svetvinčenat entries**. The same film gives a continuous De Franceschi presence there from **1657 to 1737** under twelve different fathers. This is now standard practice for any «Croazia, Austria» row.
rows.dest: The parish books, on this site

rows.src: The whole Croatian index, resolved film by film
rows.what: 954 indexed records of the surname traced from index entry to image ark to DGS film to catalogue
rows.got: **Ninety-three parishes.** This archive had eighteen. The Croatian index mostly gives no parish — «Croazia, Austria» — but every persona carries the ark of the image it was read from, and that resolves to a film, and the film is named. Done for all 954 records it draws the map: **Omiš 145 from 1634, Rijeka 105 from 1626, Ližnjan 100 from 1794, Svetvinčenat 85 from 1666, Pula 63 from 1659**, and Bakar exactly five, 1772–1819, which is the household this archive had already reconstructed from another direction. New and unsuspected: **Vižinada 53**, Draguč 25, **Rovinj 23 from 1619** — the earliest date on the map — **Dubrovnik 38** across two parishes, and Bednja and Pregrada in the Zagorje from 1706 and 1674. Published as a chart on the Every Town page.
rows.dest: The parish books, on this site

rows.src: The roster, attributed parish by parish
rows.what: Every record id in the film map joined back onto the 1,021 people
rows.got: **367 of the 1,021 now carry the name of the parish register they were actually found in**, across 27 parishes — recovered from records the index labelled only «Croazia, Austria». The «no place» bucket falls from 386 people to 185, and «not placed» rises from 150 to 323, which is the honest direction: naming the parish usually tells you the family is one this archive has not attached to a line. Filterable on the People page as «Parish known».

rows.src: Svetvinčenat parish register, DGS 005497884 — read, not searched
rows.what: Images 397, 398 and 442 opened tile by tile and read line by line
rows.got: **Three unindexed occurrences on the first three openings.** «M.ro Nadal de Franceschi» stands godfather on 20 May 1666, five months before his own daughter is baptised; «il Sig.r Ant.o di Franceschi» stands godfather on 9 February 1674. Godparent roles are never indexed, which is the whole reason to open the page. The baptisms of Colotta (24 Oct 1666) and Fioretta (22 Nov 1666) are confirmed word for word, both fathers styled **M.ro**. And the company is the argument: the godparents across these openings are **Spinoti, Fiorenza, Felicer, Fabri** — the Canale di Gorto set, standing at each other's fonts in a Croatian village in 1666. By 1674 Anto is **Sig.r** and his son's compare is a **Count Luciani**: the same household, eight years, artisan to gentleman.

rows.src: «il Sig.r Conte Lucciani», Svetvinčenat 1674 — chased
rows.what: The godfather at Mattio de Franceschi's baptism, traced through the index and the films
rows.got: **He is of the Albona house.** The surname enlarges cleanly to **Lucciani**; the place after «da» will not settle between D and R. The index carries a Luciani family baptising at exactly these dates — Bartolomio Zuane on 12 November 1674, and five more between 1682 and 1693 — and every one of them resolves to the parish register of **Labin (Albona)**, DGS 005494791–2. Which closes a circle: Carlo De Franceschi names «cav. Tomaso Luciani … di Albona» among his sources in 1879, Luciani's **ex libris** is in the family library now at Zagreb, and Hauptmann found **letters of Tomaso Luciani** in the wrecked house at Gologorica in 1945. Two hundred years, one surname, one town — pairing stated, descent not claimed.

rows.src: Count Damian de Franceschis (Gallignana, 1720) — searched again
rows.what: Carlo De Franceschi's «L'Istria: note storiche» (1879) downloaded whole and searched
rows.got: **Not there.** The full text of Carlo's own history of Istria contains no Damiano de Franceschi and no count of the surname — nine occurrences of «Franceschi» in the whole book, none of them him. So the only man ever recorded as **Comes Damianus de Franceschis** is still known from exactly one line of one baptism register, and the family's own historian, writing a hundred and sixty years later about his own county, had never heard of him.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat film, seven openings read band by band
rows.got: **Eight occurrences the index does not have, all godparent roles**, plus four baptisms confirmed word for word. The best line is «Comp.ri furono **M.ro Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero**» (25 Oct 1667) — a patronymic, which gives Anto a father and pushes the family a generation behind the twelve the index knows. Also: Mattia of 1669 is «fig.a… nata», **a daughter**, not the son the name suggested; Anto stands godfather twice in eight days in October 1669; and the honorifics turn out **not** to be a clean ladder — M.ro, S.r and no style at all all appear in 1669–71, which corrects a tidier claim published here earlier. Carnian company in the same pages: **Spinotti, Fiorencis, Felice, Fabris, Festa**. Twelve openings of this film still to read.

rows.src: Wikimedia Commons — portraits for the people pages
rows.what: A first pass at David's request that our people have faces, as his old site's did
rows.got: **Seven images found, licensed, captioned and wired in** — and one of them is a discovery in its own right. Searching for Domenico de' Franceschi the printer turned up the title page of **Palladio's «I quattro libri dell'architettura», Venice 1570, «Appresso Dominico de' Franceschi»** — the most influential architectural book ever printed, and this archive's entry for him had never mentioned it. Also: a portrait of **Carlo De Franceschi** (PD, before 1893); Domenico's own woodcut of **Charles V storming La Goletta** from the Statens Museum for Kunst; the **Vayron lithograph of Franceschi-Delonne** and Philippoteaux's painting of his capture in 1809; the **Dien engraving after Riesener of Jean-Marie-Antoine Defrance, 1820** — which also supplies his death year, 1835, that this archive lacked; and the National Gallery of Art's *After Titian* portrait of **Andrea de' Franceschi** (CC0). Built by a new tool, `tools/commons.py`, which keeps every image's Commons page, licence, author and date.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat, DGS 005497884 — nineteen openings, the indexed run complete
rows.what: Every image the index pointed at, read band by band: 1666–1707
rows.got: **Twenty occurrences the index does not have**, sixteen of them godparent roles. Eleven baptisms verbatim; one filiation («Ant.o di Franceschi **di Piero**»); one death dated (Batta, before July 1688); three people added; one sex corrected (Mattia 1669 is a daughter); **one duplicate found in the register itself** — a boy called Piero baptised twice, 6 and 15 October 1707, to a father written Nardo once and Lunardo once and a mother Eufemia both times, with **the same two godparents in both entries**; one within-family godparent link; and **M.ro Mattio Lupieri** standing for a De Franceschi child in 1707. It also overturned this archive's own reading of opening 578 as empty — it is not. **What the film did not give is an origin** — not one entry says where these people came from. And 576 of its 595 images, including all the marriages and deaths, are still unread.

rows.src: Stjepan Antoljak, «Hrvati u prošlosti» (475 pp., supplied by David)
rows.what: Full-text search of the whole book for every spelling of the surname
rows.got: **Two finds, and one of them is uncomfortable.** Antoljak cites Carlo De Franceschi twenty-one times across his study of the Slav settlement of Istria — and corrects him twice: once for misreading a charter («netočno pročitan»), once, harder, for writing in 1885 that Istria was never occupied or ruled by any Slav people, having confused the Rječina with the Raša. Published on Carlo's Book, under the claim it complicates. And, in the Zadar chapter, **a palace: «Ferro-Grisogono-Franceschi», on the corner of Široka ulica**, with a footnote to an article «Famiglia Franceschi» in the Zadar almanac for 1859 that this project had never heard of.

rows.src: FamilySearch personas, surname De Franceschi, Croatia, births 1600–1700
rows.what: A filter this archive had never applied to a query it had run many times
rows.got: **Seven records nobody here had seen, and three of them read on the film.** A De Franceschi household in **Fiume in 1626** — Giovanni Antonio and Lucia, three children baptised 1626, 1628 and 1632 — **113 years before the Valentino whom Kobler and Carlo took for the first of the name in the city**. The 1628 godfather is the imperial Captain of Fiume; the 1632 baptism was performed by the Bishop of Senj in person. Almost certainly not this family, and said so on the page. Also four unread: two at Omiš (1644, and a man born about 1581 who died in 1645) and two at Split.

rows.src: Omiš and Split parish registers — DGS 005494111 and 005494166
rows.what: Opening the films behind four index entries this page had published as unread
rows.got: Three of the four read. **Two index errors corrected** — the Omiš child of January 1644 is indexed «Nicolaa, Female» and the register says «il figlio … Nicolò»; the 1645 death is indexed 20 March and the register reads 29. **Two godparent appearances that exist in no index** — Sig.ra **Francesca de Franceschi** stands twice on one opening of the Omiš book. A father styled **Cap.n Zuane de Franceschi**. An **emergency baptism at Split in 1700**, «l'acqua in casa, in caso di necessità», to Egidio de Franceschi and Maria. And **Gioannes Maria de Franceschi, died 29 March 1645 aged 64** — born about 1581, the oldest birth year this archive holds for the surname anywhere in Croatia. The fourth, a Split burial of 1716, is still unopened and is labelled so.

rows.src: Findmypast — Travel & Migration, surname «defranceschi»
rows.what: All 328 movement records harvested from the result listings (transcripts paywalled, none bought)
rows.got: **Four of the Eleven found in it, and one gravestone finished.** Bruno born 1907 petitions for United States citizenship at New York in 1939 and again in 1942 as «Bruno de Franceschi Or Seedorf»; Gerda born 1913 petitions in the same year — **the surname the Millbrook stone cut off is SEEDORF**. Antonio 1887 and Albina 1900 both cross in **1922**, brother and sister in the same year. Joseph 1892 petitions at New York in 1912, 1915 and 1916. Basilio, Dario and Benito all sail in 1955–56. And the shape of the whole file: **the commonest event is the same man arriving three times** — circulation, not emigration. Four Vermont border crossings point at the Barre granite sheds, which is where a stonecutter's sons would go. Published on Leaving.

rows.src: Findmypast — full subscription, every category, every spelling
rows.what: David took a trial and asked for everything; transcripts read, not just index rows
rows.got: **The American half of the family, in documents.** The 1930 census puts **three of the Eleven in one Brooklyn flat** — Albina, her husband Frank Chinkojan, and her brothers Anthony (immigrated 1922) and «Grochina», the enumerator's Gioacchino. **Albina's marriage licence of 23 April 1925 names her mother Maria Volhart**; Joseph's of 1926 names Maria Valbart; Bruno's of 1931 names Mary Walhal — three children, three clerks, one woman, and the parish book's Volhardt behind all of them. **Gerda's surname is Seedorf**, of Hanover. Joseph's 1917 draft card gives 12 March 1892 and «Frieste»; the 1940 census gives him a wife and two children; and a Sergeant Joseph De Franceschi of the First World War lies at Long Island National Cemetery, dead 26 April 1940, twenty-five days after that census. **Basilio died 15 June 1994.** And the fused spelling **Defranceski** returns thirty-six of its own — a family of five off the *Slovenija* at Philadelphia in 1954, and two graves at Horsham, Victoria.

rows.src: Findmypast — keyword «Gallignana», «Pedena», «Pisino»
rows.what: Searching the village name instead of the surname
rows.got: **«Gallignana» returns ten records in the whole database and three are this family's** — Joseph's naturalisation petition of 1915 and Albina's of 1928, both giving «Gallignana, Austria» as the birthplace in a United States federal record, and Albina's 1922 arrival. The other seven are the village's other emigrants: Poldrugovac, Millassich, Lanza, Silich. **«Pedena» and «Pisino» then gave the crossing**: Antonio and Albina De Franceschi, one index number apart, on the *Conte Rosso* out of Genoa in 1922 — he aged 35 living at **Pićan** with a wife **Marta** left behind, she aged 22 at Gallignana; and Albina's husband under a fourth spelling, **Frank Schinkopan of Pisino, born 24 February 1896**, naturalising at New York in 1920 and 1926.

rows.src: Findmypast — the images, through the IIIF image service
rows.what: Opening the documents behind the transcripts: census sheet, naturalisation petitions and declarations
rows.got: **An address, a ship and a date.** Albina's 1928 petition, in her own words: «I emigrated from **Genoa** on or about the **29 day of August 1922**, and arrived at the port of **New York** on the **9 day of September 1922**, on the vessel **Conte Rosso**» — and her residence, **2922 Ave. L, Brooklyn**, which is the house the 1930 census sheet shows the family **owning, valued at $16,000, with a radio**. The sheet also gives the trades: Frank Chinkojan a **chef**, Anthony a **fireman at an electric company**, and «Trochina» a **counter man in a restaurant, twenty-four weeks out of work** in the first spring of the Depression. Gerda's 1939 declaration carries her **photograph**, her arrival at New York on the **Dresden** from Bremen on **21 October 1929**, and the line «**he was born at Gallignana, Italy on August 12, 1907**». **And a correction**: the 1939 and 1942 records indexed under Bruno's name are Gerda's own papers. Two leads closed as well — Peter b.1902 was born at **Basel**, and the **1939 Register has no Defranceschi in England at all**.

rows.src: Findmypast images, second pass — Joseph's naturalisation file; BillionGraves, Horsham
rows.what: The certificate of arrival, the petition, and the Australian headstone
rows.got: **Joseph went first, and twelve years early.** His certificate of arrival, issued at Ellis Island on 2 December 1915: «Date of arrival **October 11, 1910** · Name of vessel **Martha Washington** · Line **Aus.-Amer.**» — out of **Trieste** about 24 September 1910, aged eighteen, on the Austro-Americana line. His petition gives **148 Sackett Street, Brooklyn**, on the docks, and an occupation this archive reads as **oiler**. **And the Horsham headstone is legible**: «IN LOVING REMEMBRANCE OF ZDRAVKO FRANK DEFRANCESKI · DIED 22ND DECEMBER 1979 AGED 58 · BELOVED HUSBAND OF ROSA», photographed 8 May 2018. The war-grave record for Sergeant Joseph De Franceschi is an index only — no image exists to open.

rows.src: Findmypast — the 1926 Martha Washington manifest, and a search for Marta
rows.what: Whether Antonio ever went back to the wife he left at Pićan
rows.got: **He did, and he came out again.** The manifest of the S.S. **Martha Washington** sailing from **Trieste**, stamped New York **31 May 1926**, line 6: «DEFRANCESCHI, ANTONIO, 39, married, **mason** … **last permanent residence N.Y., Brooklyn** … nearest relative in country whence came: **wife, Defranceschi Marta, Pedena 10, Istria, Italy**». «Last permanent residence Brooklyn» is a **returning resident** on a re-entry permit — so he had gone home to Istria between 1922 and 1926 and come back. **He was a mason**, the trade his father is given by in the Gračišće book of souls. And it is the ship **Joseph** crossed on in 1910. **Marta never came**: her only «record» carries the identifier one digit along from Antonio's — she is the relation field of his own manifest line. After April 1930 he appears in no American source at all, and never completed naturalisation.

rows.src: Findmypast British & Irish Newspapers — keyword «Defranceschi»
rows.what: Seventy articles; the earliest sixty are shipping intelligence
rows.got: **A whole chapter nobody knew was there.** Between **1865 and 1878** a master of this name commands Austrian ships in the Black Sea grain and Bristol Channel coal trades — the ***Natalia*** out of Constantinople and Galatz, the ***Rachel*** from Odessa to Antwerp, the ***Peppina Luigia*** Trieste to Troon, and above all the ***Aquilone***, «**Aus, 350, Defranceschi**», tracked through nineteen printed sightings from Alexandria and Sulina to Belfast, Malta, Venice, Ghent, Barcelona and out of **Cardiff for Guadaloupe on 11 December 1877**. The masters printed beside him are Bujanovich, Lacovich, Cattarinich, Ivancich, Nicolich — **the sea-captain families of Lošinj, Rijeka and Bakar**, and this archive has an unplaced *Dominus* household at Bakar. And in 1896 the South Wales Echo writes that «**Signorina Defranceschi belongs to an old Cardiff family, and has recently taken her degree at the Vienna Conservatoire of Music**», playing harpsichord recitals at the Cardiff Exhibition. Published at **/at-sea/**.

rows.src: Findmypast newspapers, second pass — «de Franceschi» and «Defranceski»
rows.what: 83 more articles under the particle spelling, and one under the fused
rows.got: **Three more Aquilone voyages** (Queenstown with Alexandria wheat, 3 July 1872; **Leith for Trieste**, January 1874; Deal, Alexandria for Stockton, February 1875) — and a second man of the sea entirely: **«George De Franceschi, A.B., an Austrian»**, giving evidence at the Board of Trade inquiry into the loss of the Shields steamer *Aberlady Bay*, June 1889. The first man of this surname anywhere in the archive who is named, dated, put on a named ship and quoted. Also **Enrico de Franceschi, baritone of La Scala** — recorded 1924 with Zita Fumagalli-Riva («here is very excellent singing»), listed in 1926 among Amato, Galeffi, Rouard and Stracciari, and **broadcast live to Britain from La Scala in March 1938 with Gigli and Pagliughi**. And the single «Defranceski» hit fills in a career: **Josip Defranceski, Director of External Services, Radio Belgrade**, leaving Peshawar for Kabul in December 1959.

rows.src: Lloyd's Register of Shipping, 1875 and 1877–78 (Internet Archive full text)
rows.what: The Aquilone's port of registry
rows.got: **She is not in it.** Both volumes downloaded and searched in full; the only near match is the French *Aquilon* of Jersey, 48 tons. That is informative rather than disappointing: Lloyd's classed British ships and foreign ships whose owners paid London. **An Austrian barque of 350 tons belongs on the register of the Austro-Hungarian Veritas, whose books are at Trieste and Rijeka.** The port of registry — the fact that would say whether she was a Bakar, Rijeka or Lošinj ship — has to be asked there. What London gives instead is her Cardiff agent, **G. Montaldo & Co**.

rows.src: British & Irish newspapers — the archive's own place-names
rows.what: Gallignana, Pisino, Buccari as keywords
rows.got: **«Gallignana»: zero articles in the entire archive.** «Pisino»: 915, every one of them OCR noise — «early rising» mis-set, and a brand of stove polish called Pisino Sun. **«Buccari»: 1,377, and all of them shipping** — Bakar had its own standing heading in the London shipping press from at least 1850, between Cagliari and Carloforte in the alphabetical run of ports. The town where this archive has twelve unplaced *Dominus* people was tracked daily by the London insurance market for a century. **And no Defranceschi ever appears under that heading.**

rows.src: Trove, National Library of Australia — newspapers and gazettes
rows.what: The Australian press, which is not on Findmypast
rows.got: «Defranceski» returns **two**, both government gazettes. «Defranceschi» returns **thirteen**, and one is a story: *The Age*, Melbourne, **25 January 1954**, «Girl Saw Friend Drown» — «**Giordano Defranceschi, laborer**, swam out into the … but Defranceschi disappeared … **before the eyes of a girl he met here last week**.» The Australian inward passenger lists carry a **Giordano de Franceschi arriving in 1950**; this archive believes they are the same man and cannot prove it. Also **DeFranceschi Bros, 716 Chappie Lane, Broken Hill**, NSW Government Gazette, 17 June 1966. **And no nineteenth-century Defranceschi in the Australian press at all** — the name arrives after the Second World War, exactly as the passenger lists say.

rows.src: NSW Unassisted Passenger Lists — the 1893 Australian outlier
rows.what: The one Australian record fifty-seven years before all the others
rows.got: **Solved, and it is not a migrant.** «INWARD. A LIST of the Crew and Passengers arrived in the Ship **Miowera** of London, **James Stott** Master, of the Burthen of 1,911 Tons, from the Port of Melbourne to Sydney, New South Wales, 1893.» In the seamen's column, dittoed down from the quartermaster above him: «**G. Defranceschi · ″ · 28 · Austrian**». **Q.M. — quartermaster**, twenty-eight, Austrian, on the overnight run from Melbourne to Sydney on **6 January 1893**. He was not going to Australia; he was passing through it. The surname reaches Australia in 1893 as a sailor and does not settle there for another fifty-seven years.

rows.src: Findmypast images, third pass — Frank Schinkopan's declaration; the Conte Rosso manifest
rows.what: Albina's husband's own papers, and the 1922 embarkation list
rows.got: **Frank Schinkopan's declaration of intention, Brooklyn 1920**: «aged 24, occupation **Cook**, complexion fair, height 5 feet 8, weight 144, hair dark brown, eyes gray; **born in Pisino, Italy, on the 24 day of February 1896**; residing **304 Ninth Avenue, Brooklyn**; emigrated **from Trieste, Austria**, on the vessel *Elenor*; **not married**; renouncing particularly **Victor Emmanuel III, King of Italy, of whom I am now a subject**; arrived at the port of New York on or about the **15 March 1920**.» A cook in a Brooklyn room in 1920; a chef owning a $16,000 house on Avenue L by 1930. **And the Conte Rosso manifest opened** — the Italian form, «Numero dei biglietto · COGNOME E NOME · **PATERNITÀ** · ETÀ» — with **De Franceschi Antonio 35** and **De Franceschi Albina 22** on consecutive lines. **The paternità column is blank but for a tick**: the one document that asked directly who their father was did not write it down. A «going to join» column exists but the rows could not be aligned across the spread with certainty and were not guessed at.

rows.src: Findmypast — deaths of Bruno and Gerda de Franceschi
rows.what: A death record for either of them
rows.got: **Nothing.** Bruno died at Millbrook, New York, on 6 July 2000 by his gravestone, and the Social Security Death Index and obituary collections on Findmypast carry neither him nor Gerda. Their dates come from the stone and from the naturalisation papers, and that is where they stay.

rows.src: Split, Župa Sv. Dujma — DGS 005494174, image 378
rows.what: The last of the four unread records
rows.got: **The best single line found all day.** The index said «Nicolo De Franceschi, burial 18 May 1716, birth 1626». The register says: «**Can.co Don Nicolò de Franceschi** ⟨*Can.co di S. Vito di Candia*⟩ passò da questa alla miglior vita **d'anni 90 incirca** … et **fù sepolto nella Chiesa del Domo in Coro nella sepoltura delli Sig.ri Can.ci**.» **A canon of a church in Candia — Crete — buried in the choir of Split cathedral in the canons' vault, aged about ninety.** Born about 1626; Candia fell to the Turks in 1669 when he was forty-three. **The Seget branch's Cretan origin has been treated on this site as the family's own tradition. It now has a document standing beside it.**

rows.src: Rovinj, Župa Rovinj — DGS 005497871, images 225 and 466
rows.what: The Rovinj records, from 1619
rows.got: **A new earliest.** «**Adì 27 Mago 1619 · morì ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola. Fu portato il suo cadavere … off. L 24**» — the oldest dated appearance of this surname in Istria the archive holds, seven years before the Fiume baptisms and a hundred and forty-two before the name is first written at Gologorica. He is styled **ser**; he is **of Pola**, not of Rovinj; his **body was carried** there; and his offering of 24 lire is near the top of a page whose other entries run at 2, 6 and 12. **And the second-oldest is also a stranger**: «Ob.to di **Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**», 27 December 1728, 6 lire — Vodnjan, which this archive lists among the *unplaced*. The film holds fourteen more, including a Rovinj household across three generations (Giacomo → Vittorio & Domenica Moscarda → Piero Anto 1736) — **and Carlo De Franceschi's own marriage to Maria Michelcich, with his parents named as «Giuseppe da Gologorizza» and «Lambertina Pesle». That image has not been opened.**

rows.src: Vodnjan (Dignano) parish registers — DGS 005497893–95, catalogue koha:963267
rows.what: Finding and opening the registers, after this archive first said they did not exist
rows.got: **Found, and a correction retracted.** This archive said in the afternoon that the seventy-eight Vodnjan records were really Vižinada's, because the catalogue answered the film number 005497893 with «Župa Vižinada». **A reel can carry two parishes.** That one holds Vižinada's deaths 1754–1831 *and* **Vodnjan's baptisms 1815–1866**, catalogue item koha:963267 — «metrical books for the Roman Catholic congregation at **Dignano** … later **Vodnjan**». The marriages **1815–1884** and deaths to **1893** are on films 894 and 895. The baptismal book is headed «**LIBER BAPTIZATORUM IN ECCLESIA S. BLASII DIGNANI**», and entry 149 of **4 December 1816** gives house **376**, «**Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore**», «**Maria Malusà q.m Matteo di Antonio**», condition **civile** — and the baptising priest is «**D. Stefano De Franceschi, de Parocho licentia**». **A priest of the name at Vodnjan, and five lay households.** The one death on that reel, **Mathaeus De Franceschi son of Anton, house 32, 7 August 1819**, is in the *Liber Defunctorum of Castellier* — **Kaštelir, under Vižinada** — which is exactly why the wrong answer looked right.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum 1815–1884 — DGS 005497894, images 172–182
rows.what: Reading the marriage register by eye, because nobody has indexed it
rows.got: **The register is not indexed.** Two hundred and eighty-six marriage-query arks were resolved against film 005497894 and **none** of them is on it, which is why these marriages have never been seen. Read opening by opening instead. Eleven openings in, **five De Franceschi appearances**: **30 March 1818, house 312 — «Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio. Maria, vedovo della q.m Veniera Franzin q.m Domenico», aged 42, marrying Lorenza Tesser q.m Ambrogio, widow of Andrea Manzin**, which puts his birth about 1776 and his father's death before 1818; **«+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe, tessitore»** and **«+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore»** as witnesses in March and September 1818, **both signing with a cross** — brothers, and a different Pietro from the widower; **«Don Stefano De Franceschi, Sacerdote»** as witness on 7 June 1819, with the page signed by **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D., parroco e preposito del Capitolo** — so Don Stefano was a priest of the town, not the parish priest; and **«la fu Domenica De Franceschi»**, mother of a bride aged 40 in November 1817, **dead before the register begins** and born about 1750. Images 183–265 still to read.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 183–187
rows.what: Reading on: 1819 and 1820
rows.got: **A priest, a ploughman and a weaver turn out to be brothers.** On 17 August 1820 the clerk writes the witness in full — «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi *di Giuseppe* — Sacerdote**» — the same patronymic already recorded for «+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore» and «+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe, tessitore», both of whom sign with a cross. Don Stefano witnesses **four** marriages in these openings (7 June and 20 August 1819, 17 August and 13 November 1820), twice beside a canon of the chapter, never as officiant — the parroco who signs every page is **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D.** Also found: **«la vivente Antonia Maria De Franceschi»**, widow of Damiano Storcovich, alive 30 June 1819 with a daughter aged 40 — a **second** woman of the name born about 1750, alongside the Domenica already dead in 1817.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, image 188
rows.what: The 1821 marriage that closes a chain
rows.got: **Four generations off one page.** From 1821 the register rules new columns — «Sponsus **et Genitores**» — and names both parties' parents in every entry. The first result: 9 June 1821, house 356, «**Gio: Maria De Franceschi figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e della fu Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**», aged 22, marrying **Lucia Bonassin**, aged 27. That is the household this archive had reconstructed from the baptism register — now with its father, grandfather and great-grandfather named. It also **settles this morning's open question**: the Gio Maria fathering children in the 1820s was flagged as probably a grandson of the Gio Maria dead by 1818, marked inf because it was not proved. It is proved.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 189–190
rows.got: **A third De Franceschi woman married out.** 14 November 1821, house 54: Maria, daughter of Alvise Birattan q.m Saba and **«Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro»**, marries at twenty-one — so Lucia married by 1799 and her father Pietro was dead by 1821, which makes him **older than the Pietro who remarried in 1818**. The witnesses are **Giannandrea Dalla Zonca, Nobile** and **Guglielmo Conte Lombardo di Pola**, and the couple needed a dispensation in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Also **Don Stefano's fifth witness appearance**, 3 July 1822, house 200. And one deliberate miss recorded — «Maddalena **Franceschich** q.m Gio, di Pinguente», a Slavic patronymic out of Buzet that is not this surname.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 191–192
rows.got: **«Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., da Dignano — Tessitore»**, witness on 30 January 1824 at a marriage celebrated in **Šišan** by that village's curate. Because the wedding was outside Vodnjan the clerk records where each witness came from, and this is the same formula that labelled «Matt.o de Franceschi **da Dignano**» when he was buried at Rovinj in 1728 — ninety-six years apart, the name written down only from outside the town. He is a **fourth distinct Pietro** — son of a Giovanni, and a weaver like Cristoforo. Also **Bianca Bortolan, second daughter of Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro**, married 14 June 1824 aged 20, fixing that household's dates without a baptism surviving for any of them.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, image 193
rows.what: 1823–1824: a second male line
rows.got: **A second Vodnjan line, three generations deep, unrelated to Giuseppe's.** 19 November 1823, house 684: **Bonetta, «figlia del fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Dom.co e Domenica Manzin q.m Dom.co»**, marries at twenty-three — so born about 1800, her father dead by 1823 and **his** father a **Domenico**. Ninety days later, 28 February 1824, house 764, a **«Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro, agricoltore»** witnesses — a man whose father Pietro is newly dead, and on the dates almost certainly Bonetta's brother. Left open on purpose: whether this Pietro q.m Domenico is also the «q.m Pietro» who fathered Lucia, married out by 1799. A shared forename is not evidence.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 194–195
rows.what: 1824–1825, and a correction
rows.got: **A third daughter, and a misreading put right.** 15 January 1825, house 667: **Lucia, «figlia di Alvise Birattan q.m Saba e di Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro»**, marries at 28 — born about 1797, alongside Maria (b. c.1800) and Bianca (b. c.1804). Three weddings out of one house, none of them indexed anywhere. This entry also writes the husband's surname clearly, and it is **Birattan**, not the **Bortolan** this archive published earlier today off the 1821 hand; the earlier rows have been corrected in place with the change stated. Also **Don Stefano's sixth witness appearance**, 28 October 1824, house 208, again beside Canon Michiel Benedetto.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 196–198
rows.got: **Pietro had a brother.** 25 January 1826, house 224: Michiela, «figlia di **Cristoforo De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria** e di Maria Luigia Manzin q.m Domenico», marries at 26 — the same dead father as the Pietro who remarried in 1818, so **Cristoforo is his brother** and the eldest Vodnjan line now carries two sons. It also means **two men named Cristoforo De Franceschi are alive in the town at once** — this one q.m Gio: Maria, and the weaver di Giuseppe — told apart only by the father's name. And 10 July 1826: **«Ant.o De Franceschi fu Vittorio»** witnesses at a wedding celebrated by the archpriest **at Svetvinčenat** — a Rovinj given-name in the patronymic and a Svetvinčenat venue, recorded as a coincidence of the page and **not** claimed as a link. One miss ruled out by eye on image 196: «Pietro **Francin** q.m Fran.co», not Franceschi.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 199–202
rows.got: **A sister, and the eldest line becomes a family of three.** 7 February 1828, house 366: Michiela Damiana, daughter of the late Domenico Pastrovicchio and **«della vivente Veniera De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria»**, marries at twenty — and the witness is **«Cristoforo De Franceschi fu Gio: M.a, Agricoltore»**, her uncle. So Gio. Maria De Franceschi, dead before 1818, is now shown with **three children — Pietro, Cristoforo and Veniera** — none of whom has a baptism on any film this archive can reach; the register found them by naming their dead father the same way three times across ten years. Also **«Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., Tessitore»** witnessing again on 23 September 1828, in Vodnjan this time and without the «da Dignano», which shows he lived there. And **Don Stefano's seventh and eighth appearances**, 16 February and 23 September 1828. Images 199 and 200 read with no De Franceschi on them.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 203–204
rows.what: Late 1828 into 1829
rows.got: **Cristoforo the weaver, named in full at last** — «Cristoforo De Franceschi **di Giuseppe**, Tessitore», witness 25 November 1828 — which is what safely separates him from the other Cristoforo, *fu Gio: Maria*, the ploughman who witnessed his own niece's wedding ten months earlier. Two men, one name, one town, one volume. **Don Stefano witnesses twice more the same afternoon** (entries 42 and 43, both 25 November 1828), taking him to ten. And the near-miss worth keeping: «Giuseppe figlio del fu **Pietro Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**» — not Franceschi, but the **identical patronymic** to Pietro De Franceschi's first wife «Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel», so this groom is Veniera's nephew and a first cousin of the 1821 bridegroom. Francin is not Franceschi, and in this parish the two families are a household deep in each other. Image 204 read clean.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 205–206
rows.got: **Don Stefano reaches fourteen witness appearances in ten years** — four of them on these two openings alone (23 May, 31 August, 19 and 22 December 1829). The May wedding was held in the **church of San Martino** and he stood beside **Ferdinando Verbits, Maestro delle Scuole Elementari**, the town schoolmaster; the December one carried a dispensation from the three readings of the banns granted by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**. He is never once the officiant: that is always the parroco Giovanni Tromba. **Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., Tessitore** witnesses a third time on 22 February 1830, on a marriage dispensed in the fourth degree of consanguinity by the **Ordinariate of Pola** — which is where Vodnjan's church paperwork ran, and where to write next.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 207–208
rows.what: 1830, and a fifth generation
rows.got: **A widow's second wedding names her grandfather.** 25 June 1830, house 483: **Veniera De Franceschi**, widow of Domenico Pastrovicchio, remarries at forty-nine — and because a widow's remarriage is written out in full, the clerk records her parents: **«Gio. Maria De Franceschi *fu Pietro* e Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo»**. The father who has been a bare name since March 1818 now has a father and a wife of his own, and the Vodnjan line stands **five generations deep** off this one unindexed book, back to a marriage of the 1770s. **Michiela Zambaletta is the first woman named as a mother anywhere in the line.** Don Stefano witnesses twice more, 8 June and 24 November 1830, reaching sixteen.

rows.src: Family photograph collection — the hand-tinted portrait pair
rows.what: Whose face is on the Crikvenica page
rows.got: **The face was wrong, and it was on the direct line's own page.** A hand-tinted portrait of a bearded man in a bow tie had been published here as **Josip Defranceschi, born at Gračišće 22 March 1863** — David's great-grandfather, and the only likeness the direct line had. **David identified it: the photograph is from the Imotski branch**, and the sitter is a Josip of that family. Two branches' pictures sit in one collection; a card carried the name, this line has a man of that name, and this archive matched face to name without asking which Josip. The register plates on that page were checked against Gračišće and Ledenice — **the portrait was never checked against anything.** Withdrawn from the head card and from the 1906 entry in the story, recaptioned in the gallery, and a correction section added to the page where it stood. The companion portrait published as his wife Ana is **also withdrawn**: its only identification was that it matched the man beside it. **No likeness of the Crikvenica Josip is known to this archive.** Note the pattern — the retired 2018 GEDCOM spliced Imotski onto this line too. The same seam has now caught this archive twice, once in a pedigree and once in a photograph.

rows.src: Rovinj, marriages — DGS 005497870, image 211, entry 31
rows.what: Carlo De Franceschi's own marriage, opened at last
rows.got: **The historian was married lying down.** 1 March 1852 at Rovinj: «Il Signor **Carlo De Franceschi q.m Giuseppe e della Sig.ra Lambertina Pesle di Mattia, da Gologorizza di Pisino, Assessore presso quest'I. R. Corte di Giustizia**, celibe d'anni 40» marries «**Maria Michelcich di Luca e di Maria**, celibe d'anni 26» — **«al letto dello Sposo, per essere gravemente ammalato»**, at the bridegroom's bed because he was gravely ill. The banns were **dispensed the same day by the Imperial-Royal District Captaincy, note № 898, *urgente necessitate***, and the witnesses are the **deputy State Prosecutor Zaccaria Maver** and **Dr Barzan, physician** — the law and the medicine, not the family. He did not die; he lived to 1893. The entry also fixes his office in 1852 and names both parents. Two corrections fall out: the register says **d'anni 40** and he was **forty-two** (b. 16 Oct 1809); and this archive's marriage table carried the year as **1812** — it is **1852**, now fixed with the reason stated. On the same film, a burial of «Julius, son of Carlo», born 1853, dead 13 February 1854 — very probably the first child of this marriage.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 209–210
rows.got: **A fifth woman married out, and a fourth trade.** 17 November 1831: «Ant.o Gio., figlio di Fran.co Gorlato q.m Biaggio e della **q.m Luigetta De Franceschi**», marrying at twenty-three — so she was born about 1808's mother's generation and dead by 1831, and she joins Domenica, Antonia Maria, Lucia and Veniera as women of the name recoverable only through a child's wedding. 18 February 1832: **«Giovanni De Franceschi q.m Pietro, Calzolajo»** witnesses — a shoemaker, and on the patronymic very likely a brother of Bonetta and of Pietro the ploughman in the line descending from a Domenico. **Pietro q.m Pietro** also witnesses again, 15 October 1831. Don Stefano reaches **eighteen**. One generation of one surname in one small town now shows a **priest, a ploughman, a weaver and a shoemaker**.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 211–212
rows.got: **A third wife named in the parents' generation.** 17 July 1832, house 325: **Domenico De Franceschi**, forty-six and a widower, «figlio delli furono giugali **Pietro De Franceschi e Martina Civico q.m Domenico**, Vedovo della q.m **Veniera De Rocchi fu Onorato**», marries a widow. Because both parties are widowed the clerk writes every name out, and it yields a couple this archive did not have. **Martina Civico** joins Michiela Zambaletta and Domenica Manzin as the third named wife of that generation. Whether her husband Pietro is the same man as the Pietro q.m Domenico who married Domenica Manzin is left **open** — this parish has produced four Pietros and two Cristoforos, and only a patronymic settles it. Don Stefano witnesses a **nineteenth** time, 16 November 1832.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, image 213
rows.what: Late 1832 into 1833
rows.got: **A second son, and a correction.** 1 December 1832, house 282: «**Domenico figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e della q.m Veniera Francin q.m Domenico**», aged 29 — the same parents as the 1821 bridegroom, so a **younger brother of Gio: Maria**, born about 1803. And on **26 January 1833** the priest's signature reads «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi, De Parochi lic., li congiunse e benedisse nella Chiesa Parrocchiale**» — **he married them himself**, which retires this archive's repeated claim that he was never the officiant. The claim was true of 1819–1832 and was stated as though it covered a book that was still sixty openings from being read. What survives is better: he acts «De Parochi lic.», by the parson's licence, the same formula as the 1816 baptism.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, image 214
rows.what: February 1833
rows.got: **Giuseppe De Franceschi's death bracketed.** The weaver is «Cristoforo De Franceschi ***di*** Giuseppe» in March 1818 and November 1828, and «***fu*** Giuseppe» on 12 February 1833 — so the father of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver **died between November 1828 and February 1833**. Also **Don Stefano officiates a second time**, in the church of the **B. V. del Carmine**, and **Pietro De Franceschi fu Pietro** witnesses a third time. And a reading withdrawn the day after publishing it: «**De Par. lic.**» is the register's **standard formula for any deputising priest** — the next entry uses it of Don Pietro Bradamante — not the personal arrangement this archive took it for. Vodnjan is running marriages through at least four churches: the parish church, San Martino, the B. V. del Carmine and the B. V. della Trovesa.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Copulatorum — DGS 005497894, images 215–216
rows.what: 1833: the brothers' own household
rows.got: **The household of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver opens.** 27 July 1833, house 324: «**Maria Francesca, figlia del fu Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro e di Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo**», marrying at twenty-eight. That gives Giuseppe **a father (Pietro)**, **a wife (Lucia Tromba)** and **a fourth child** — and confirms his death inside the bracket his sons' patronymics had already set, after November 1828 and before February 1833. **The mother is a Tromba**: the surname of **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D., the parroco who signs every page** and who licensed her son Don Stefano to baptise in 1816 and to marry couples in 1833. One of the two witnesses is Andrea Tromba, Possidente Civile. A ploughman's and a weaver's family produced a priest of the chapter, and their mother came from the family that held the parish. *(the kinship is inf, on a shared surname in a small town)*

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum 1815–1833 — DGS 005497894, images ~471–575
rows.what: Opening the death register
rows.got: **The third book on the film, and it is not indexed either.** Deaths 1815–1833 run from about image 471 to 575 — thirteen entries a page, six images to the year, in a Latin ruling with a cause-of-death column. A query for De Franceschi deaths 1826–1836 across the whole of Croatia returns **eight dated records and none from this parish**. First entry read: **11 March 1829, house 325, «Maria, figlia di Stefano De Franceschi e di Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio»** — a child of one of the eight households reconstructed from the baptism index, which now has a burial and a house number. Images 546–548 read; the target is **Giuseppe De Franceschi**, bracketed by his sons' patronymics to between November 1828 and February 1833.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 546–550
rows.what: 1829, and two households given their dead
rows.got: **Two of the eight reconstructed households now have a burial, a house number and — in one case — a generation above them.** 11 March 1829, house 325: «Maria, figlia di **Stefano De Franceschi e di Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio**». 23 July 1829, house 48: «Pietro, figlio di **Dom.co De Franceschi *q.m Pietro* e di Zacchera Cerlon di Franc.o**» — which names Domenico's own dead father, a **Pietro**, where the baptism index had only a bare pair of names. Also caught and fixed: the reader's crops were being **clipped to the viewport, losing the bottom fifth of every page**, silently. Images scanned before the fix are being re-scanned.

rows.src: FamilySearch — both the persona API and the Deep Zoom image service
rows.what: Automated reading, stopped
rows.got:
**403 — «This request was blocked by our security service.»** After two days of reading register images tile by tile, FamilySearch's bot protection has blocked this session: the persona search endpoint and the `deepzoomcloud` image service both now return a 403 with a NOINDEX/NOFOLLOW block page rather than data.

**No attempt has been made or will be made to get around it.** This archive does not bypass bot checks or CAPTCHAs, and a block is a legitimate answer from a service that has given it a very great deal already — five generations at Vodnjan came off these films in two days.

**What this stops, for now:** the rest of the Vodnjan marriage register (images 217–470), the death registers (546–575 on film 894 and all of 895), the Vodnjan baptism re-read, Svetvinčenat's marriage register, and the Rijeka and Bakar films. Those six items are paused, not abandoned.

**What it does not stop:** everything already read and published, and the work that does not touch FamilySearch — the itineraries, the portraits, the archive letters, and the reconciliation of David's own GEDCOM when it arrives.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 553–557
rows.what: Giuseppe De Franceschi, found
rows.got: **The bracket closes exactly.** This archive had no date for Giuseppe De Franceschi — only a range derived from how his sons were written, «*di* Giuseppe» in November 1828 and «*fu* Giuseppe» in February 1833. The death register gives **14 February 1830**: «**Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro era ammogliato con Lucia Tromba fu Cristoforo**», **house 324**, **aged 72** — so born about **1758** — of an **organic defect of the chest**, and, in the sacraments column, «**senza assistenza spirituale per morte improvvisa**»: **suddenly, with no priest**. His own son was a priest of that parish. **And five months later, 13 July 1830, house 501: «Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro era Moglie di Alviso Birattan q.m Sabà», aged 70**, of dropsy — the woman whose three daughters married out in 1821, 1824 and 1825. **Both «q.m Pietro», born about 1758 and 1760, dead five months apart**: almost certainly brother and sister, which joins the two households and puts a Pietro born around 1730 behind both.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 558–559
rows.what: House 325 gets its family
rows.got: **11 September 1830, house 325: «Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio, Moglie di Stefano De Franceschi *di* Domenico *q.m* Pietro»**, aged 57 — born about 1773 — of pulmonary consumption, eighteen months after her daughter died in the same house. The two different words matter: ***di*** Domenico means **his father was alive**; ***q.m*** Pietro means his grandfather was not. A third Vodnjan line stands — **Pietro → Domenico → Stefano** — and it gives that household three generations where the baptism index gave none. It also makes **house 325 theirs**, which sharpens the question raised two days ago: the same number stands against Domenico De Franceschi, 46, son of a Pietro and Martina Civico, remarrying there in 1832. The connection is now **likely**; which connection it is stays **open**, because on the stated ages that Domenico is too young to be Stefano's father.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, images 560–575
rows.what: Deaths, late 1830 – Feb 1833
rows.got: **The tile server refused.** `image.xml` still answered 200, but every image tile came back **403** from the Incapsula security service, at every zoom level, on the first request of the session — no CAPTCHA offered, no rate warning, nothing to wait out. **No attempt was made to get round it.** The reading stops here until the block lifts. The targets it was going to answer — **Luigetta De Franceschi**, dead by November 1831; **Martina Civico** and **Veniera De Rocchi**, both dead by 1832 — stay open on What we cannot close.

rows.src: The Register — 1,508 harvested FamilySearch personas
rows.what: Vodnjan households, mined from the catch instead of the film
rows.got:
With the film shut, the **1,508-row catch harvested the day before** was read for parent-pairs instead. It gave **four households the archive did not have** — *Sebastiano Giachin × Domenica De Franceschi* (1817–1832), *Giuseppe Forlani × Lucia Michiela De Franceschi* (1848–1857), *Stefano De Franceschi × Maria Forlanichio* (1858–1860) and *Domenico De Franceschi × Mattea Delcarro* (1858–1865) — plus **two children** for households already standing: **Teresa Domenica**, 1820, to Pietro and Maria Malusà, and **Lucia**, 25 July 1826, to Gio Maria and Lucia Bonassin.

It also gave a **warning about itself**. A ninth apparent household, *Giovanni Moscarda × Maria Defranceschi*, dissolved on inspection: **Antonio 1835 and Antonio 1836, Stefano 1844 and Stefano 1844, Epifanio and Giovanni Epifano both June 1849** are the same children indexed twice, in Latin and in Italian. Nothing was added from it. That is the Register's own caveat — *an entry is not a person* — proving itself within a day of being published.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 560
rows.what: December 1830 – January 1831
rows.got:
**Entry 151, 15 December 1830, house 456.** «Pietro figlio di Pietro De Franceschi **q.m Pietro** e di Maddalena Francin **di Giovanni** giugali», aged **11**, of **scarlatina**, and in the sacraments column «**senza assistenza spirituale per la malattia repentina**».

He is a **new eldest child** for a household this archive already had — three years older than its earliest baptism — so **that marriage was made by 1818**, not 1822. His father's father was dead by 1830; his mother's father was alive. The house is **456**, a third Vodnjan house number after 324 and 325.

**Entry 4, 6 January 1831, house 24.** «Domenica figlia di Andrea Palin q.m Pio. e **della fu Michiela De Franceschi fu Pietro** giugali» — a **sixth** woman who left the surname, dead before 1831, recoverable only because her daughter died young enough to need her named.

**Two rejected.** Entry 157 reads «Nicolò Sussani **q.m Francesco**» and entry 16 «Antonia Palin **di Francesco**». Both are patronymics. At low zoom both looked like the surname; neither is.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 560, entries 149–155
rows.what: Scarlatina, December 1830
rows.got: Five of seven consecutive entries — **150, 151, 152, 153, 155** — give the cause as «**Scarlatina**», and the dead are aged **7, 11, 6, 6** and a child. **Scarlet fever went through Vodnjan in December 1830**, and the eleven-year-old Pietro De Franceschi died in it. The register writes the age as «d'an. 11» in a column headed *Aetas*; the two entries on either side of him are other people's children of six and seven.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 561
rows.what: A slip of paper left in the book
rows.got:
Image 561 is a **re-shoot of the same opening as 560**, with a loose slip laid across the left page — so the December 1830 entries are hidden and the slip is filmed instead.

**Recto:** «**Cercare ne' libri de' morti — Maria Celin fu moglie del fu Marco Silla, morto da anni 25, 26 c.a**» — someone's instruction to *search the books of the dead*.

**Verso, upside down:** a draft entry — «**165 · Dom.ca Gasparro fu Dom.co e Cat.a Baldarin № 505, morta li 23 ottobre 1843, da male di petto**», then two names, «**Giorgio Cossich e Fran.co Maravo**».

Neither side concerns this family. It is kept because of what it is: **parish office scrap from 1843, lying in an 1831 opening, photographed because nobody moved it** — and on one side of it, somebody else's unfinished search.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 562
rows.what: February 1831, first half
rows.got: Twelve entries, 1–11 February 1831, read in full: Portolato, Manzin, Toffetti, Vidich, Rotta, Muscovich, Del Carro, Ciritico, Cattarin, Gasparo Toffetti. **No De Franceschi.** The second half of the page was not reached — the security service blocked the film mid-page.

rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 562 onward
rows.what: February 1831 onward
rows.got: **Blocked mid-page.** After roughly four hundred tile requests the Incapsula service began returning **403 on `image.xml` itself**, which had answered 200 all session. The reading stopped there. No pacing was tried, no route was looked for, no request was repeated. The film is open at **image 562, second half**, and that is where it resumes.

rows.src: The Register — 1,508 harvested FamilySearch personas
rows.what: Every household in the catch, not just Vodnjan's
rows.got:
With the film blocked, the whole catch was mined for parent-pairs rather than only its Istrian rows. It gave **48 households the archive did not have**, holding **151 children** — among them *Veneranda Defranceschi × Antonius Subiotto* (eight children, 1858–1874), *Pascha Defranceschi × Angelus Ferrarese* (seven, 1849–1864), *Francesco Franceschi × Maria De Caralipeo* at **Almissa in Dalmatia** (seven, 1856–1873), and *Josephi Defranceschi × Mariæ Defranceschi* at **Ližnjan** (five, 1872–1888).

Every one is filed **`index`, not `read`** — the pattern is real, the spellings are the indexer's, and no page has been seen. **34 are in Istria, 11 in Dalmatia, 10 in the Kvarner and 43 could not be placed at all.**

**Three pairs are flagged as possibly one household each** — *Bellinich* twice, *Zanghirella* twice, *Lazar* twice — where the surnames match once the spellings are set aside and the years all but touch. They are **kept apart**, because merging two households on a surname is how one family becomes a fiction.

The merge itself had to be built twice. The first pass counted **100** pairs, most of them Latin genitives of each other — *Valentini* and *Valentino*, *Ursulæ* and *Orsola*, *Josephi* and *Giuseppe* — and *Francetich* rows that are not this family at all. Normalising the genitives, collapsing doubled letters and requiring a **De Franceschi** parent brought it to 48.

rows.src: Family testimony — David Defranceski
rows.what: 1948: an attempt to leave the country
rows.got:
Asked what «went» meant, David answered: **«They went to leave the country in 1948.»**

That converts a contradiction into a **window**. Their son was born at Senj on **17 December 1951**, so they were back on the coast by about **March 1951**; Ivan died at Senj in 1995. **They left in 1948, were home inside about two and a half years, and never got out** — Hedviga reached Johannesburg only much later, and Ivan never did.

The route is not a mystery either. The family already had a household in **Pfullingen, in the French occupation zone**: Ivan had worked at Reutlingen from 21 October 1941, his father was on the 1947 Pfullingen list of foreigners, and his brothers **Zdravko and Anton** went out to Australia from there in **1949** — Anton's card stamped «Emigré Australie le 8.3.49». **Ivan and Hedviga were a year behind them at a door that was closing**, the IRO shutting its books at the end of February 1952.

**A failed exit leaves no Yugoslav paper.** The Arolsen request has been rewritten accordingly and is now the highest-value errand this project holds.

rows.src: MyHeritage tree 4, person panels — 101 individuals
rows.what: The people known only from the tree
rows.got:
All **101** people this archive held as a name and nothing else were pulled from the tree, one panel at a time, from David's own logged-in session. **No errors, and one flat result: the tree has no years for them either.** Exactly **one** of the hundred and one carries a date range, and it is not a date this archive accepts — see below.

What the tree did give was **place**. **48 of them are now placed**, and the places are the deep end of the story: **Mione in the Val Degano eight times**, **Paluzza five**, **Naunina**, **Pasian di Prato** — Carnia, where the surname is supposed to come from. Then a Trentino cluster the archive barely knew it had — **Fiera di Primiero, Telve, Strigno, Grigno, Sacco** — and Istrian parishes at **Kaštelir (five), Poreč, Pula, Pomer, Plomin, Pazin, Gologorica, Ližnjan**. Two are in **South America**: San Lorenzo in Santa Fe, and Colonia in Uruguay.

**15 people are now filed to Carnia, 8 to Trentino, 2 abroad** — lines they could not be given while they had no place. Roster people with no place at all: **209 → 161**. Parishes known to this archive: **31 → 54**.

rows.src: MyHeritage tree 4
rows.what: Piero della Francesca is in the family tree
rows.got:
The one dated person among the hundred and one is «**Piero di Benedetto «Piero della Francesca» Defranceschi, 1415–1492, Sansepolcro**» — the painter — together with his father **Benedetto Defranceschi** and his mother **Romana di Perino**.

The surname is not the error. Piero's father genuinely was a *de' Franceschi* of Sansepolcro; that much is ordinary art history. **The error, if it is one, is the join** — nothing whatever connects a Tuscan tanner's family to the Carnian and Istrian Defranceschi except the word itself.

All three are kept in the roster, marked **notable**, filed under *other*, and each carries the same sentence: *the connection to this family is not accepted*. **A Tuscan graft on a Friulian surname is exactly the kind of join this archive exists to catch** — and it is the third time this project has had to say so, after Francesco de' Franceschi the Venetian printer and Francesco de' Franceschi the painter.

rows.src: Arolsen Archives online collections
rows.what: Ivan Defranceski, Hedviga Blažević, Uršula Kovačina, Anton Rudolf — 1948–1951
rows.got:
**Not attempted: the service is down.** `collections.arolsen-archives.org` resolves to 62.90.197.110 and **times out**, while the main Arolsen site answers normally — so the online archive, not the organisation, is unavailable. David confirms it is dead from his side too, so it is not a block on this machine.

**It stays on the list.** The four searches are *Defranceski*, *Defranceschi*, *Blazevic Hedviga*, *Kovacina Ursula*, and the window that matters is **1948–1951** — the only place the failed exit can have left a trace, since a departure that was reversed leaves nothing in any Croatian register. A record of **Anton Rudolf after 1943** would separately settle whether Uršula was a widow or a wife when the man called **Car** appears.

The written enquiry to Bad Arolsen is drafted and waiting, and is deliberately **not** being sent first: their own advice is to search the online archive before joining a queue they warn may run to thirteen months.

rows.src: FamilySearch full-text search — untested
rows.what: Whether the Croatian church books are machine-readable yet
rows.got:
**A maybe, recorded so it is not lost.** FamilySearch has been extending an AI handwriting-recognition search that makes the **text inside register images** searchable rather than only the catalogue around them. **Whether the Croatian church books are in it is not known** — it has not been tested, and FamilySearch is refusing this session at the time of writing.

It matters more than anything else on the list. Reading Vodnjan's death register 1815–1833 by eye is about **105 images and four and a half thousand entries**; if the text is already searchable, that work is a query instead of a campaign. **Test this before committing to any exhaustive read**, because a positive answer makes the plan obsolete and a negative one costs a single request.

If it is not available: the fallback is **handwritten-text recognition trained on this clerk's hand** — twenty pages transcribed by hand to train on, then the rest by machine. That costs money and setup and is **David's decision, not this archive's**.

rows.src: Archives de Corse — archives.isula.corsica
rows.what: Whether the Corsican records can be searched by surname
rows.got:
**They cannot, and finding that out is the result.** The Archives of the Collectivité de Corse are free, need no account and are **not FamilySearch** — the platform refuses a command-line client but opens normally in a browser.

**No module has a surname field.** *État civil*, *Corsica christiana*, *Recensements*, *Registres matricules* all take the same three criteria — **commune, date range, record type** — and the platform says outright that anything else is *une recherche non indexée*.

So Corsica is images to be read, like Vodnjan. **But the record types include TABLE DÉCENNALE** — the alphabetical ten-yearly index French civil registration compiled for every commune, 1793–1902. That is roughly **eleven index pages per commune** instead of ten years of acts, and it is why Corsica can be finished when Vodnjan cannot: an Austrian *Liber Defunctorum* was never indexed by anybody.

Six Cap Corse communes are on the platform and all are in scope: **Tomino, Rogliano, Ersa, Centuri, Morsiglia, Barrettali**. Available types: *naissances, mariages, décès, baptêmes, sépultures, publications de mariage, table décennale*.

rows.src: ANNO — *Il Giornaletto di Pola*, the whole run
rows.what: Every issue carrying any spelling of the name, read in full text
rows.got:
**One hundred and sixty-four issues, read end to end. Four people, and a large negative.**

· **Alessandro Defranceschi** — enrolled in the levy at Pola, **18 June 1914**, one of fifty-two taken from three hundred and eighteen. Born about 1893. Not previously in this archive.
· **Luigi Defranceschi** — two crowns to the **Red Cross**, 3 September 1914, in a list a police inspector collected door to door.
· **Angelina Defranceschi** — **married at Pola, 21 November 1914**, in a notice the couple paid to place. The groom's surname will not come off the OCR.
· **Angelo Defranceschi, 63, «da Fasana»** — at no. 6 via del Prato, 25 November 1914. Supplies the village of origin missing from the archive's record of an Angelo born 1851.

**And the negative, which is the size of the thing: one hundred and fifty-eight of the one hundred and sixty-four issues are the street name and nothing else** — *via Carlo Defranceschi*, in rental advertisements. Filtering the street out is most of the work; the OCR renders *via* as *vla*, *wvia*, *ia* and *tia*, and breaks the street name across columns.

Two further mentions give no forename: a subscription line of 2 September 1914, and **«il debito Defranceschi»** of two thousand crowns in a fraudulent-bankruptcy trial reported 13 January 1915.

The name stopping in March 1915 **was tested before it was written about** and is an artefact: ANNO's run is complete for 1914, patchy to March 1915, and then absent. [The page](/giornaletto/).

rows.src: The Wayback Machine — everything under sites.google.com/defranceski.com
rows.what: Every archived URL on the family's own Google Site, before it is switched off
rows.got:
**Checked, found nearly empty, and filled.** A CDX query for every URL under that host returned **two** successful captures: the site root of **1 January 2022** and the home page of **11 July 2025**. Family Trees, The People, The Places, The Map, The Name, The Coat of Arms, Publications, Resources and About were archived **nowhere on the public net** — Google Sites builds its navigation in script, so the crawler never followed it below the front page.

The same fact made the page list uncrawlable, so it was read out of the page source instead: **twelve live addresses, not the nine of this archive's own reckoning table**, which had folded the two sub-pages under *The Story* into their parent.

**All twelve were submitted to Save Page Now on 14 September 2026 and all twelve captured**, every job reporting success, verified by fetching the snapshots back — *The People* returns at 413 KB, byte for byte the live page. Two drew **429** on the first pass and were taken on a later one.

Two things learned in the doing. **Save Page Now no longer accepts anonymous requests**: a POST without a session returns *401 «You need to be logged in to use Save Page Now»*. And a Wayback capture of a Google Sites page keeps the **frame** around an embedded My Map, not the map — which is why the KML export of 8 September 2026 is the only thing standing between those pins and the account being closed.
ev: defranceski.com — the reckoning, and the twelve permanent addresses

rows.src: FamilySearch image waypoints — every Istrian and Kvarner volume, addressed
rows.what: The waypoint tree of Croatia Church Books 2040054, walked to the level of the individual volume
rows.got:
**Three hundred and nine register volumes now have their own address, and every one of them was tested.** The archive had listed 263 Istrian volumes and 46 Kvarner ones as plain text since the day it walked the waypoints; there was no way to open a single one of them.

The tree is collection → **9RKB-7M9:391644801** (Roman Catholic) → parish → volume, and one call returns all **1,000** Croatian parishes. A volume's waypoint yields the arks of its images, and `familysearch.org/ark:/61903/<first ark>?cc=2040054&wc=<waypoint>` opens the viewer at page one of that book. **263 of 263 Istrian volumes and 46 of 46 Kvarner volumes returned a link; nothing failed.** 307 calls at 2.2-second spacing drew no rate limiting at all, against the 25–40 per burst this archive had recorded.

**The Kvarner links this page already carried were dead.** They used FamilySearch's «owc» browse form, which now answers «Something Went Wrong» for every waypoint tried. Nine broken links, replaced by 46 working ones.

**And joining the inventory to the film produced a finding.** Of the 1,151 books the Pazin inventory catalogues: 142 are on film; 495 are in parishes with no film at all; 449 are twentieth-century civil registration the church film never covered; and **26 are old parish books in parishes that were filmed, which the filming skipped** — eighteen of them still on a shelf in the village. Barban's births from **1629** and Ližnjan's marriages from **1680** are on that list.
ev: Parish Books — 309 volumes, each one openable
The Archive — and the 26 books the film skipped

rows.src: FamilySearch image waypoints — Dalmatia and Carnia, every volume addressed
rows.what: The Croatian collection walked for sixty Dalmatian parishes, and the Udine collection for twenty-six Carnian comuni
rows.got:
**Nine hundred and eighty-five more volumes now open at page one, and nothing failed.**

**Dalmatia — 343 volumes across 60 parishes**, the Omiš, Split, Trogir–Seget, Imotski, Zadar and Dubrovnik groups with the ring each married into. Earliest volume **1569**. Same collection as Istria (2040054), same method.

**Carnia is a different country and took a different route.** It is not in the Croatian collection, and the collections API **silently ignores its own text filter** — a search for «Udine» returns Alabama — so all **3,483** FamilySearch collections had to be paged to find it. There is exactly one: **«Italy, Udine, Civil Registration (State Archive), 1806-1815, 1871-1911»**, collection 1939238, 1.26 million images. **This archive had been describing it as 1806–1815 only**; the 1871–1911 half has never been looked at.

**642 volumes across 26 Carnian comuni** are now linked. Sutrio has 64, Prato 62, Paluzza 56.

**And Ovaro is not in it.** The province lists 627 comuni and Ovaro is not one of them — nor Mione, Muina, Ovasta, Luint, Liariis, Chialina, Agrons or Cludinico. **But Colza is**, a frazione of Ovaro, holding a complete Napoleonic set for 1806–1812: births, deaths, marriages, banns and indexes, **25 volumes**. Whether Mione and Muina are written inside them is a question the images can answer and the index cannot — the record API's place filter is ignored too. The volumes are linked; it is a few minutes' reading and it has not been done.

**Comeglians, the Gorto canton seat, carries the marriage *allegati* for 1807–1815** — the documents behind this archive's Giovanni Battista de' Franceschi «already dead by 1789».

**A warning with it.** The Udine collection indexes 2,201 people called Franceschi. Of the first eleven hundred, **the Carnian communes account for five**. The rest are lowland Friulian families — Lauzzana and Colloredo (209), Udine (129), Muzzana del Turgnano (114), Bertiolo (101). Most Franceschi in the Udine registers are not this family and are not from the mountains.
ev: Parish Books — Dalmatia and Carnia, every volume openable
The Atlas — the volumes hang off the places

rows.src: Findmypast — the record sets nobody had opened, swept before the trial ends
rows.what: All 38 record sets the surname touches, paged out in full under three spellings
rows.got:
**Findmypast was worked hard on 9 September and it was not finished.** That day took Travel & Migration, the US censuses and the naturalisation files. **The death, probate, obituary and parish sets had never been opened.**

**Two probate files at Horsham, Victoria, both with their Public Record Office references.**
· **Zdravko «Zdrovko» De Franceski** — died **22 December 1979**, probate granted **19 June 1980**, file **874/188**, **VPRS 28/P10 unit 148**. Occupation **labourer**, residence **Horsham**. The headstone already said the date; this adds his trade and a file that can be ordered.
· **Ruža «Rosa» Defranceski** — died **30 January 1996**, probate granted **6 May 1996**, file **1113076**, **VPRS 28/P26 unit 155**. Occupation **home duties**, residence **Horsham**, buried **Horsham Cemetery**. The stone gave her only as «beloved husband of Rosa». **She outlived him by sixteen years.**

**Twenty obituary notices and twenty-two Social Security death records** give death dates for people this archive had only birth years for — **Duilio 1921–2003** (son of Luigi De Franceschi and Libera Chimčić), **Basilio 1909–1994**, **Tobias 1911–1972**, and Connecticut deaths at **Torrington** and Waterbury.

**Two clusters that were invisible from the passenger lists.** The 1910 census puts a household of six in **Tennessee** — Antonio 1875, Bertha 1882, Pietro 1904, Alberts 1905, Aurora 1907, Alba 1908. The 1930 census puts six more in **Michigan**.

**British Armed Forces banns and marriages, 1946: one at Trieste, one at Venice** — British service marriages in occupied Italy, a seam this archive has never touched.

**New York Roman Catholic parish marriages name the parishes**: Our Lady of Pompei, Transfiguration, St Anthony of Padua, St Joseph Sixth Avenue, Ascension — which places the New York family street by street.

**And a negative worth the time it saves: «defranceschi» and «de franceschi» are the same corpus.** Findmypast folds the space, returning 548 and 612 for the same records. **The fused «Defranceski» is the one that behaves differently** — 36 results, and they are almost all this family.

rows.src: Findmypast — «de Franceschi» in the 1920 United States census
rows.what: Why one census returns forty entries the other censuses do not
rows.got:
**There is a Puerto Rican De Franceschi population, and it is large.** Forty of the forty-two Puerto Rico hits in the whole Findmypast corpus sit in the **1920 census**: **Isabela (11), San Lorenzo (9), Ponce (7), San Juan (3), Yauco (3)**, and singles at Peñuelas, San Sebastián, Lajas, Guayama, Luquillo and Ceiba. The forenames are Spanish throughout — Carmen, Aurora, Mercedes, Dominga, Concepción, Ramona, Filomena, Josefa.

**This is not the Istrian family and should never be folded into it.** It is recorded here for the same reason the archive records the Tyrolean and the Corsican groups: so that a future search which turns up forty De Franceschi in Puerto Rico knows immediately that they have been seen, weighed and set aside.

One of them does reach this archive's own list: **Maria, born 1888, died 1983 at San Juan** — already a pin on the Atlas from the geocoding pass, and now dated.
ev: Namesakes — other families of the name

rows.src: David's Google My Map — imported whole from the KML
rows.what: Every layer, pin, note, link, line and shaded area, before the map is switched off
rows.got:
**A My Map dies with the account and no crawler saves one.** The earlier JSON export kept the pins; the KML keeps everything. Imported: **10 layers, 1,289 pins, 56 lines, 10 polygons, 111 notes and 188 links.**

**The 56 lines are named movements David drew by hand** — *«Ivan moves to Senj»*, *«Tomasso travels to Omis»*, *«Bakar to Gologorica»*, *«Frank and Ruza Move to Horsham»*. They are now the arrows on the Atlas, drawn dashed and labelled as his, because motion on a map is persuasive in a way that evidence is not.

**The 10 polygons are the hot-spots he shaded** — Udine, Venezia, Austrian, three in France, and three «De Franceschi Hot Spot» areas in Istria and the Veneto. They are a toggleable overlay.

**And 129 of the map's own FamilySearch links are already dead**, because they use the «owc» browse form that now answers «Something Went Wrong». The map was decaying before it was switched off.
