rows.src: Findmypast — the transcripts, read before the trial lapsed
rows.what: The documents behind the death, marriage, parish and passport index rows
rows.got:
**Two war brides, married in the year the Allies held both cities.**
· **Daphne De Franceschi married Leslie Wain at Trieste**, 1946 — GRO Army Marriages, page 3654, line 102.
· **Placida V De Franceschi married Reginald Onions at Venice**, 1946 — page 2865, line 103.
They are consecutive lines in the same register. Two women of this name marrying British servicemen in occupied Italy, and **this archive had no idea either existed.**

**Two United States passport applications**, which are the documents that prove a man went back:
· **Giovanni De Franceschi, born 1876 in Italy — applied in Connecticut in 1922**, certificate 109256, NARA M1490 roll 1807. Connecticut is **Torrington**, where this archive already stands twelve people.
· **Louis De Franceschi, born 1873 in Italy — applied 1919**, certificate 148535, roll 1008.

**And a Neapolitan family of the name.** *Ignazio Luigi Nicola De Franceschi*, baptised **25 April 1842 at San Marco di Palazzo, Napoli**, son of **Carmine de Franceschi and Angiola Conti**. Logged, not absorbed.

**Blocked, and worth writing down:** the **New York Roman Catholic parish registers** — baptisms and marriages at Our Lady of Pompei, Transfiguration, St Anthony of Padua, Ascension and St Joseph Sixth Avenue — sit behind a higher subscription tier than the trial carries. Seven records, named and located, that could not be opened.

rows.src: The Register's own lead pile, classified
rows.what: Whether 1,153 «leads» are really 1,153 leads
rows.got:
**Nearly half of them are another family.** Sorting the 1,153 lead rows by whether the spelling is this surname at all:

· **498 — Francetich, Franchini, Franceschini, Franceskini.** The archive's rule has always excluded these. **Nobody had counted how much of the lead pile they were.**
· **429 — indexed under the father's surname only.** Real, and the way into the early parish books, but not searchable by name.
· **104 — this surname, plainly.** · **122 — unclear, and each needs an eye.**

**One hundred and forty-five rows carry both the parents and the parish**, which is everything needed to open a book. That is the worklist, and it is now published parish by parish with the number of volumes this archive can already open for each.

**Forty-five of the hundred and forty-five are at Vodnjan, which has no film at all.** Those forty-five are a letter to Pazin, not an afternoon at a screen — which is exactly the distinction the number 1,153 was hiding.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Carnia side
rows.what: The surname across the whole Italian state-archive portal, and then the Carnian communes
rows.got:
**It is open again, and Carnia is in it.** This archive's note said Antenati 403s both browsers; on 14 September the portal answered normally. The search is at `/search-nominative/` and the parameter is **`cognome`**, not `q` — which is why earlier attempts looked like a block and were not one.

**418 results for «de franceschi»**, spread across five spellings: De Franceschi (393), De' Franceschi (7), Dè Franceschi (6), De Franceschi Roncadin (2), Dé Franceschi (2). The heaviest places are **Roma (63), Brescia (59), Dosolo (45), San Ferdinando (26), Genova (21)** — and thirty-nine more localities behind them.

**The very first result is Carnian**: *Maria De Franceschi, born **Paluzza, 1865**, married Gio Batta Della Pietra, daughter of **Costantino De Franceschi and Giovanna Lazzara*** — a marriage record with both parents named. Paluzza is eighteen kilometres from Mione.

**Then the bot protection closed.** An XHR fetch to the same endpoint returned 403 and the navigations that followed returned «403 Forbidden». **No attempt was made to get round it.** The portal is worth a patient second visit: the Carnian communes David named — Tolmezzo, Enemonzo, Socchieve, Ampezzo — were never reached.

rows.src: Matricula Online — the Senj and Karlobag side
rows.what: Whether it holds Croatian parish registers at all
rows.got:
**Matricula does not hold Croatia.** Its fonds are Germany 9,123 · Austria 2,857 · Slovenia 723 · Switzerland 292 · Luxembourg 277 · **Italy 106** · Poland 5 · Serbia 5 · Bosnia 2. There is no Croatian section, so **Senj and Karlobag are not there and cannot be**.

**Nor is Carnia.** Italy on Matricula is **Bozen-Brixen only** — South Tyrol. Friuli, Udine and the Val Degano are absent.

**And it cannot be searched by name at all.** The search page is headed *«Search for Places»* and its fields are `place`, `diocese` and `date_filter`. There is no surname index. Matricula is a shelf you browse, not an index you query — which is worth knowing before anyone spends an evening trying.

**One thing it does have.** The Koper diocese carries 198 parishes including the whole Vipava valley — **Ajdovščina, Vipava, Podnanos, Col, Budanje, Vrhpolje and Šturje itself**. Šturje is the parish of the *Johann Defranceski* this archive found acting as court-appointed *curator ad actum* at Laibach between 1865 and 1875, and whose village it had never placed in a register. **That is a door, and it is open.**

rows.src: Trove — the zones and the spelling the first pass missed
rows.what: Books & Libraries, and the surname written with a space
rows.got:
**The first Trove pass ran newspapers only, and only the fused spellings.** It reported «Defranceski» 2 and «Defranceschi» 13. This archive's own variant rule — that each spelling returns a different, non-overlapping set — was never applied to Trove.

**«De Franceschi» with a space returns 82 newspaper articles.** Six times the fused count. The samples are twentieth-century Canberra: *«Carol De Franceschi, 19, of Flynn»* in the Canberra Times of 7 July 1981, and a fatal accident report of 22 June 1977 naming a sister at Willyamba Place, Flynn. **An ACT family of the name, which this archive had not seen.**

**Books & Libraries — a zone never opened — returns 19.** It does not find new relatives; it hardens two namesakes the archive already carries on assertion:

· **Carlo Prospero Defranceschi** is confirmed as **Salieri's librettist** from two independent catalogue authorities. *«Cäsar auf Pharmacusa»* (Theater an der Wien, 3 editions 1801–1808) — *«Libretto by Carlo Defranceschi — New Grove»*; and *«Angiolina, oder Die Heyrath durchs Getöse»* (4 editions 1803–1807) — *«la poesia è del Sig. Carlo Defranceschi»*, per the **U.S. RISM Libretto Project** and *Stieger, Opernlexikon*.
· **Jean Defranceschi**, *«La Corse française: 30 novembre 1789 – 15 juin 1794»* (1980) — the Corsican historian the archive lists, now with a book and a date.

**A note on the tool.** Trove's interface now loads each zone only on a click and throttles under repeated queries; its API needs a key this project does not hold. The remaining zones — Diaries, Images, Magazines, People & Organisations — were not completed and are left open.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the registers, not the name index
rows.what: Whether the Carnian civil registers are online anywhere at all
rows.got:
**Mione has fifty-nine registers of its own, digitised, free, and open — and this archive has been saying for months that they were not online.**

The name search was the wrong door. Antenati says so itself: *«Non tutti i nomi sono ricercabili perché solo una parte dei registri disponibili è stata completamente indicizzata»* — only part of the holding is name-indexed, and Tolmezzo returns **nothing** by surname. The other form, **`/search-registry/`**, browses the registers themselves.

**Ovaro: 271 registers**, all held by the **Archivio di Stato di Udine**, in two fonds — *Stato civile napoleonico* (173) and *Stato civile italiano, Comuni afferenti al Tribunale di Tolmezzo* (98). The series break down by village:

· **Mione (oggi frazione di Ovaro) — 59 registers**
· Ovaro itself — 144 · Lenzone — 9 · Chialina — 8 · Cludinico — 8 · and nine more series behind them

By type: **Morti 61, Matrimoni 49, Nati 39, Matrimoni pubblicazioni ed opposizioni 31, Matrimoni allegati 28**, and eighteen more. By year they run from **1806** through **1871** and beyond — so both the Napoleonic registration and the Italian civil registration after unification.

Each result carries its own shelfmark and a *«Vedi il registro»* link — for example *Registro 1806, Nati, segnatura 12995, Agrons con Cella*; *1806, Matrimoni allegati, segnatura 185, Lenzone*.

**Tolmezzo has 452 registers on the same portal**, and the other Carnian communes are there too.

**This is the same material FamilySearch holds and keeps behind «Image Restricted».** The Italian state archive has published it itself, and published it open.

rows.src: Antenati — the Ovaro marriage allegati, opened one by one
rows.what: The twenty-eight allegati files, starting with the two for Mione and the one for Muina
rows.got:
**The Mione allegati had already been read, and the page that says so is this archive's own.**

**Mione 1806** (segnatura 185, six images) is a single marriage file: **Ignazio di Prato of Chialina × Giacoma de' Franceschi of Mione**, September 1806. It holds the groom's Latin baptism of **13 December 1777** — *Ignatius, son of Iacobus son of the late Leonardus de Prato* — the bride's parish certificate of **25 May 1789**, and the consent of the groom's mother **Catterina, widow of the late Gio: Giacomo di Prato**, who could not attend the signing. **Every one of those facts is already on the Carnia page.**

**Mione 1808** (segnatura 12984) is catalogued as *Matrimoni, allegati* and **is not a marriage file at all**. It is one image: a covering letter of **17 February 1809** from the Municipalità of Mione to the Civil Tribunal of First Instance at Udine, transmitting the previous year's registers. **No names of this family, and no marriage.**

**Muina 1806** (segnatura 185, ten images) is the one still worth opening. Only its cover sheet was reached: Antenati's session then returned **«400 Bad Request — size of a request header field exceeds server limit»**, which is the cookie growing across a long sitting rather than a block. It clears with a fresh session.

**And a correction made before it was published.** On the first pass this reader transcribed the Mione 1806 certificate as *«Giovanna, daughter of Giacomo q. Gio: Batta, born 1785»*. **All three were wrong.** Zoomed properly it reads ***Giacoma**, daughter of **Osvaldo** q. Gio: Batta, born **1789***. It was caught by checking the archive before writing, which turned up the same certificate already transcribed correctly — and had it not been checked, this archive would have gained a daughter, a father and a birth year that do not exist.

rows.src: Antenati — the Muina marriage allegati, 1806–07, read in a fresh session
rows.what: The ten-image file for Muina, the second village Carlo De Franceschi named
rows.got:
**No De Franceschi in it.** The file holds two marriages, and both belong to other Muina families:

· **Giovanni Battista Corva × Cattarina Fabris**, November 1806. The groom's Latin baptism of **16 October 1782** — *Joannes Bapta, son of Paolo son of the late Giacomo, formerly of Giovanni Corva of Muina, and Maria Maddalena his wife*. The bride's certificate gives **Cattarina, daughter of Giovanni q. Pietro Fabris of Muina, born 12 May 1780**, and her father's own signed consent is in the file.
· **Giovanni Battista Micoli × the daughter of Tomaso**, June 1807, with the groom's certificate: *son of Giovanni q. Pietro Micoli of Muina and Marta his wife, born December 1777*.

**Corva, Fabris and Micoli are all names this archive already knows from Muina** — Osvaldo Corva of Agrons and Teresa Corva of Muina are in the 1807 death index, and Micoli is on Ferigo's list of the families that walked the road of the Furlans. **They are the neighbours, not the family.**

Eight of the ten images were read; two are blank versos. **This is the negative the errand asked for**: the second village Carlo named has a surviving marriage file from the right decade and the surname is not in it.

rows.src: Hotel Kvarner Palace, Crikvenica — the former Hotel Therapia
rows.what: Whether anything survives from the years Hedviga Blažević is said to have sung there
rows.got:
**A full and generous answer, and the answer is that the paper is gone.** Martina Riedl of the Kvarner Palace replies that the hotel has been owned by the Austrian Holleis family since 2004, and that **almost nothing survives from the period asked about**: *«we do not have guest books, personnel records, seasonal or entertainment programmes, posters or similar documents from the immediate post-war years… we assume that a large part of the original documentation and historical material was unfortunately lost over the decades.»*

**They had already tried themselves.** *«When we took over the hotel approximately twelve years ago, we ourselves made considerable efforts to research the history of the property and the former Hotel Therapia… From the immediate post-war period that you are particularly interested in, we were unable to find practically anything.»* They do not know where, or whether, any of it was transferred.

**One lead came with it.** They suggest **Theodor de Canziani Jakšić**, whose family's historical collection is at **Villa Ružić, Rijeka**, as a man with exceptional knowledge of the region and contacts among its historians, archives, museums and private collectors.

**And a standing offer**, which is worth honouring: if this research turns up anything on the Therapia — documents, photographs, programmes — they would be glad of it for the hotel's own history.

So the family memory that **Hedviga sang at the Therapia and met Ivan Defranceski there** stands where it stood: as testimony, uncorroborated, and now with the hotel's own archive formally eliminated as a route to it.
rows.dest: Villa Ružić, Rijeka — the de Canziani Jakšić collection

rows.src: MyHeritage Y-DNA, powered by FamilyTreeDNA
rows.what: The paternal haplogroup of the direct male line — David's kit and his father's
rows.got:
**Both kits return L-M27, and it is not a European lineage.**

Among this test's own participants L-M27 runs at **6.5% in Sri Lanka, 4.2% in India, 3.9% in Pakistan**, then through the Gulf and Mesopotamia. **Italy returns five men out of 6,068 — 0.1%. Croatia does not appear in the table at all.**

Against that, the autosomal estimates for both men are **100% European**, with Ivan's strongest sub-cluster **«Croatia (Lika-Senj and Primorje-Gorski Kotar)»** — Senj and the coast under it, exactly where the paper trail puts the family. There is no South Asian and no Middle Eastern component in either man at any confidence setting.

Both readings can be true. **Autosomal ancestry halves every generation** and drops under the 1% reporting floor after about seven; **a Y chromosome does not halve at all.** One man far enough back leaves a haplogroup and no ethnicity — which is the exact pattern here.

**What this is not:** it is a haplogroup read off an autosomal chip, not a Y test; two kits in one account agreeing is not two platforms agreeing; and **nothing in it identifies a generation.** No break in the male line is claimed, named or dated here. The Time Tree, which would date the branch, is behind a Big Y-700.

Graded **disputed** — the observation is documented, the reading is not settled.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1808 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The loose documents behind the De Franceschi × Salante marriage at Muina
rows.got:
**Five of the file's seventy-eight pages are this family**, and they correct the archive and extend it.

**The correction:** the notary takes the marriage consent not from the groom's father but from *«Donna Maria nata Corva, vedova del fu Antonio de Franceschi»*. **Antonio was dead.** With his own written consent dated 25 October 1807, that brackets his death to the fourteen weeks before 28 January 1808.

**The extension:** the groom's full baptismal name was **Osvaldo Antonio**; his birth on **14 March 1788** is confirmed a second time, from the priest's own certified extract rather than the register's recitation of it; the baptisms sit in the **Pieve Matrice di Gorto, «a parte Luincis»**, certified by **D. Giovanni Battista Dazio** on 21 January 1808 and authenticated at Mione by **Valentino Lupieri**; the consents were drawn by the notary **Giacomo Micoli del fu Francesco** at Muina before **Angelo Micoli** and **Zuane Fabris**.

**And a caution about the name.** The notary writes the bride's surname **Galante** twice, in a clear G. The priest and the file's own docket write **Salante**. The archive keeps Salante and records Galante beside it.

The file was reached only after correcting a count: the register browser pages ten at a time, and this archive had answered from page one.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1809 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the thirty-nine pages of the 1809 marriage papers
rows.got:
**Bundle number one is this family, and it reaches a generation further back than the village had ever given.**

The priest of the Pieve di Gorto certifies at Luincis on 4 February 1809 that **«Orsola figlia legittima e naturale di Pietro quondam Matteo De Franceschi di Mione e di Maddalena sua moglie»** was born **11 April 1768**.

**«Pietro quondam Matteo».** The 1806 birth act had given Pietro de Franceschi of Mione as the deepest name in the village. This gives **Pietro's father, Matteo** — a man whose granddaughter was born in 1768, so born himself around 1700–1720, within living memory of the Zuane De Franceschi who left this valley for Istria in 1679.

Orsola is also the **earliest-born Mione De Franceschi in this archive with an exact date**, and she is dated from the baptismal book rather than the Napoleonic register.

The other document in the bundle is the baptismal extract of **Giovanni Pietro Antonio Cramaro**, born 28 April 1758 — almost certainly the groom, though the marriage act is in another volume and the pairing is graded *inferred*, not documented.

The remaining five bundles of 1809 are Zanan × Colledan (published at **Pola**), Cole × Morocutti, one at Saurìs, Brovedan × Luchin, and Rotar × Provenzai. No other De Franceschi.
ev: The allegati deliver what this page said they would

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1810 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the forty-five pages of the 1810 marriage papers
rows.got:
**A clean negative, and worth publishing as one.** Five marriages, read from their baptismal extracts and notarial consents: **Lorenzin × Urai**, **Larese × Zanier**, **Fachin × Stefani**, **Masin × Brovedan**, and the Colledan and Desanutti papers. Consents taken by the notary **Giacomo Micoli** at Muina, Luint and Mione.

The individuals named are Desanutti, Urai, Larese of Auronzo, Bassi, Micoli, Fachin, Brovedan, Colledan, Stefani, Zanier, Masin, Solaro and Fedele. **No De Franceschi anywhere in the file.**

The dockets for 1810 carry only a bundle number — no names — so this year had to be read from the documents themselves rather than the wrappers.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1811 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the seventy-four pages of the 1811 marriage papers
rows.got:
**No marriage of this family — and a priest of its name.**

A bride of 1811, Anna Maria Giorgi «de Nave» of Mione, had to produce her baptism. The parish priest copied it out of the register of the Pieve di Gorto and certified the copy at Luincis on 20 June 1811. The entry is of **20 February 1785**, and it says that she was baptised *«hodie de mea licentia a R. D. Franc.o Ant.o **Deffranceschi de Mione**»* — today, by my licence, by the Reverend Father **Francesco Antonio Deffranceschi of Mione**.

**This is the first cleric of the surname this archive has found in Carnia.** He is styled *«de Mione»* — of the village. The archive already holds **Mattia Defranceschi, parish priest of Gologorica in Istria**, from the visitation of **1788**: two priests of one name, three years apart, at the two ends of this family's road. **No link is claimed.** But the Istrian encyclopedia entry already on the Carnia page lists De Franceschi clergy who went on working *in Carnia* — Filippo at Previs, Gian Matteo at Moncalvo and canon of Pedena — and a De Franceschi priest at Mione in 1785 is what that list predicts.

The rest of the year is Gortan, Zorzi, Bassi, Micoli, Bilbiani, Vernier, Crosilla, Sortiza, Varnier, a Gaier of Forni Avoltri and a bride from Cesclans.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1812 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the fifty-four pages of the 1812 marriage papers
rows.got:
**No marriage — and a man standing at the font.**

A certified extract of a baptism of **10 January 1789**, copied out at Luincis on 28 June 1812, records that the child was *«ex sacro fonte suscepta … a **D. Osvaldo DeFranceschi de Nave Mionensis**»* — lifted from the font by **Don Osvaldo DeFranceschi of Nave, of Mione**.

This is **probably the elder Osvaldo** whom the 1806 birth act showed only as a dead father («Osvaldo de Franceschi, son of the late Osvaldo»). A godfather in 1789 is an adult; an adult in 1789 dead by 1806 fits. *Inferred, not documented.*

**«De Nave» is new to this archive.** Nave is a hamlet, and these same files give **Giorgi «de Nave»** in 1785 and **Corva «de Nave»** in 1785 and 1801 — the Corva being the surname of Maria née Corva of Muina. A cluster of households in one named place.

The file also carries the death extracts of **Nicolò quondam Antonio Corva of Muina** (d. 11 August 1808) and **Jacoba his wife** (d. 6 February 1801).

The rest is Brovedan, Zoran, Spinotti, Fadri, Pellis, Stefani, Pedri, Martin, Brugia, Manetti, De Stephano, Capedari, Drossi and Cleva.
ev: 1812, and a hamlet with a name

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1813, 1814 and 1815
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the last three years of the Mione marriage papers
rows.got:
**All three are clean, and with them the whole Mione run of twelve volumes is finished.**

1813: Della Vedova de Caneva, Clevo, Crisilla, Erman, Micoli Toscano, Jacotti, Sortan, Gortan, Nigris, Plozzi de Prato, Machin. 1814: Goin de Muina, Odorico Micoli, Della Pietra, Marcuzzi, Urban, Rubin, and the **Paludi of Verona** resident at Mione. 1815: Novis of Agrons, Lupieri of Liariis, Brenci, Toriano de Nave, Disopra, Gusset, De Quas, Miudaris.

**Three things worth keeping from the negatives.** A witness signs himself **«pietro galante»** in his own hand at Mione in 1813, which shows Galante is a real surname here and that the 1808 notary was not simply slipping when he wrote the bride's name that way. A godfather of 1794 is **«Dominus Joannes Micoli-Toscano de Nave Mionensis»** — putting the palace family whose archive holds the 1679 Gorto contracts in **the same hamlet** as the De Franceschi of Nave. And in 1815 the parish priest swears that Valentino Disopra of his parish **died in Upper Istria in December 1797** — the Carnia-to-Istria road, certified, in a document that has nothing to do with this family.

By 1814 the acts are headed *«In Nome di Sua Maestà Francesco Primo, Imperator d'Austria»*. Napoleon has gone and the paperwork has not changed.
ev: 1812, and a hamlet with a name

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, Lenzone, Luint and Cludinico, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1806–1815
rows.what: The village files outside Mione — any De Franceschi, and anything about the Istrian road
rows.got:
**No De Franceschi in the files read so far** — Luint 1806 (De Corte × Lupieri), Lenzone 1806 (Fiorenzi × Vidale), Lenzone 1807, Cludinico 1807, Ovaro 1807, Ovaro 1814 (Delle Corte × Agarinis) and Ovaro 1815 (Fedele × Solari).

**But two of them are Istrian.** The Ovaro file of 1807 carries a letter from **the civil officer of Capodistria to the civil officer of Ovaro**, dated 28 May 1807, certifying banns cried in that city on 17 and 24 May, with a notarial act drawn at Capodistria and authenticated there. The Lenzone file of 1807 carries a certificate from **«Dipartimento d'Istria, Distretto di Capodistria, Cantone di Pirano, Comune di S. Lorenzo»** — **Sveti Lovreč**, inland Istria, twenty kilometres from Poreč — dated 16 July 1807.

Neither is this family. Both are **the route**, documented: two Carnian communes and two Istrian ones exchanging marriage paperwork as routine business in a single year.

Also corrected here: **«Nave»** is not a hamlet *of Mione*. The Lenzone file gives «Fiorenzi de Nave Luincis», so the clerks attach the name to two villages, and it is a small locality shared between them.
ev: Two Istrian marriages, filed in Carnia

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, Lenzone, Luint, Cludinico and Entrampo, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1806–1815, complete
rows.what: Every remaining village file of the Ovaro district — fourteen volumes, 296 images
rows.got:
**No De Franceschi in any of the fourteen.** With the twelve Mione volumes that closes the whole Ovaro run of **twenty-six files and 716 images**, and it bounds the question: between 1806 and 1815 this family married **once** in the entire district, and it married at **Muina**.

The families that do appear are the same two dozen names over and over — De Corte, Lupieri, Fiorenzi, Vidale, Del Fabro, Conan, Caneva, Berton, Cavallari, Missana, Mazzolini, Del Missier, Biliani, Schivas, Dell'Ost, Novis, Colledan, Calderani, Del Osol, Lenna, Cavarnis, Vidal, Cortidas, Delle Corte, Agarinis, Fedele, Solari, Micoli and Micoli-Toscano.

**Three of the fourteen are Istrian**, which is the real yield: Cittanova and Verteneglio in 1806, Capodistria in 1807, San Lorenzo near Pirano in 1807.

**A note on coverage, because it matters.** Every short certificate and every baptismal or death extract was read in full. The long notarial consents were read from their opening lines, which name the parties and the village. The largest files were not transcribed line by line — so a surname buried mid-act as a neighbour or a boundary could still be there. This is a negative for the parties to these marriages, not a guarantee about every word on every page.

rows.src: 23andMe — David's kit (paternal haplogroup, ancestry composition, timeline)
rows.what: Whether a second company confirms L-M27, and whether anything South Asian shows in the autosomes
rows.got:
**Both, and they agree.**

**«David, your paternal haplogroup is L-M27»** — 23andMe's own chip, own Y-tree, own algorithm, with the full path published (K-M9 → LT-P326 → L-M20 → L-M22 → L-M2481 → L-M27) and a change log recording that in April 2024 they *«excluded variants that were performing poorly on our v5 chip»* to make paternal assignments more accurate. *(One caution stands: if the MyHeritage kit is an upload of this same 23andMe file, the two are one reading. The father's kit is a separate sample regardless.)*

**And the thing MyHeritage could not see.** 23andMe puts David at **99.5% European** with **0.5% Trace Ancestry** — a category MyHeritage's model does not have: **Southern Indian & Sri Lankan 0.2%**, **Angolan & Congolese 0.3%**. Southern Indian and Sri Lankan is **exactly where L-M27 peaks** (6.5% Sri Lanka, 4.2% India by MyHeritage's own counts). MyHeritage's floor is about 1%; this is 0.2%; the signal was under the floor.

**0.2% is 1/512 — nine generations, about 1750–1780.** That is the window this archive reasoned to from the Y chromosome alone, published hours earlier, before the trace was known.

**Graded with care.** A 0.2% call sits at the edge of the method and could be noise; the halving arithmetic assumes one ancestor and average recombination. It is a **consistency between two independent measurements**, not a proof.

**Still open:** which parent the trace came from. 23andMe's Parental Inheritance is paywalled and was not bought — **Ivan's own 23andMe kit answers it free.**

Also: 23andMe names **Lika-Senj County, Croatia** first inside Greek & Balkan, agreeing with MyHeritage from a different reference panel. Maternal haplogroup **H**. Health reports were not read in and are not published.

rows.src: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA) — Jasna Vlahović, Odsjek za sređivanje i obradu arhivskog gradiva
rows.what: Whether the Svetvinčenat marriage registers survive for 1623–1762
rows.got:
**They survive, and most of them are already digitised.**

*«Državni arhiv u Pazinu ima knjigu vjenčanih 1581-1589, 1622-1623, a knjige vjenčanih 1588-1674 i 1674-1762 imamo u digitalnom obliku.»*

So Pazin holds the marriage book of **1581–1589 and 1622–1623** as a physical volume, and the marriage books of **1588–1674** and **1674–1762** **in digital form**. Between them they cover the whole of the period this archive asked about — and they bracket both of the dates that matter here: the **Svetvinčenat baptism of 1628** already found, and **1679**, the year a Zuane De Franceschi is argued to have left Carnia for Istria.

**This is the single most valuable door opened in months**, because it is a marriage series, and marriage acts name fathers.

**It is not free and it is not automatic.** Copies are issued only against a completed request form, which must carry the applicant's personal details, a delivery address and billing details — *«naziv uplatitelja, adresu i OIB»*. The archive answers within 30 days by law, 15 if the form is complete. **The form has not been submitted**: it asks for personal data, and that is David's to give.
rows.dest: DAPA — what to state in a request

rows.src: Knjižnica HAZU, Zagreb — Jelena Prekratić
rows.what: A scan of Danilo Klen, «Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine», Starine 58 (1980)
rows.got:
**Delivered, and they went further than asked.** The library replies that the article *«is fully available»* in their digital collection — **DiZbi 177355** — and, unprompted, **identified and scanned the second Klen article** David had a title for but no journal: *«Iz prošlosti Kostela — Petre Pilose i njegovih sela»*, **Buzetski zbornik, knj. 2 (1977), pp. 29–50**, sent as a PDF.

The 1425 urbar has now been read. **See the separate entry for what it says.**

rows.src: Danilo Klen, «Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine», Starine 58 (1980), pp. 85–124
rows.what: Whether the 1425 tax roll of the Petrapilosa fief reaches this family at Šterna or Sovinjak
rows.got:
**It does not, and the reason is worth recording so nobody chases it twice.**

The urbar is a household-by-household survey taken in 1421–25, after Venice seized Petra Pilosa, Buzet and Oprtalj from the Patriarch of Aquileia. The villages it covers are **Zrenj (Sdregna), Čepić, Šalež, Nugla, Grimalda, Crnica, Sočerga and Kodolje**, with Vrh and Draguć appearing at the edges.

**Neither Šterna nor Sovinjak is in it** — and those are the two places where this family is actually documented in Istria in the eighteenth century, with **Zuane Franceschi buried at Sovinjak in 1759** and **Sebastiano De Franceschi born and buried there on 6 August 1783**. The fief was a smaller and more northerly thing than its later district name suggests.

**The surname appears three times in the article and never in the roll.** All three are citations of **Carlo de Franceschi** and his son **Camillo De Franceschi**, the Istrian historians — and they are quoted disagreeing. Klen notes that Benussi relied on Carlo's 1852 identification of *«castrum Rivin»* with a castle on the upper Mirna, **without noticing that Carlo himself abandoned it** in his *Note storiche* of 1879, allowing that «Druine» might be old forms of **Draguć**. Camillo then asserted that «Ruvin» was **Rovinj**, *«whatever has been written to the contrary»* — contradicting his own father in print, fifty years on.

This archive holds **Carlo's letter to Kobler** and cites **Camillo's family archive at Trieste**. It had not seen the two of them argue.

rows.what: Copies of De Franceschi / Defranceschi entries in the Pićan baptisms and deaths, c. 1880–1915

**The form has not been submitted.** It carries personal data and that is not this archive's to enter on David's behalf.

rows.src: Trove — National Library of Australia (newspapers and government gazettes)
rows.what: The surname in Australia: the arrival, the Horsham household, and anything after
rows.got:
**An address, and a date, and the last sighting of Zdravko alive.**

*Commonwealth of Australia Gazette*, Periodic, **No. P2, Friday 16 February 1979, page 66**, under the heading **VICTORIA**:

> **Defranceski, Roza, 19 Anderson St, Horsham 3400, 21 7 78**
> **Defranceski, Zdravko, 19 Anderson St, Horsham 3400, 21 7 78**

Page 1 of the same issue says what the list is: *«a list of persons to whom the Minister for Immigration and Ethnic Affairs has granted a Certificate of Australian Citizenship, during the period July 1978 to September 1978 … published pursuant to section 42 (e) of the Australian Citizenship Act 1948 … The full name and address is given in respect of each person … together with the date on which the Certificate was granted.»*

So **Zdravko and Rosa became Australian citizens on 21 July 1978**, and the state told the world where they lived: **19 Anderson Street, Horsham 3400**.

**Three things follow.** This archive has never had **the family's Australian address**; it has it now, and it is the address to give the Public Record Office with the probate request. It is also the **last documented sighting of Zdravko alive** — seventeen months before the **22 December 1979** on his headstone, and it sits comfortably with the **1980** probate file while sitting very badly with the **1999** death that the family file and the MyHeritage tree both carry. And **«Defranceski, Roza»** puts Ruža née Hreljac under her married surname in a government record, at his address, eighteen months before he died.

**Also in Trove, and not this family.** **Giordano Defranceschi, 24, labourer**, described as a *«New Australian»*, drowned at the **Wigley waterhole near Alice Springs** on Sunday 24 January 1954, in front of a girl he had met the week before — *The Age*, 25 January 1954, p. 6, «Girl Saw Friend Drown». **DeFranceschi Bros**, a firm at **716 Chappie Lane, Broken Hill**, in the NSW Gazette of 17 June 1966 and a lease auction of 1972. A **Defranceski, M.** owed a few dollars in the NSW unclaimed-moneys list of 18 April 1975. Carol DeFranceschi in a Canberra Times notice of 1982, Mick Defranceschi in 1989, and a company, Defranceschi Brister Australia Pty Ltd, wound up between 2001 and 2004.

**Counts:** Defranceski **2**, Defranceschi **13**, «De Franceschi» **128**, Defranzeschi **0**.

**A method note worth keeping.** Trove's *newspapers* mostly stop at **1954** for copyright, and this family arrived after the war — so the newspapers were never going to hold them. The **government gazettes run to 2001 and beyond**, and that is where the whole yield came from. **Search the gazettes, not the papers, for anyone who arrived after 1950.**

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1809 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The marriage act behind the 1809 allegati — does it confirm the Orsola pairing?
rows.got:
**It confirms the pairing and corrects the name.**

Act N. 1, **Monday 13 February 1809**: **«Erman de Franceschi Gio: Pietro»**, 56, farmer, widower of **Cattarina née Carlevaris**, son of the late **Pietro Erman** and **Maddalena née de Franceschi**, born 28 April **1752** — marries **«Orsola de Franceschi»**, 40, *villica*, daughter of the late **Pietro de Franceschi** and **Maddalena née Fedeli**. Witnesses all of **Luint**: Valentino Lupieri 39, his brother Matteo 21, Giovanni Colledan 58 a tailor, Antonio Bressan 26 a servant. Registrar **Giacomo Micoli**.

He signs for both: *«per me e per Orsola de Franceschi mia moglie che non sa scrivere»*.

**The correction.** This archive had published the groom as «Cramaro», born 1758, on the strength of the priest's extract — *«figlio di Pietro cramaro»*. **Cramaro was the father's trade**, the Carnian pedlar, not a surname; and the birth year's last digit had been cropped out of the zoom and guessed.

**The name it should have read is Erman** — and *«Zuane d'Erman»* is one of the three men in the 1679 headmen's list who went from Mione into Istria with Zuane De Franceschi. The two families were still intermarrying in 1809, for at least the second time.

**Three more sightings in the same nine pages:** **Osvaldo de Franceschi, 22, carpenter**, witness 9 August — which settles the archive's own «nineteen in 1806 versus twenty-six in 1810» contradiction in favour of a birth about 1787. **Francesco de Franceschi, 25**, witness 21 September. And **Pasqua née de Franceschi**, named as the living mother of the bride **Maddalena Luchini, born 23 January 1789** — dating a household the archive had only as a name.
ev: The act itself, read at last

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1806 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The marriage act behind the 1806 allegato this archive read and corrected today
rows.got:
**Act N. 1, August 1806: «Ignazio di Zuato» × «Giacoma de Franceschi».**

He is a ***negoziante*** — a merchant — of **Chialina**, twenty-eight, born **13 December 1777**, son of the late Gio: Giacomo di Zuato and Cattarina née Cneva. She is the daughter of the late **Osvaldo de Franceschi** and **Cattarina née Gobbi** — **the mother's surname is new**.

**Osvaldo the elder now has a twelve-month death window.** He consented to this marriage **in writing on 7 September 1805**; by the wedding in **August 1806** he is *«il fu Osvaldo»*. Add the godfather sighting of January 1789 found in the 1812 allegati, and a man who had no dates at all this morning now has three fixed points.

**And Giacoma signed her own name** — *«Giacoma de Franceschi q.m Osualdo affermo m.p.»* Three years later Orsola de Franceschi, aged forty, could not, and her husband signed for her.

The registrar is **Giovanni Micoli-Toscano**, of the palace family whose archive holds the 1679 Gorto contracts.

*One thing is left unresolved rather than forced: the bride's stated age and the birth year read into the act differ by a year against the allegato's 1789. Both readings are recorded; neither is asserted.*

rows.src: 23andMe — DNA Relatives, and the shared profiles of both parents
rows.what: Which parent the 0.2% Southern Indian & Sri Lankan came from
rows.got:
**The mother's. Which means this archive's own headline of two hours earlier was wrong.**

Both parents share their 23andMe results with David, so the comparison panels answer it directly:

**Central & South Asian — David 0.2% · Ivan 0.0% · Cheryl 0.5%.**
**Sub-Saharan African — David 0.3% · Ivan 0.0% · Cheryl 0.8%.**

David has about half of his mother's in both, which is what inheritance requires, and his father contributes nothing because his father has nothing to contribute. **Neither trace has any connection to L-M27.**

**This makes the Y finding starker rather than safer.** Ivan is **99.9% European** — a cleaner European result than his son's — with 0.0% of anything else, and he carries **L-M27 on 23andMe as well as on MyHeritage**. The haplogroup now has **no autosomal corroboration at all**.

**Also found, and worth keeping:** Ivan's maternal haplogroup is **H14a**. His mother was Hedviga Blažević of Senj, so H14a is **the Blažević matriline** — the first haplogroup this project has for that side. Cheryl's is **H1**.

**And from the self-entered family backgrounds:** Ivan gives his **paternal grandmother's birthplace as Korčula** — which, if it means Ursula Kovačina, is a place this archive has never associated with her. It is family testimony typed into a form, not a record, and it is recorded as such. Cheryl's entries independently confirm what the memoir said: her **paternal grandmother from England**, her **paternal grandfather from Argentina**.

**DNA Relatives** runs to the 1,500 cap. The father's-side matches cluster on Croatian littoral surnames — Miškulin, Vrkljan, Katalinić, Prpić-forms, Serich. **No living match of the surname De Franceschi appears**, which is the one that would matter for the Y question. *Match names are third-party living people and are not published here.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1806 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The death of Osvaldo de Franceschi the elder, bracketed to September 1805 – August 1806
rows.got:
**Not there, and now we know why.**

The entire 1806 death register for the Comune di Mione contains **one act**: **Gio: Batta Antonio Giovanni Brenci**, aged three years and nine months, died **18 November** at half past eight, registered on **20 November 1806** by **Giovanni Micoli-Toscano**, who went to the house of the heirs of the late Zuanne Brenci to view the body.

**Civil death registration at Mione begins in November 1806.** Osvaldo consented to his daughter's marriage on 7 September 1805 and was dead by August 1806 — **before the series starts**. No amount of reading Antenati will produce his death.

**It can only be in the parish book of the Pieve di Gorto.** That promotes the Pieve registers from a good idea to the only route.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1808 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The marriage act of Osvaldo de Franceschi and Appolonia, 28 January 1808, read whole
rows.got:
**The register says GALANTE**, and this archive has said Salante for months.

Act N. 1, **28 January 1808**, before the civil officer of Mione with four farmers of **Muina** as witnesses — Angelo Micoli 57, Zuane Micoli, Giuseppe Clemani 40, Pietro Micoli:

> *«…sono comparsi per contrarre matrimonio **Osvaldo de Franceschi** di professione agricoltore, dell'età d'anni **venti**, domiciliato nel Villaggio di Muina … figlio di **Antonio de Franceschi**, e di **Maria nata Corva** pure agricoltori, ed **Appolonia Galante** villica di professione, dell'età d'anni **venticinque e mezzo**, figlia di **Antonio Galante** e di **Speranza nata Micoli**.»*

Galante twice, in the same looped G the notary used in his two consent acts. With **Pietro Galante's own signature** of 1813, that is **four hands for Galante against two for Salante** — the two being the parish priest's extract and the file docket.

**And one nuance that cuts the other way.** The register calls Osvaldo's parents *«pure agricoltori»* without ever saying **fu** — it does not record that Antonio was dead. The allegati do, unambiguously. **On this point the loose papers are the better source and the register is the worse one**, which is the reverse of the 1809 case. Neither series outranks the other; both have to be read.

The rest of the year is Bulfon × Steffani of Cella, Gotardis × Feranda, and the other bundles already listed from the allegati.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the nominative name index
rows.what: Whether the Mione and Ovaro registers are name-indexed, which would make page-by-page reading unnecessary
rows.got:
**They are not, and this is why nobody has found these people before.**

The index returns **418 records** for the surname *de franceschi* across Italy. Its own locality facet lists **Roma (63), Brescia (59), Dosolo (45), San Ferdinando (26), Genova (21)** and thirty-nine more. **Ovaro, Mione, Tolmezzo, Comeglians and Rigolato appear nowhere in it** — not in the facet, not in the results.

**Paluzza does appear**, which shows Carnia is not excluded as a region; this particular commune simply has not been indexed.

So there is no shortcut. The twenty-seven Mione volumes have to be read image by image, which is exactly what this archive has been doing, and exactly why the four sightings of 14 September were not already known to anyone.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1810 and 1811
rows.what: Any De Franceschi marriage in the two years after Orsola's
rows.got:
**Clean.** 1810 runs Steffani × Micoli, Brenci × Steffani and three more; 1811 runs Steffani, Bulfon, Gortan and the rest. The witnesses are the same Lupieri, Micoli, Brovedan and Bressan of Luint and Muina.

**No De Franceschi in either year, in any role.** The family's marriages cluster in **1806, 1808 and 1809** and then stop, which is what redirected this archive to the **death** registers — where a stated age reaches back before the series begins.

*Scanned page by page rather than transcribed; the later pages of the 1811 volume are badly faded.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1808 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Antonio de Franceschi's death, and anyone else of the surname
rows.got:
**Not Antonio — but a household this archive did not have, and a fact about how this family married.**

**30 April 1808, five in the afternoon, Mione.** Valentino Lupieri views the body of **«Francesc'Antonio de Franceschi … nell'età d'anni cinque»** — a boy of five, so **born about 1803**, three years before any surviving register.

The witnesses declare him *«nato nello stesso Villaggio da **Antonio de Franceschi**, e da **Giovanna pure de Franceschi** giugali, di professione il primo **sartore**, la seconda economa di casa»*.

**«Pure de Franceschi» — also a de Franceschi.** Both parents carry the surname. This archive has been tracking daughters marrying *out*; here is a couple where both sides are the name, and the registrar wrote *pure* so nobody would think he had duplicated it.

**Antonio is a second tailor** of the surname at Mione — Francesco × Margherita Gortan is the first, and the tailor is the *cramar* trade this page argues walked into Istria.

The first witness is **Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi, «d'anni cinquantacinque in circa»** — the man who marries Orsola de Franceschi ten months later, here as the widower he then was.

**Antonio senior's own death is not in this volume**, and the 1807 deaths do not exist: there is no Morti register for 1807 at all. He died between 25 October 1807 and 28 January 1808, which falls in that gap. **Him too, only the parish book can hold.**

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1809, act N. 1
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1809 death register
rows.got:
**The single most useful sentence found in this series.**

14 January 1809, Mione. The registrar views the body of Maria della Vecchia, thirty, wife of Giuseppe Pol. The two men who came to identify her are declared as:

> **«Presenti alla ricognizione furono Francesco ed Osvaldo fratelli de Franceschi»** — *brothers*.

**Francesco**, twenty-four, **tailor**. **Osvaldo**, twenty-two, **carpenter**. Both of Mione, no relation to the dead woman — which is precisely why the register troubled to say how they were related **to each other**. Both sign in their own hands: *«Francesco de Franceschi»* and *«Osvaldo Ant.o de Franceschi»*.

**This merges two of the four Mione households.** The archive has carried «Francesco the tailor × Margherita Gortan» and «Osvaldo the carpenter × Cattarina Brencis» as separate rows in a table with nothing joining them. They are brothers.

**And it points at a third sibling and a father.** The 1806 birth act gives «Osvaldo de Franceschi, son of the late Osvaldo», about nineteen; the 1806 marriage act gives **Giacoma de Franceschi, «q.m Osualdo»**, daughter of the late Osvaldo and Cattarina née Gobbi. If those are the same Osvaldo, then **Francesco, Osvaldo Antonio and Giacoma are three children of the elder Osvaldo** — and the four households collapse toward one family with a dead father. *Inferred, not documented.*

**On the ages:** Osvaldo is now nineteen (Oct 1806), twenty-two (Jan 1809), twenty-two (Aug 1809) and twenty-six (1810). **Three against one** for a birth about 1786–87.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1810, 1811 and 1812
rows.what: The whole volume read, acts N. 1 to N. 13, looking for a Pietro De Franceschi
rows.got:
**No Pietro. But four De Franceschi deaths in one year, a man in minor orders, and a signature that undoes a distinction this archive has been making.**

**Act N. 1, 25 January** — *«de Franceschi **Anna Cecilia** morta questo giorno alle ore otto pomeridiane **in età di un Mese c.a**»*, witnesses **Bressan Antonio**, twenty-six, and **Lupieri Matteo**, twenty-two, both of Luint; born at Mione to **Francesco de Franceschi**, *sarto*, and **Margherita nata Gortan**. **She died on the 25th, not the 28th, and she was eleven days old, not a month** — the birth act in the Nati of the same year has her born Sunday 14 January. [Both figures were published wrong](/corrections/).

**Act N. 10** — *«de' Franceschi **Sebbastiano** morto il giorno di jeri … **di condizione iniziato al Chiericato**»*, born at Mione to **Antonio** and **Giovanna nata de' Franceschi**, *«agricoltori, domiciliati attualmente in Mione»*. **A De Franceschi in minor orders**, dead young enough that both parents are living — and his mother a De Franceschi by birth.

**Act N. 11** — *«de' Franceschi **Maddalena** … dalli **morti** de' Franceschi **Sebbastiano**, e **Lucia nata Brencis** jugali»*. A second Sebastiano, and a fourth woman of the Prences house.

**Act N. 12, 17 September** — *«**Marianna** di Franceschi … in età d'anni uno circa»*, witnesses **Giorgis Giovanni** and **Brencis Biaggio**, seventy.

**The signature is the finding.** On both acts N. 10 and N. 11 the clerk writes *«**de' Franceschi Erman Gio: Pietro**, d'anni cinquantanove, di professione agricoltore»* — and the man signs **«Erman De Franceschi Gio: Pietro»** in his own hand. This archive has carried him as *Pietro Ermanni*, of the **Erman** family named beside *«Zuane De Franceschi»* in the 1679 weavers' return. **The register does not keep the two names apart, and neither does he.** In Carnia a *soprannome* sits on a surname exactly so; the plainest reading is that Erman is a by-name on a De Franceschi house. Recorded as **inf** — one signature is not a pedigree.

*Also in the volume, not ours:* **Mario Catterina** of Entrampo, 2 March, seventy-five; **Casanova Catterina** of Luint, 11 May, forty-nine; **Brovedan Domenica** of Muina, 11 July, fifty. Countersigned *«Li 13 Ottobre 1810, Rigolato. Visitato, e registrato. G. Capellari Giudice di Pace»*.
ev: The birth, and the eleven days

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1813 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1813 death register — read act by act, then checked against the volume's own alphabetical table
rows.got:
**Seventeen deaths, and not one of them ours.**

The comune buried seventeen people in 1813 across Mione, Muina, Luint, Luincis, Ovasta, Agrons, Liariis and Entrampo. The surnames are **Bulfon, Della Pietra, Senni, Pol, Rossi, Raffael, Tolson, Steffani, Nino, Fortin, Duminj, Urban, Vernier** and one *«infante maschio non battezzato»* at Agrons.

No De Franceschi as the dead, as a parent, or as a witness.

**The volume taught the method that made 1815 cheap.** Its last leaf is a **«Tavola Alfabetica»** — surname, village, day, month, act number, folio, in a ruled table. Every Mione register from 1813 onward has one. Reading the table takes three screenfuls; reading the acts took seventeen.

One near miss worth recording: the witness at act 14 signs as **«Osvald'Antonio»**, which is our carpenter's name exactly. He is a **Tolson**.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1815, act N. 23 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1815 death register, via the volume's alphabetical table
rows.got:
**«De Franceschi Anna — Mione — 11 9bre — n. 23 — foglio 5.»** The second row of the table, and it opens a house.

**Saturday 11 November 1815.** Matteo Lupieri goes *«nel Villaggio di Mione in casa di de Franceschi **Paolo**»* and views *«il Cadavere di Anna de Franceschi … in età d'anni **quarantaquattro**»*, *«maritata col suddetto Paolo de Franceschi»*. The witnesses — Fabris Osvaldo di Giuseppe and Fabris Giuseppe, forty-four, tailor — declare that she *«è nata in quell'istesso Villaggio di Mione»*.

**Born about 1771, at Mione.** That is thirty-five years before the earliest surviving civil register here, and it is exactly what the death books were opened for.

**Paolo is a fifth Mione household** and a new name: he is in none of the 1806–1813 births, marriages or deaths already read.

**And she carries the surname herself.** Either she was born a de Franceschi — which the 1808 act's *«Giovanna pure de Franceschi»* shows is possible in this village — or the clerk entered a wife under her husband's name. He does not do that to the other women in this volume, but one volume is thin evidence about a clerk's habits, so this archive leaves both readings standing.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1814, acts N. 12 and N. 13 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1814 death register — swept leaf by leaf, the volume having no alphabetical table
rows.got:
**«Osvaldo de Franceschi d'anni 27 ventisette, Servitore» — twice, in his own hand, at Muina.**

**Act N. 12, 10 September 1814** and **act N. 13, Saturday 26 November 1814**, both drawn at the *Agenzia Comunale di Mione* for deaths in the frazione of **Muina**. The same two witnesses both times: **Osvaldo de Franceschi, 27, servant**, and **Fabris Giovanni, 41, also a servant**, *«non parenti, ma vicini del Defunto»*. Both acts are signed **«Osvaldo de Franceschi»** in a large upright hand that is plainly not the registrar's.

**The age is the prize.** Twenty-seven in late 1814 means born **1786–87** — which is what the October 1806 act says (about nineteen) and what both 1809 acts say (twenty-two). The 1810 act, alone, would put him at 1784. **Four against one**, and the window for finding his baptism in the Pieve di Gorto books narrows to two years.

**The identification is not settled.** In 1809 he is a *carpenter* «di Mione»; in 1814 a *servant* and a **neighbour at Muina**. Mione and Muina are 784 m apart, and the signatures look to me like one hand — but that is an opinion, not a finding, and the household tables have not been merged on it.

*The volume has no Tavola Alfabetica — 1813 and 1815 do. The negative for the rest of 1814 is a page-level sweep and is weaker than the 1813 one.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1812 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1812 death register — swept leaf by leaf, the volume having no alphabetical table
rows.got:
**One act, and it carries two men of the surname signing their own names.**

**Monday 18 August 1812, eight in the morning.** Matteo Lupieri views the body of **Ottaviani Valentino**, twenty-five, a tailor of Mione, dead the previous day. The two men who come to identify him are:

> *«Erman de' Franceschi **Gio: Pietro** d'anni cinquantanove, **Possidente**, e de' Franceschi **Paolo** d'anni **quarantadue**»*

**Paolo is the husband whose house Anna dies in three years later.** Forty-two in 1812 → born about **1770**; Anna was forty-four in November 1815 → born about **1771**.

**Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi is now a «Possidente»** — a landowner — where in 1808 and 1809 he was an *agricoltore*. Between those acts sits his marriage to Orsola de Franceschi. Born 28 April 1752, he should be sixty here, not fifty-nine; the year's slack is recorded, not smoothed.

**And he signs «Erman de' Franceschi Gio: Pietro».** Byname first, in his own hand, as he did in 1809. *Erman* at Mione is a **branch-name inside the surname**, not the separate family this archive has been treating it as — which re-reads the 1679 headmen's list and makes every «Erman» entry in the Mione indexes a candidate.

Paolo signs too, smaller and less practised: **«paolo de Franceschi»**, lower-case p.
ev: Two men sign the same page

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1813 and 1814, alphabetical tables (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi marriage in 1813 or 1814, read off each volume's own «Tavola Alfabetica»
rows.got:
**Nine marriages in two years, and none of them ours.**

The method that broke open the death registers works on the marriage registers too: **from 1813 each volume ends with a ruled table** giving surname and forename of both parties, the frazione, the date, the act number and the folio. Two pages answered what would otherwise have been twenty.

**1813 — five marriages** (ark an_ua667522, image 11): Del Fabro Gio: Giacomo × Maria de' Prato, Agrons, 26 Feb · **Erman** Mar.o × Maria Fran.ca de' Prato, Agrons, 29 Aug · Fabris Ant.o × Gortan Maddalena, Ovasta, 28 Sept · Gortan Ant.o × Rupil Maddalena, Luincis, 7 Oct · Corpo Micoli Daniele × Micoli Toscano Maria, Muina, 22 Sept.

**1814 — four marriages** (ark an_ua667523, image 9): one at Chialina 6 June · one at Muina 16 Aug · one at Entrampo 29 Sept · one × Lupieri Giovanna at Luint 21 Oct.

**One row to come back to.** The 1813 *Erman* marriage is at **Agrons**, not Mione — but this archive established today that at Mione **«Erman de' Franceschi» is one signed name**, so Erman rows can no longer be passed over as a neighbouring family without looking.

*Matrimoni 1812 (11 images) and 1815 (5 images) have no tables and are still to be swept.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Opened by mistake while hunting for the birth registers — and it is the richest Mione series found yet
rows.got:
**A son for Paolo, a maiden name for Anna, and nine volumes nobody had opened.**

**Sunday 4 June 1815, ten in the morning.** Matteo Lupieri reads the promise aloud and nails it to the town-hall door:

> *«…la promessa di Matrimonio tra **de' Franceschi Felice Santo**, di professione **Sartore**, nativo e domiciliato nella Frazione di **Mione**, … **figlio di de' Franceschi Paolo e di Anna nata Brunis** giugali, e di **de' Canova Lucia Santa**, figlia del fu Osvaldo Antonio e Lucia nata Pellia…, di condizione Possidente, nata e domiciliata nel Villaggio di **Liariis, agenzia d'Ovaro**.»*

**Felice Santo is new** — Paolo's son, and the **fourth tailor** of the surname at Mione.

**«Anna nata Brunis» settles a question this archive published as open the day before.** She married into the surname; the 1815 death act's *«Anna de Franceschi»* is her husband's name, not hers. Logged as a correction.

**And the series matters more than the act.** A Napoleonic banns notice names **both parties, their trades, their villages and all four parents**, with *«del fu»* marking the dead. Mione has one volume a year, **1806–1815, arks an_ua667544–667552**, fifty-odd images, entirely unread.

**The marriage itself is not in Mione's 1815 register.** The bride is of Liariis; under the code the act belongs to the bride's comune, so it should be in **Ovaro's** 1815 marriages — with allegati carrying a baptismal extract out of the Pieve di Gorto.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1812, act N. 4 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1812 banns — the second volume of the series opened
rows.got:
**The deepest De Franceschi couple this project holds from Carnia outside the 1679 list.**

**Sunday 9 August 1812** (published again **16 August**), at the outer door of the town hall of Mione: the promise of marriage of **Zanelli Giambattista**, *«d'anni trentadue compiti»* — thirty-two exactly, born about **1780** — a **tailor** of **Ovasta**, to **Roder Lucia**, twenty-one, of the same village.

The groom is *«figlio delli viventi **Zanelli Francesco** delli fu Pietro e Isola nata Valle, e di **Ottavia nata de' Franceschi**, figlia **delli fu Batta de' Franceschi, e Maria nata Brenis**, giugali»*.

**Three generations in one sentence.** Ottavia, born a de' Franceschi, bearing a son about 1780 — so born herself about **1750–60**. And her parents **Batta de' Franceschi × Maria née Brenis**, dead by 1812, therefore **born in the 1720s or 1730s**.

**They appear nowhere else.** Not in the Mione births, marriages, or the deaths 1806–1815, all now read. A clerk had to say whose daughter the groom's mother was, and that is the only reason this archive has them.

**Ottavia is also a married-out daughter recovered from the wrong end** — not from her own marriage act but from her son's banns. That is a method: where a daughter's marriage is missing, her children's banns will name her, with her maiden surname and her father's.

**And «Brenis» corroborates yesterday's correction.** Paolo's wife was read as *«Anna nata Brunis»*; here is the same surname a generation earlier. The family is already in these books as **Brenci** (the single act of the 1806 death register) and **Brencis** (Cattarina, wife of Osvaldo the carpenter; Agostino, witness in 1808).

*The marriage act itself should be in Mione's own Matrimoni 1812 — ark an_ua667521, eleven images, not yet read — because Ovasta is a frazione of this comune.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1811 and 1814 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1811 and 1814 banns — both volumes swept leaf by leaf
rows.got:
**Twenty pages, no De Franceschi in any role — not as a party, not as a parent.**

**1811** (ark an_ua667548, thirteen images) and **1814** (ark an_ua667551, seven images) were swept page by page at a magnification that shows a name of that length clearly. The surnames that do appear are **Rupil, Rugo, Gortani, Steffani, Bulfon, Fiorenzi, Zanelli, Colledan, Nino, Della Pietra, Vernier, Marcuzzi, Barazzutti, Sivilotti, Roder** and **Zorzi**.

Recorded because a negative in this series is worth more than a negative elsewhere: **a banns notice names four parents**, so a year with no De Franceschi in the banns is a year in which no child of this family married *and* no De Franceschi daughter's child married either.

*Still to sweep: the banns for 1806, 1808, 1809, 1810 and 1813 — fifty-five images.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1808 and 1809 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The banns behind the two marriages this archive already holds — and what they add
rows.got:
**Two notices, both of them ours, and one of them settles an argument from yesterday.**

**1808, act N. 1 — Sunday 17 January, ten in the morning** (ark an_ua667545, image 3): *«la promessa di matrimonio di **Osvaldo de Franceschi, d'anni venti**, domiciliato nel villaggio di **Muina**, di professione agricoltore, **figlio di Antonio de Franceschi** … **e di Maria nata Corva**, economa di casa, domiciliati in Muina, con **Appolonia Galante** dell'età d'anni **venticinque e mezzo** … figlia di **Antonio Galante e di Speranza Micoli**»* — and the *Avviso* adds *«il matrimonio sarà celebrato li vent'otto Gennajo corrente nel Villaggio di Muina»*.

**«Galante» twice more, in a clear looped G.** The count against *Salante* goes from four hands to **six**.

**And the age settles which Osvaldo stood at Muina in 1814.** Born 14 March 1788, he is nineteen years ten months here and called **twenty**; twenty-six and a half in September 1814 and called **twenty-seven**. Same rounding, six years apart. Logged as a correction, together with the withdrawal of yesterday's signature comparison.

**1809, act N. 1 — Sunday 29 January, nine in the morning**, published *«sulla piazza comunale»* (ark an_ua667546, image 3): *«**Erman de' Franceschi Gio: Pietro**, d'anni cinquantasei, agricoltore … figlio delli defunti **Erman Pietro e Maddalena nata de' Franceschi** jugali, **furono villici di professione, già domiciliati nello stesso villaggio**, con **Orsola de' Franceschi** dell'età d'anni quaranta, villica … figlia delli estinti **Pietro de Franceschi e Maddalena nata Fedeli** jugali»*.

Every name matches the marriage act of **13 February 1809** — so the banns ran **fifteen days** ahead of the wedding. What is new is small and human: the groom's dead parents are described as **villici**, peasants, who had lived in that same village.

*1813 swept: five marriages, no De Franceschi, matching the alphabetical table.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1806, 1810 and 1813 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The last three unswept banns volumes — completing the series 1806–1815
rows.got:
**Thirty-one more images, no De Franceschi — and with that the series is finished.**

**1806** (an_ua667544, 3 images) opens thin: a title leaf, a blank, and one notice. **1810** (an_ua667547, 13 images): Steffani, Lungo, Nassivera, Micoli, Fabris, Screm, Gortani, Trifoni, Colledan. **1813** (an_ua667550, 15 images): nothing, and the marriage volume's own alphabetical table agrees — five marriages that year, none of them ours.

**The whole run now stands read: nine volumes, ninety-one images, 1806 to 1815, four De Franceschi notices.** 1808 (Osvaldo × Appolonia Galante), 1809 (Erman de' Franceschi × Orsola), 1812 (Ottavia and her parents), 1815 (Felice Santo and his).

*The five negative volumes were swept page by page rather than transcribed. The 1813 one is confirmed independently by the alphabetical table; the other four rest on the sweep alone, and a name buried mid-sentence as a grandparent could have escaped it.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1812 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The Zanelli × Roder marriage act, which should name Batta de' Franceschi and Maria Brenis a second time
rows.got:
**Six marriages, the register closed on 31 December 1812, and the Zanelli–Roder promise is not among them.**

Eleven images. **Act N. 5**, Thursday 17 September: *Steffani*, a shoemaker of Luincis, thirty, with *Osvalda Corva* of Muina. **Act N. 6**, Monday 28 December: *Steffani Lorenzo*, twenty-nine, villico of Ovasta. **Act N. 4**, 22 July. Acts **1–3** read at page level only — Bressan, Poli, Nino, Vidoni, Fabris, Roder, Gortan, Della Pietra, Micoli.

Then: *«Li 31 trent'uno del mese di Decembre anno mille ottocento dodeci — Il sottoscritto Ufficiale dello Stato Civile della Comune di Mione dichiara chiuso il presente Registro.»*

**Nor is the couple in the 1813 or 1814 alphabetical tables.**

**This matters because of what the series is called.** The 1806 title leaf reads *«Registro per l'esposizione delle pubblicazioni matrimoniali, e per le **opposizioni**»* — publications **and oppositions**. A banns notice invites the world to object. Most are followed by a wedding; some are not.

**It does not touch the Ottavia finding**, which rests on the notices themselves: she and her parents are named there by a public official whose job was to get the filiation right.

*Three of the six acts are still untranscribed, and the 1814 table's left column is partly lost in the binding shadow. Probably not married at Mione in 1812–14; not certainly.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1808, act N. 16 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The birth registers, finally located — and the first volume opened
rows.got:
**A sister nobody had, and a child nobody had, in four lines.**

**Sunday 10 July 1808.** *«Si è presentata al sottoscritto Ufficiale dello Stato Civile **de' Franceschi Margherita**, dell'età **d'anni ventidue**, domiciliata nel villaggio di Mione, villica di professione, portando seco un Infante di sesso femmineo nato il giorno suddetto alle ore otto di mattina … a cui fu imposto il nome di **Cattarina**. La suddetta Margherita ha pure dichiarato, che la neonata è figlia di **suo fratello Osvaldo de' Franceschi** di professione **Fallegname**, e di **Cattarina nata Prencis** di lui consorte.»*

**Margherita is a fourth sibling and the first one that needs no argument.** Francesco and Osvaldo are called brothers outright in 1809; Giacoma was added to them by inference. Margherita stands in front of the registrar and says whose sister she is. Twenty-two in 1808 → born about **1786**, between Francesco and Osvaldo.

**Cattarina, born 10 July 1808 at eight in the morning**, is a new child — the carpenter's elder daughter, registered the same day she was born.

**Witnesses: Micoli-Toscano Gio: Batta**, twenty-one, of Mione, and Lupieri Valentino, thirty, of Luint. **She could not write** and made her mark.

**And the birth series is located at last: arks an_ua667570–667573, being 1806, 1808, 1809 and 1810 — and nothing after.** The ark space above is empty, checked twice, while marriages, allegati, banns and deaths all run to 1815. **Only the births stop, and they stop in 1810.**

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1808, act N. 22 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The second De Franceschi entry in the 1808 birth register — and a check on my own method
rows.got:
**Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi carries a newborn into the town hall, and signs for it.**

**Sunday 21 August 1808.** *«Si è presentato … **Erman de' Franceschi G. Pietro, d'anni cinquanta otto**, domiciliato in Mione, di professione agricoltore, portando seco un infante di sesso mascolino, nato il giorno di ieri venti … a cui fu imposto il nome di **Gio: Batta Benedetto**. … esser il neonato figlio di **Pietro Ermanni, e di Orsola nata Crosilla** jugali.»* Witnesses **Lupieri Gio: Batta, thirty-two, «medico di professione»**, and Lupieri Valentino, thirty, both of Luint.

**A new household** — Pietro Ermanni × Orsola née Crosilla of Mione — and **a new child**, born 20 August 1808 at three in the afternoon. The relationship to the notificante is *not stated*; a man of fifty-six carrying a newborn is most naturally the grandfather, and Gio: Pietro's own father was a Pietro Erman, so the child is probably his son's. **Inferred, and labelled so.**

**And it marks down one of my own arguments.** Against his documented birth of 28 April 1752, Gio: Pietro is recorded as **55** (April 1808), **58** (August 1808), **56** (February 1809) and **59** (August 1812) — when he was 56, 56, 56 and 60. **Four months after being called fifty-five he is called fifty-eight.** Yesterday I leaned on age-consistency to identify the Muina Osvaldo and called it the convincing part; on this evidence register ages scatter ±2 and that leg is worth less than I claimed. The identification stands on village and trade.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1809, act N. 4 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The 1809 birth register re-read for notificanti and witnesses, not only parents
rows.got:
**A household nobody had, headed by a man with the deepest name in the file.**

**Thursday 2 March 1809.** *«Si è presentato … **Maria figlia di Matteo de Franceschi, d'anni dieci otto circa**, domiciliata nel Villaggio di Mione, villica di condizione, portando seco un Infante di sesso femminile nato il giorno d'oggi alle ore due antimeridiane … alla quale furono imposti i nomi di **Giovanna-Maddalena**. … essere la neonata figlia di **Matteo de Franceschi di professione Calzolajo, e di Anna nata Fasiol** sua moglie.»* Witnesses **Valentino Lupieri**, thirty-one, possidente, and **Gio: Battista Roter**, twenty-four, **also a calzolajo**, both of Luint.

**Two Matteos, not one.** Orsola's baptismal extract calls her father *«Pietro quondam Matteo»* — an elder Matteo dead before 1809, born about the 1710s. This one is alive, a shoemaker, with a daughter of eighteen. **The name is being reused a generation and a half later**, and this archive is not welding them.

**A fifth trade** for the surname at Mione: tailor, carpenter, farmer, landowner, and now *calzolajo*.

**And the clerk's own word for the daughter:** *«Notificante de Deffranceschi Maria **illetterata** fa il segno di croce»* — not the ordinary *«per non saper scrivere»*. Quoted rather than softened.

**The birth count was understated.** This archive said the 1806–1810 birth index *«opens on three De Franceschi entries»*; those were the first three lines. With Cattarina (1808) and Giovanna-Maddalena (1809) the true figure is **at least five** — and the birth index itself is still not located: the three-page tables at an_ua667540 and an_ua667566 are the **marriage** and **death** indexes.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1809, act N. 15 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi as a witness — and what his title says about the year of his second marriage
rows.got:
**«Ambi possidenti» — and it dates a change of station to within five months.**

**Sunday 9 July 1809.** Maria Ortis, thirty-four, *illetterata*, of Muina, brings in a girl born the previous day at one in the morning, **Lucia Lauretana**, daughter of Filippo Ortis and Margherita née Sottardi. The witnesses are *«**Erman de Franceschi Gio: Pietro** d'anni **cinquantaquattro circa** e **Gio: Pietro Giorgi** d'anni cinquantotto, **ambi possidenti**, domiciliati nel villaggio di Mione»*.

**He is already a landowner in July 1809.** The marriage act of **13 February 1809** still calls him *agricoltore*; so does every act before it. **Five months, and the word changes** — which is a much tighter bracket than the 1812 death act gave, and it sits squarely after his marriage to Orsola de Franceschi.

**And his age goes the wrong way again.** Born 28 April 1752, he was **fifty-seven** that day and the register says **fifty-four circa**. The run is now 55, 58, 56, **54**, 59 for a man who was 56, 56, 56, 57, 60 — a spread of five years. Any argument of mine that leans on register ages should be discounted accordingly, and the Muina Osvaldo identification has been re-graded to rest on village and trade.
ev: The Erman man, a class up

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1810, acts N. 1 and N. 21 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The last surviving birth register, read for notificanti and witnesses as well as parents
rows.got:
**Two acts, and the second of them proves my own method wrong.**

**Act N. 1, Sunday 14 January 1810.** *«**Francesco de' Franceschi, d'anni ventisei circa, di professione Sarto**, portando seco un infante di sesso feminile nato il giorno d'oggi **alle ore tre antimeridiane** … **Anna Cecilia**»* — his daughter by **Margherita nata Gortan**. Witnesses Antonio Bressan, twenty-six, *domestico*, and Matteo Lupieri, *possidente*, of Luint. He signs. **The child is dead on 25 January, eleven days old** — the death act guesses *«un mese circa»*.

**Act N. 21, Thursday 15 October 1810.** *«**de Franceschi Osvaldo, d'anni ventisei**, di professione **fa legname** … nato il giorno d'oggi **alle ore dieci antimeridiane** … **Gio: Batta**»*, his son by **Cattarina nata Crencis**, *«fa legname il primo, agricoltrice la seconda»*. Witnesses **Roter Gio: Batta, twenty-four, calzolajo** and **Brovedan Pietro, twenty-seven, sarto**, both of **Luint**.

**The signature is the finding.** In January 1809 Osvaldo signed *«Osvaldo Ant.o De Franceschi»* — upright, capitalised, practised. Here, twenty-one months later, he signs *«**de franceski osualdo**»* — lower-case, surname first, *Franceschi* as *franceski*, his own forename as *osualdo*. **One man, two hands so different that in separate parishes I would have called them two people.** Three days ago I compared two signatures and leaned on the likeness; I withdrew that yesterday on other grounds. This is the demonstration that the withdrawal was right, and it comes from the man himself.

**And the wife's surname will not hold still**: **Brenci** (1806 Morti), **Prencis** (1808 Nati, a clear P), **Crencis** (this act), **Brenis** (1812 banns), **Brunis** (1815 banns). This archive has tried three times to settle it and now records all the forms with their acts and prefers none.

**The 1810 «twenty-six» outlier is real** — read off the act, reported by the father in person. Ages here are worth about three years either way.

*With Gio: Batta the civil births stop. Anything born to these households 1811–1815 is in the Pieve di Gorto or nowhere.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, «Matrimoni» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Felice Santo de Franceschi's marriage act, predicted to be at Ovaro because the bride was of Liariis
rows.got:
**It was where the Code said it would be, and it carries a word this archive has never had.**

**«Registro Matrimonj, Anno 1815, Comune di Ovaro»** — ark an_ua679991, five leaves. **Thursday 15 June 1815, five in the afternoon.** Banns on two Sundays, 28 May and 4 June; the second is the Mione notice already published here.

> *«…sono comparsi per contrarre matrimonio **Felice Santo de Franceschi, di professione tessitore, d'anni ventidue compiti**, nato, e domiciliato in **Mione** … **figlio di Paolo de Franceschi di professione falegname** …, e di **Anna nata Brencis** di condizione villica … e **Lucia Santa de Canova d'anni ventitré**…»*

**A weaver.** The 1679 headmen's return that opens this archive is a return of **weavers** — *«compaiono soltanto i tessitori recatisi nella contea di Pisino»* — and it names *«Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo»* of Mione. This archive has held tailors, a carpenter, farmers, a landowner and a shoemaker of the surname; **it has never held a weaver.** Now it does, in the same village, 136 years later. It proves no descent and is not offered as one.

**But the Mione banns of 4 June call the same man «Sartore».** Two clerks, eleven days, two cloth trades. That weakens the weaver finding *and* the tailor argument this page has leaned on; what survives is that the family worked cloth.

**And Anna's surname is written «Brencis» here** — the form already held for Cattarina, the carpenter's wife. After six spellings across five acts I had written that the two women were «two clusters that may join»; a second comune joins them.

**Witnesses**, all of Liariis, all with their fathers named: Giovanni del fu Giacomo Crisilla (69, possidente) · Daniele del fu Osvaldo de Canova (49, possidente) · Giacomo del fu Nicolò Crisilla (69, falegname) · Giovanni di Nicolò Sabina (27). **He signed; the bride «dichiara essere illetterata».**

*One oddity left open: Daniele «del fu Osvaldo» de Canova stands at the wedding of a bride «figlia del fu Osvaldo Antonio» de Canova, and the act calls all four witnesses «non parenti, né affini». Either two dead Osvaldos at Liariis, or the formula is boilerplate. The Ovaro 1815 allegati would say.*
ev: The banns that sent me there

rows.src: Matricula Online (data.matricula-online.eu) — the whole portal
rows.what: Whether Senj and Karlobag, and any Croatian parish at all, are on Matricula — the plan said they were
rows.got:
**Croatia is not on Matricula. Not Senj, not Karlobag, not one parish.**

The portal's own fonds index lists exactly twelve countries — **Germany, Austria, Poland, Serbia, Luxembourg, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland** and three private collections. There is no Croatian section. Its place search returns **nothing** for *Senj*, *Karlobag*, *Rijeka* or *Fiume*.

**This archive's own plan said otherwise.** Matricula was written down as a fifth provider *«(Senj, Karlobag)«* and scheduled for building into the research map. That was an assumption never checked, and it was wrong. It is struck from the plan rather than quietly dropped.

**One thing there is worth keeping**: searching *Trieste* returns two Austrian Protestant congregations — **Triest AB** and **Triest HB** — under the Evangelical section. Not Croatian, not Catholic, and no De Franceschi is known in either; but Trieste Evangelical registers are a shelf this archive has never looked at, and the family was in the Littoral.
rows.dest: Matricula Online — fonds index and place search
ev: The research map, which now has four providers and not five
