rows.got:
**Still does not resolve.** Neither `https://arhinet.arhiv.hr/` nor the plain-HTTP form answers at all — not a 403, not a redirect, no connection. `ara.arhiv.hr` is the same.

This is the second time this archive has tried ARHiNET and the second time it has recorded nothing. **Pazin's own list stays the only Croatian archive catalogue in the research map**, and it is the only source in it that admits which volumes are not digitised anywhere.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Udine inventory for Mione and Ovaro, catalogued rather than read
rows.what: Every civil-register volume for the two comuni, turned into an addressable list
rows.got:
**Fifty-nine volumes, each one openable, none of them indexed by name.**

Mione's Napoleonic and Austrian civil registration runs in seven series — **Matrimoni** (9 volumes), **Matrimoni allegati** (13), **Matrimoni indici** (3), **Pubblicazioni** (9), **Morti** (9), **Morti indici** (3) and **Nati** (4). Ovaro adds a **Matrimoni** run of nine.

**The shape of that list is itself the finding.** Deaths and marriages run nine volumes; births run four. The civil births stop at 1810 while everything else carries on to 1815 — and 1807 is absent from every series. Anyone born into these households between 1811 and 1815 is in the **Pieve di Gorto** or nowhere.

**Years are given only where an act fixes them.** Four of the Nati are dated exactly, and two Ovaro Matrimoni are; the rest are numbered within their series and given the series span, because that is what the inventory supports.
rows.dest: Antenati, Archivio di Stato di Udine
ev: All fifty-nine, every one a link

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Mione inventory, walked ark by ark (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Forty-six catalogue pages fetched one at a time, to fix which comune, series and year each ark actually is
rows.got:
**The inference held, and the assumption behind it did not.**

Mione's marriages, allegati, indices and banns came back exactly as this archive had predicted from the ranges: **Matrimoni 1806, 1808–1815 (9) · Pubblicazioni, the same nine years · Matrimoni allegati, 13 across those years with two apiece for 1808–1811 · Matrimoni indici, three only — 1806–1810, 1811, 1812, and then nothing.** Every series missing 1807.

**But the very first ark fetched was not Mione.** `an_ua667510` is **Mieli, in the Comune di Comeglians** — Morti 1807 — and 667512 and 667513 are Mieli's Nati for 1806 and 1807. The portal does not number one comune per block, and an Ovaro range this archive had claimed on that assumption is withdrawn.

**Antenati stops answering after about forty-six pages.** Every request after that returns **HTTP 400**, including arks already fetched successfully — a rate limit wearing an error code, not a bad address.

*The catalogue now records how each volume's identity is known* — walked, read, or unconfirmed — and five arks inside Mione's range are left unconfirmed rather than given a year they might not have.
ev: The catalogue, every ark a link

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Ovaro inventory, walked ark by ark (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Whether Ovaro's civil registers have the 1807 that Mione is missing
rows.got:
**They do. Ovaro's marriages run 1806 to 1815 without a single gap** — ark an_ua679982 through an_ua679991, ten volumes, and **1807 is an_ua679983**.

**Only the marriages are digitised at Ovaro**: no births, no deaths, no banns. The **allegati** run eight volumes (an_ua679993–680000) and are missing 1806 and 1809; the **indices** are two, 1806–1810 and 1811.

**This is the correction that matters.** This archive had written, twice, that 1807 was absent from both comuni. It is absent from **Mione**. The next comune up the valley kept it — so 1807 is not a year the system failed, it is **one lost Mione volume**, and that is a question an archivist can answer.

**And it points at a cheaper route than a letter.** The Mione index says Osvaldo Defranceschi married Valentina Prencis on 6 August 1807. The Ovaro 1807 allegati exist and cost nothing to open.

*The 400 errors that stopped the first Antenati walk were never a rate limit.* The portal writes a «recently viewed» entry into the cookie for every register opened; at about 8 KB the Cookie header exceeds Apache's limit and the server answers *«Size of a request header field exceeds server limit»*. **Fetching with credentials omitted returns 200 immediately.** Forty-six pages of throttling that was not throttling.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua680000
rows.what: Felice Santo de Franceschi's proof of birth, demanded by the Code before the registrar would marry him
rows.got:
**It names his grandfather, and the archive did not have one.**

*«**Die 2 9mbris 1792.** Sanctus = Felix filius leg. ac naturalis **Pauli filii Petri De Franceschi mionensis**, et Annae, jugalium. Heri … est ad lucem, et hodie solemniter baptizatus fuit a me Joannem Baptistam Darium P.M. in Ecclesia Parochiali Plebana.»*

**Pietro De Franceschi of Mione** — Paolo's father. The extract is the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto's own baptismal register, copied out and certified by the priest who held it at **Luincis on 14 June 1815**, because the Napoleonic Code would not marry a man without proof of birth and Mione had no civil register before 1806. **A page of the book this archive has been trying to reach for two days has come to us inside a civil marriage file.**

**Godfather: «Domino Joanne quondam Floreani Micoli = Toscano»** — a Micoli Toscano, the family whose Mione palace holds the 1679 weavers' contracts. **Godmother: «Domina Magdalena filia quondam Joannis Prencis»**, both of Mione — the P-form of the surname, in a priest's Latin, in 1792.

**Also in the file:** Lucia Santa de Canova's own extract — born **12 May 1793 at the fourteenth hour**, daughter of Osvaldo Antonio De Caneva and Lucia Colinassio, baptised at S. Vigilio; and her consent act of 14 June 1815 before her widowed mother, which calls Paolo **«il vivente Paolo de Franceschi»** — alive — and **«possidente»**, where the marriage act eleven days later calls him a carpenter.

*Born 12 May 1793 she was twenty-two at the wedding, not the twenty-three the act gives.* Four images of the eleven belong to a different couple entirely, the Fedele–Solari wedding of Clavais.
ev: The six spellings, and the P-form

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1810, acts N. 1 to N. 5 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua667557
rows.what: The first of the nine Mione death registers to be read end to end, looking for a Pietro De Franceschi
rows.got:
**No Pietro. But the first act on the first page corrects this archive twice.**

*«Comune di Mione **li 25 Venticinque Gennajo** mille ottocento dieci … ove ha riconosciuto il cadavere di **De Franceschi Anna Cecilia** morta questo giorno alle ore otto pomeridiane **in età di un Mese c.a**»* — witnesses **Bressan Antonio**, twenty-six, *domestico*, and **Lupieri Matteo**, twenty-two, *possidente*, both of **Luint**, who declare her born at Mione to **Francesco de Franceschi** and **Margherita nata Gortan**, *«di professione sarto il primo, agricoltrice la seconda»*.

**She died on the 25th, not the 28th** — the date is written in figures and spelled out, agreeing. **And she was eleven days old, not a month**: the birth act four images away in the Nati of the same year has her born **Sunday 14 January 1810 at three in the morning**, presented by the same father before the same two witnesses.

**Giacomo Micoli wrote both acts and guessed the age of a child whose birth he had himself recorded.** This archive believed the guess, built a December 1809 birth on it, and then kept the wrong death date even after finding the real birth. [Logged](/corrections/).

*The rest of the volume, so far:* act N. 4 is **Mario Catterina** of Entrampo, 2 March 1810, aged seventy-five, daughter of Mario Giacomo and Catterina nata Roder. No De Franceschi in acts 2 to 5.
ev: The birth, and the eleven days
